store_data.about_the_game:
A new kind of puzzle


One block. One grid. Four arrow keys.

The block does not slide — it rolls. Every roll puts a different face on the floor, and a face that has touched the floor cannot be used again until all six have been used.

Which means four tiles is as far as one direction goes


The fifth roll would land on a spent face, so it is refused. Brute force is closed off from the very first move. Seeing where you need to go does not mean you can keep going there — you have to decide the order of the six faces first.

2,478 stages. All of them included.


One purchase opens all four campaigns. There is nothing to buy later.

999 — where you learn the rule, and the longest campaign. It starts with a single block and moves into two-stage boards: land the first block on the goal and it locks there, waking the second. That locked block is now a wall.

666 HELL — the same rule, a narrower road. Half of it is two-stage, and where you parked the first block, and in what pose, is the terrain of the second.

444 PANDEMONIUM — two blocks live at once. Roll one and the other stays put, in the way, and each turns its own face cycle.

369 TARTARUS — three. All three block each other and all three turn their own cycle. This is as far as the game goes.

The block is not always a cube


1×1×1, 2×1×1, 3×1×1, 3×2×1. A long block covers different tiles depending on whether it stands or lies, and the goal demands a specific pose. Arriving is not enough.

All 2,478 are confirmed solvable


Every stage was re-solved from scratch, with its stored answer thrown away, to confirm the goal can be reached. Where a stage has a move limit, the number it is built on is not an estimate — it is the exact minimum.

Undoing is not a penalty


Roll back the way you came and the move is simply undone. A move limit is a budget, not a failure device. Try things.

One input, one roll


Arrow keys, mouse swipe, touch, gamepad — all the same. Holding a direction does not roll you again. Every move should be a decision.

Seven languages


English / 简体中文 / 한국어 / 日本語 / Français / Deutsch / Español

store_data.about_the_game:
Trapped in a coma but conscious enough to experience every terrifying moment, you must survive days of sleep paralysis while awaiting a life-saving surgery. A relentless demon stalks the shadows of your hospital room, appearing whenever you close your eyes. You must find it and hold your attention on it long enough to drive it away, or it will invade your mind and drag you into a sleep from which you may never awaken. Balance your desperate need for rest against the horrors waiting in the darkness, survive each night, and stay alive until the day of your operation in this simple yet intensely frightening psychological horror experience.

Controls

LMB - Move/Sight

RMB + Hold - Remove demon

Rebelote: Belote & Coinche

brings the most-played card game in the French-speaking world straight to your screen — alone against an AI, or online with your friends.

A classic, two ways to play

Classic Belote and its variant, the Coinche. Call your suit, watch your opponents' play, and dare the coinche — or even the surcoinche!

An AI that actually plays

No more opponents playing at random. All three difficulty levels were tuned through repeated head-to-head testing, and Hard doesn't just play the first card it finds — it weighs several possible moves before choosing.

Play with your friends

Team up with a partner and take on another pair online, wherever they are. Belote with your buddies, no need to be sitting around the same table.

  • Solo mode with AI across 3 difficulty levels

  • Online multiplayer, teams of 2

  • Rules faithful to tradition

store_data.about_the_game:
The Decree is a 3-player cooperative horror game about hunting souls under a relentless clock.

The city is full of wandering souls. Everyone has a value. Everyone moves according to its own pattern.

Your job is simple:

Fulfill the Decree.

But finding them is only half the problem.

HUNT THE SOULS

Humans constantly move through the world, following patterns that can be learned and exploited.

Watch.

Track.

Predict.

Then make your move.

There are four levels of souls, from common souls worth little to extremely valuable Legendary souls.

But the greater the value...

the harder they are to capture.

CAPTURE UNDER PRESSURE

Capturing a soul isn't just pressing a button.

Every soul presents a different typing challenge.

Common

WASD sequence.

Uncommon

Two-word phrase.

Rare

Three-word phrase.

Legendary

A five-word sentence.

You have seconds to get it right.

Make a mistake and the soul escapes.

No health bar.

No damage.

Just your time.

SOMETHING ELSE IS HUNTING

Soul Drainers periodically emerge throughout the Order.

Ignore them and they cost you.

Fight them and keep moving.

Your Sisters already know how to fight.

The question is whether you can decide when to fight and when to hunt.

90 SECONDS

Every Order gives you 90 seconds.

Collect enough souls before the clock reaches zero.

Fail an Order and you get another chance.

Fail three in a row...

the run is over.

SIX ORDERS. THEN IT GETS WORSE.

The first six Orders steadily increase the pressure.

Complete all six and the game doesn't end.

It gets harder.

Then harder again.

And it keeps going.

There is no final round.

No forced return to the lobby.

No artificial stopping point.

How far can you go?

When you're ready, extract.

Or keep going until the Decree finally breaks you.

PLAY YOUR WAY

The Decree doesn't assign you a class.

One Sister might track valuable souls.

Another might handle the Drainers.

Another might take on the hardest captures.

Then switch.

Communicate.

Adapt.

Survive.

HOW FAR CAN YOU GO?

Complete Orders.

Build your run.

Push past the first six.

Extract when you're ready.

Then try to beat your record.

The Decree remembers how far you made it.

store_data.about_the_game:
Trace an Artifact Through Time and Place

Can you tell where an artifact came from, and when it was made, using only what you can see? Study its form, motifs, materials, and craftsmanship, then place your guess on the map and timeline. Relic Tracer is not about memorizing trivia. Every answer is a deduction built from the clues in front of you.

1,000+ Artifacts Across Chinese History

From prehistoric jade and ancient bronzes to ceramics, paintings, lacquerware, metalwork, and everyday objects, more than 1,000 artifacts form a playable journey through Chinese history. Every run brings a different mix of objects, periods, and clues to uncover.

4 Game Modes 

Trace Mode: Study an artifact and determine both its place and time.

Speed Challenge: You have just 10 seconds to identify the right era. Three jade lives are all you get.

Reverse Trace: Start with a time and place, then identify the correct artifact from four candidates.

Reveal Challenge: The artifact begins hidden in darkness. Use up to three reveals to uncover just enough detail to make your call.

Curated Challenges

China Through the Ages: Travel across the full sweep of Chinese history, with artifacts spanning different periods and categories.

Kilns Through the Ages: Follow centuries of ceramic tradition through changing forms, glazes, and techniques.

Objects of Power: Explore artifacts shaped by courts, ritual, authority, and the visual language of power.

The World Beyond: Enter the world of tombs and burial culture, and discover what objects reveal about changing ideas of death and the afterlife.

Build Your Archive

Every artifact you encounter adds to your growing Archive. Some also unlock Story Cards that reveal the people, beliefs, conflicts, trade, and traditions behind the objects. What begins as a guess gradually becomes a collection of stories pieced together from the past.

Daily Challenge

Take on a fresh combination of collections and game modes every day. Post your score to the leaderboard, compete with other players, and see how far your knowledge and instincts can take you.

store_data.about_the_game:
Santa is gone.

It’s Christmas Eve.

After hundreds of Christmases, thousands of chimneys, and way too many rooftop landings,
Santa burned out and took off for Hawaii.

All he left behind was the sleigh, a pile of tools, and one simple instruction:

“You guys do Christmas this year.”

Now a completely unprepared crew of gingerbread cookies has to take the sleigh, sneak into houses,
and somehow keep Christmas alive.

Wish Impossible is a 1–4 player online co-op physics adventure about tiny cookies taking on jobs
they are absolutely not qualified for.

Find the wish. Figure out what needs to be done. Make it happen.
Preferably without destroying the house.

Sneak In. Make a Mess. Fix It Somehow.

Grab, carry, throw, stack, freeze, cook, and break your way through each mission.

Work together to find what you need, move oversized objects, and improvise ridiculous solutions
with whatever you can find around the house.

A simple Christmas wish can turn into a complete disaster very quickly.
Especially when your friends are helping.

Tiny Cookies. Huge Problems.

You are small.
Very small.

Climb furniture, squeeze through narrow gaps, cross dangerous rooms, and use ridiculous tools to
reach places no gingerbread cookie was ever meant to reach.

To you, an ordinary house is a giant obstacle course.

Whatever You Do, Don’t Wake Them Up.

Noise draws attention.

Drop something heavy, smash a decoration, cause a kitchen disaster, or make one too many
questionable decisions and everyone in the house may start waking up.

Stay quiet when you can.
Deal with the chaos when you can’t.

Better With Friends. Probably.

Play solo or team up with up to three friends online.

Help each other reach high places, carry enormous objects, solve problems, and survive the mission.

Or become the reason everyone else fails.

Both are valid forms of teamwork.

Grant the Wish. Get Back to the Sleigh.

Find the wish.

Make it come true.

Then get back to the sleigh with as much of the house — and as many of your body parts — still intact as possible.

Santa’s in Hawaii.

Christmas is your problem now.

Good luck.

After hundreds of Christmases, thousands of chimneys, and way too many rooftop landings,
Santa burned out and took off for Hawaii.

All he left behind was the sleigh, a pile of tools, and one simple instruction:

“You guys do Christmas this year.”

Now a completely unprepared crew of gingerbread cookies has to take the sleigh, sneak into houses,
and somehow keep Christmas alive.

Wish Impossible is a 1–4 player online co-op physics adventure about tiny cookies taking on jobs
they are absolutely not qualified for.

Find the wish. Figure out what needs to be done. Make it happen.
Preferably without destroying the house.

Sneak In. Make a Mess. Fix It Somehow.

Grab, carry, throw, stack, freeze, cook, and break your way through each mission.

Work together to find what you need, move oversized objects, and improvise ridiculous solutions
with whatever you can find around the house.

A simple Christmas wish can turn into a complete disaster very quickly.
Especially when your friends are helping.

Tiny Cookies. Huge Problems.

You are small.
Very small.

Climb furniture, squeeze through narrow gaps, cross dangerous rooms, and use ridiculous tools to
reach places no gingerbread cookie was ever meant to reach.

To you, an ordinary house is a giant obstacle course.

Whatever You Do, Don’t Wake Them Up.

Noise draws attention.

Drop something heavy, smash a decoration, cause a kitchen disaster, or make one too many
questionable decisions and everyone in the house may start waking up.

Stay quiet when you can.
Deal with the chaos when you can’t.

Better With Friends. Probably.

Play solo or team up with up to three friends online.

Help each other reach high places, carry enormous objects, solve problems, and survive the mission.

Or become the reason everyone else fails.

Both are valid forms of teamwork.

Grant the Wish. Get Back to the Sleigh.

Find the wish.

Make it come true.

Then get back to the sleigh with as much of the house — and as many of your body parts — still intact as possible.

Santa’s in Hawaii.

Christmas is your problem now.

Good luck.

store_data.about_the_game:
A battle pet that lives on your desktop — and now has a home.

Glims don't live inside a window. They walk along your taskbar, climb the edges of your programs, sit down, take naps and talk to each other while you work. When you call them, the game happens on your screen — not in a fullscreen window on top of it.

THE HOUSE

A small, transparent isometric 3D house in the corner of your screen. Furnish each room by dragging pieces from a catalog of nearly two hundred, pick the floor and the wall color, and drag your glims in and out — they live in the house or on the desktop, never both. Buy new rooms with in-game gold: in the living room they rest; in the office, the workshop and the training area they work, earn gold and get tired. Each room has its own catalog.

INVASION: DEFEND YOUR DESKTOP

A jade lawn assembles over your desktop and the invaders come in from the right, lane by lane. You plant your glims to hold them: swords hold the line up close, bow and magic hit from across the field. Cards drop onto the lawn mid-match and fly into your hand with one click. Every stage they come faster and tougher — how far can you hold?

THE DUNGEON, TWENTY FLOORS

Build a squad of up to three and go down floor by floor. The fighting is automatic; enemies have special moves of their own, and every three floors a boss waits. After it, the only question that matters — walk away with the loot, or go one floor deeper? Whoever falls stays down, and anything not banked is lost.

THE TAVERN AND THE ARENA

At the tavern, a card game of combat: cards are strikes with a force and a style, hands are combos named after dojo moves, and trinkets bend the rules. In the arena, a squad duel with glimbucks on the line — the currency only the arena pays.

TEN GLIMS TO COLLECT

Each with a card, stats and a way of fighting of their own. Weapons are real 3D models fitted into the hand — or stowed on the back, for those who fight with claws and magic. Special weapons are numbered: every piece carries its own serial number. Swap them in the inventory and see the change on screen right away.

FREE, LIGHT AND OFFLINE

The game is free and runs without a connection. It's light, it stays on all day, and it never gets in the way of what you're doing. Purchases are optional and fixed: three packs with their contents listed — nothing random costs money. Chests, furniture and rooms are bought with gold earned by playing.

While you were away, a jealous wizard turned your library upside down, and scattered 1,560 items throughout your library: 1,312 numbered books and 248 potions to be precise!

  • See a placement preview before shelving a compatible item.

  • Pet, rename and customize your wizard cat.

store_data.about_the_game:
Command the battle. Then fight it yourself.

SPEARHEAD is a WW2 game set on the Eastern Front in 1944, combining a real-time strategy layer with direct tank

control in a single battle. Fight with historically organized German and Soviet forces.

Commander and Ace — two battlefields in one

Direct infantry, vehicles, and armor from above, coordinating artillery and air support. When the line starts

to break, climb into your ace tank and fight through the gunsight yourself. Both roles are the full game.

No HP bars

Tanks survive by armor, not health. Real armor thickness and impact angles decide penetration — shells

ricochet, crews die, tracks break, ammo racks cook off. A Tiger's front is genuinely hard. Its flank is

genuinely not.

Weapons as they were

Armor values, penetration, rate of fire, muzzle velocity — all based on historical data. An 88 fights like an

88.

Infantry lives by cover

Hug walls, dig trenches, garrison buildings. Suppressed squads keep their heads down. Kill the machine gunner

and the assistant picks up the gun.

Battles escalate in phases

Encounter → Deployment → Engagement → Decisive Engagement. Heavier equipment unlocks as the battle escalates,

and victory points settle the war.

Modes

Single-player vs AI · 1v1 Multiplayer · Spectating and replays

Sister title — SPEARHEAD TACTICS, a turn-based hex wargame with the same army and the same armour.

store_data.about_the_game:
Building it is only the beginning. The real question is: will it stand?

In Will It Stand?, you design structures with limited materials and budgets, protect critical objectives, and watch your creations face earthquakes, crushing loads, and violent impacts.

Every beam, joint, and support matters. A structure that looks solid may collapse because of one overlooked weakness. A bizarre-looking design might survive through clever engineering alone.

From blueprint to physical test

Plan your structure in the blueprint, choose your materials, and decide how everything connects. When you are ready, run the simulation and watch your design bend, break—or remain standing—under real physics.

Failure is part of the process. Find where the collapse began, understand how the forces travelled through the structure, then redesign and test it again. Every disaster teaches you how to build something better.

More material is not always the answer

Heavier, thicker, and more expensive does not necessarily mean safer.

Balance strength, weight, cost, and structural layout. An extra support may reinforce one section while placing more stress on another. Removing a single beam may save money—or eliminate the one connection holding everything together.

Reliable structures are built through good decisions, not brute force.

Take on different challenges

Put your engineering instincts to the test as you:

  • Survive earthquakes of increasing intensity

  • Support heavier and heavier loads

  • Protect fragile or critical objectives

  • Withstand impacts, falls, and sudden destruction

  • Complete missions with limited materials and budgets

There is rarely only one correct solution. Minimize the cost, use as few materials as possible, pursue an elegant design, or create something ridiculous that somehow survives.

Even failure can be spectacular

Watch structures buckle, joints snap, and materials scatter while your beaver engineer discovers whether your latest creation is a masterpiece—or a magnificent accident.

Build boldly. Watch closely. Improve relentlessly.

Then let physics answer the only question that matters:

Will It Stand?

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to Shinjuku, 199X – A Visual Novel of Power and Revenge

You are Miyazaki Sō, a man out of time. A citizen of the cyberpunk Neon Nation, you awaken in 1990s Tokyo and join the Shinjuku Precinct as a detective. When a kidnapping case forces you to take your reckless superior, Kurokawa Sakura, hostage—not with a gun, but with a secret that could destroy her career—you strike a deal that will change everything.

From that moment, you walk a razor's edge. Leverage Kurokawa's connections to solve cases, rise through the ranks, and pursue Hashiguchi Yoshio—the man who destroyed your family. But in the neon-lit underworld of Okubo, every favor comes with a price, and every ally has a hidden agenda.

What You Will Do: Read, Choose, Shape the Story

This is a narrative-first experience. Your primary tools are observation and conversation.

  • Branching Dialogues – Every conversation offers multiple responses. Choose to be persuasive, intimidating, or diplomatic. Your words carry weight—NPCs remember how you treat them.

  • Critical Decisions – At key moments, you will face irreversible choices. Trust the wrong person, and a case may go cold. Reveal too much, and your enemies gain leverage. These decisions lead to multiple distinct story branches.

store_data.about_the_game:
Hit the beat. Build the run.

Duckstep is a rhythm game with a roguelite bolted onto its spine. Gems fall down four lanes (six on the piano stages) and you catch them on the beat — but every clean hit feeds a build. Skills draft mid-run. Your character's power switches on at 25 combo and never switches off. By the time you're deep in a track, half the screen is fighting for you, and the only question is whether you can hold the streak long enough to see what's next.

Your combo is the engine

Everything in Duckstep keys off the number in the corner.

  • 25 combo — your stepper's signature power latches on and stays on for the rest of the run. It never drops off on a miss.
  • 100 / 200 / 300 — that power tiers up. Blaze's fire ring widens. Scholar gains another orbiting tome. Thundor's bolts come faster and reach further.
  • 400 combo — the game freezes and hands you three cards. Pick an Ultimate. It's permanent, it's run-defining, and it does not stack or evolve — it just changes what the run is.

Miss, and the ladder holds. Whiff repeatedly, and you'll find out how much of that screen was carrying you.

Twenty steppers, twenty answers

Every character plays the same charts and solves them differently. Duckstepper earns autonomous helper ducks that wander the field grabbing gems on their own. Blaze ignites and burns anything near a catch. Ribbit locks a tongue laser up-screen through five tiers. Blackhole periodically swallows every gem inside a growing radius. Snek weaves across the lanes trailing a body that grows and slices. Chubs just gets bigger and pierces straight through.

They're not skins. Picking a stepper picks a strategy.

Thirty skills, drafted live

Clean hits fill a meter; filling it stops the run and offers a draft. Twenty active skills and ten passives, eight active slots and four passive slots to fill. Stack three copies of a skill and it evolves into a stronger version of itself — Slow-Mo goes from calming the field to nearly stopping it, Second Wind goes from absorbing one miss to shielding three.

Flaming Potion lobs bottles that shatter and burn patches of gems out of the air. Slipstream auto-glides you to the next gem's lane after a Perfect. Gem Vault banks a share of every coin into your permanent wallet, whether the run ends well or not.

Stages, Endless runs, and one level with the assists ripped out

Twenty levels, each with its own song, its own hand-authored chart, and its own idea of what's hard.

  • Stages have a clear score. Hit it and the run ends in a win, not a death.
  • Endless tracks never cap. The speed keeps climbing toward impossible and your reward scales with how far you got.
  • Density stages never speed up at all — the notes just keep thickening into chords and jumps until the chart is a wall.
  • RAW turns off the passive catch, the skills, and the character powers. It's just you and the chart. Good luck.

store_data.about_the_game:
From One Box to a Finished Model

Cut parts from sprues, paint them in your favorite colors, apply decals, and snap everything together. Plamo kits is a 3D simulation game about enjoying the process of building plastic models at your desk.

No sanding. No waiting for paint to dry. Build straight from the box or customize every last detail—the choice is yours. Take your time and complete each kit your way.

Cut, Then Assemble

Position your side cutters at each gate and free the parts from their sprues one by one. Pick up parts from the cutting mat, check their orientation and connection points, then fit them together. Assemble them in any order you like.

Choose Your Colors and Finish

Paint directly onto each part with brushes and an airbrush. Color individual sections, adjust the position, rotation, and scale of decals, then add texture with weathering. Painting and decals are entirely optional, so a clean straight build is just as valid.

Pose It, Display It, Keep Tinkering

Move the joints of your finished models to pose them, then display them on the shelves in your room. Take photos from your favorite angles, or bring a model back to the workbench to disassemble and repaint it. Finishing a model is not the end—it is the beginning of a growing collection.

Kits From Worlds of Their Own

Each kit comes from an original fictional series, with its own story and design. Build while browsing box art and reference materials, then fill your room with finished models and posters as those worlds gradually take shape around you.

Key Features

  • A hands-on 3D building experience: cut parts from sprues with side cutters

  • Freeform painting with brushes and an airbrush

  • Decals with adjustable position, rotation, and scale

  • Weathering for adding texture and character

  • Assemble parts in any order, or enjoy an unpainted straight build

  • Pose finished models, display them on shelves, and take photos

  • Disassemble completed models to repaint them or readjust their decals

store_data.about_the_game:
Wizard Harder Or Get Laid Off is proudly made with zero AI. Besides a light smattering of purchased assets from the itch.io store, a majority of the art is created by local artists, and all voices in the game were recorded in the developer's home. This is a labor of love, and we hope you enjoy the game as much as we enjoyed creating it.

In Wizard Harder Or Get Laid Off, you and up to three friends play as powerful wizards who, after being evicted from their homes, travel to a new kingdom to find work. Here, you’ll explore the land and defend the kingdom from invading forces, all the while training to become the kingdom’s next Grand Wizard!

  • Pick up quests from the quest board, earning the gold required to complete your studies

  • Enhance your abilities at ten different buildings, and meet the lovely, colorful, and fully voice-acted characters who inhabit them

  • Learn new spells and use them in the auto-battler to fight off the incoming goblins wielding spell-enhanced wands and stop their quick-spell system from entering the borders

  • Befriend a familiar and train their abilities to aid you in battle - four unique familiars to choose from!

  • Buy beautifully designed and whimsical clothing to customize your character

  • Meet the king, introduce yourself, and give him gifts! Maybe that’ll make him like you more…

And, as in real life, don’t forget to eat!

store_data.about_the_game:
Nanamitsu Yushayama Has Arrived!

"Nanamitsu's Detour" is an RPG that can be played using only the mouse.
Defeat enemies, level up, defeat bosses,
then move on to new stages, defeat more enemies, level up, and defeat more bosses. It's a simple game.
Playtime is about 1–2 hours. Anyone can clear the game if they just keep clicking hard enough.

There are no shocking experiences, no touching story, and not a single cute anime girl to be found anywhere!
But I hope you can relax and enjoy the game.

Characters

Nanamitsu Yushayama

The protagonist of this game. She takes after her mother.
She has no particularly outstanding traits in battle, but
like any young person these days, she quickly becomes obsessed with highly addictive forms of entertainment (such as repeatedly swiping vertically on a smartphone).
Apparently, she's somewhat dissatisfied with her own name.

Yusha-ko Yushayama

Not the protagonist of this game. The mother of Nanamitsu Yuyama.
She was apparently a legendary hero once upon a time.

Ambient

Monsters that can be found here and there. They have lots of experience points, so they're a good deal.
Apparently, once you spot one, you're likely to encounter more of them in succession.

About Streaming

There are no restrictions on streaming or broadcasting gameplay of this game.
Feel free to stream it however you like. No individual contact is necessary.

store_data.about_the_game:
Emberwall is a top-down roguelite tower defense game focused on path-building, resource management, and powerful tower combinations. Enemies march south from the darkness toward your castle—but their route is yours to reshape.

Place tetromino-shaped wall pieces to redirect enemy waves, split their forces between equal paths, and create strong positions for your defenses. If you completely surround the castle, enemies will find the weakest route and tear through your walls—and any towers built upon them.

Your castle illuminates only a small area of an endlessly expanding, fog-covered map. Build Bonfires to push back the darkness, discover resource deposits, and force enemy spawn points farther north.

Wood and stone deposits block movement and construction. Place Sawmills and Mines on matching deposits to generate resources during enemy waves, then spend those materials on walls, defenses, and expansion.

Build Bow Towers, Cannons, Tesla Coils, Inferno Spires, Mortars, Flamethrowers, Sunbeam Lasers, and Repeating Crossbows. Each defense has its own attack pattern, strengths, weaknesses, and tower-specific upgrades.

Customize targeting priorities to focus on:

  • Enemies closest to the castle

  • Highest-health enemies

  • Lowest-health enemies

  • Enemies furthest from the castle

Enhance towers with Splash, Scorch, Hitch, Blitz, or Ice. Combine elements to unlock advanced effects such as Steam, Flash Freeze, Thermal Shock, Backdraft, Electrolysis, Whiteout, and Plasma Link.

Only one base element can be placed on each tower, making every upgrade choice and tower combination matter.

Choose from three upgrade cards after each wave. Improve damage, range, and attack speed, discover tower-specific abilities, strengthen connected walls and production lines, or accept dangerous challenges for greater rewards.

Rare, Epic, and Legendary cards provide increasingly powerful effects, while special upgrades can transform how an entire defense operates.

Later waves introduce faster Runners, armored enemies, powerful elites, and increasingly massive armies. Study the visible enemy routes, reshape the battlefield, and prepare your defenses before the next wave begins.

Gold earned throughout a run contributes to permanent progression. Upgrade your castle, improve resource production, unlock new weapons, and increase their starting power through the Keep and Armory.

Every run uses a different seed, creating a new map, resource layout, wall hand, and sequence of upgrade choices.
store_data.detailed_description:
Emberwall is a top-down roguelite tower defense game focused on path-building, resource management, and powerful tower combinations. Enemies march south from the darkness toward your castle—but their route is yours to reshape.

Place tetromino-shaped wall pieces to redirect enemy waves, split their forces between equal paths, and create strong positions for your defenses. If you completely surround the castle, enemies will find the weakest route and tear through your walls—and any towers built upon them.

Your castle illuminates only a small area of an endlessly expanding, fog-covered map. Build Bonfires to push back the darkness, discover resource deposits, and force enemy spawn points farther north.

Wood and stone deposits block movement and construction. Place Sawmills and Mines on matching deposits to generate resources during enemy waves, then spend those materials on walls, defenses, and expansion.

Build Bow Towers, Cannons, Tesla Coils, Inferno Spires, Mortars, Flamethrowers, Sunbeam Lasers, and Repeating Crossbows. Each defense has its own attack pattern, strengths, weaknesses, and tower-specific upgrades.

Customize targeting priorities to focus on:

  • Enemies closest to the castle

  • Highest-health enemies

  • Lowest-health enemies

  • Enemies furthest from the castle

Enhance towers with Splash, Scorch, Hitch, Blitz, or Ice. Combine elements to unlock advanced effects such as Steam, Flash Freeze, Thermal Shock, Backdraft, Electrolysis, Whiteout, and Plasma Link.

Every run uses a different seed, creating a new map, resource layout, wall hand, and sequence of upgrade choices.

store_data.about_the_game:
1,279 paintings by 64 artists are stacked on the floor of the museum. You have to hang them all back, each on its artist's wall. Your main tool is a book. For every artist it gives a few lines on the style and one signature painting — enough to start recognizing the other canvases. The rest is up to you: study the themes and details, group the paintings, and get every one of them to the right wall.

The paintings are real

You work with paintings by real artists — Rembrandt van Rijn, Vincent van Gogh, Edgar Degas and 61 more — taken from the collections of twelve museums.

Upgrades

Hanging paintings earns points, and points can be spent on four abilities:

  • Hint shows the wall where the painting in your hands belongs.

  • Highlight puts a glow on every canvas by the artist whose painting you're holding, even the ones buried in piles

  • Magnet yanks a painting to you from across the gallery.

  • Hands lets you carry a taller stack of paintings.

content_descriptors.notes:
Rehang shows 1,279 real paintings from museum collections, made between the 14th and 19th centuries. A handful of them depict what old religious and history painting depicts: an execution by firing squad, a bandit shot at close range, crucifixions, two severed heads, and Rembrandt's Lucretia, who takes her own life. A few works show classical nudity - bare bodies, no genitals, nothing sexual. A few tavern scenes show drinking and smoking.

All of it is paint on canvas: pictures you pick up off the floor and hang on a wall. Nothing moves, nothing is interactive.

store_data.about_the_game:
Chess, but it snowballs.

Crown & Coup is a single-player roguelike built on chess bones: every run you draft a small army, deploy it on the board, and besiege a series of score targets. Captures earn might, stratagems multiply it, and the numbers climb from "polite opening" to "the scoreboard needs more digits."

THE BOARD IS THE RUN

Battlefields grow with your legend - from a knife-fight 3×3 all the way to a sprawling 12×12. Each act ends in a boss siege that bends the rules against you. Deploy from a drafted pool, spend a limited stock of moves, and decide every siege: bank your score and cash out, or hunt the enemy king for the checkmate jackpot - miss, and the unused moves you gambled are gone.

BUILD AN ENGINE OUT OF AN ARMY

  • 117 stratagems - passive war-machines that trigger on captures, chains, files, sacrifices, and stranger things. Six at a time; order matters; nonsense combos are the point.
  • 14 runestones to socket into individual pieces - your pawn, but it strikes twice and returns home; your rook, but it pays rent.
  • Grimoire rituals, omens, planetary charts - 40+ one-shot and run-warping modifiers that reroll what "chess" means this run.
  • 9 monarchs, each with a racial passive that pushes a different playstyle - from grinding fortress economies to blood-rage tempo.
  • Banners rank up your piece types run over run; decrees and proclamations let bosses and you rewrite the battlefield's law.

A SHOP BETWEEN EVERY BATTLE

Spend siege spoils on stratagems, rune packs, and rituals. Reroll, plan around rarity, and decide whether this run becomes a cavalry-charge tempo build or a pawn-chain doomsday engine.

NO CHESS HOMEWORK REQUIRED

If you know how the pieces move, you're armed. The enemy army follows real movement rules, but this isn't a game of grandmaster calculation - it's a game of building something so unreasonable that calculation stops mattering. (Chess players will still find their line-of-attack instincts paying dividends.)

FEATURES

  • Runs of 30–60 minutes across escalating antes and boss sieges
  • 150+ collectible modifiers across five systems, with an unlock track that feeds discoveries into future runs
  • Cash-out ceremonies, score races, and a mate-hunt gamble every siege
  • Crisp pixel-art armies on a CRT-warmed battlefield, board sizes 3×3–12×12
  • Quality settings and adjustable game speed

store_data.about_the_game:
異世界に転生したあなたのスキルは、「カップラーメンを出す」！？

『ねこっとラーメン』は、猫の獣人たちが暮らす異世界を舞台にした、カップラーメン調理シミュレーションです。

偶然出会った猫獣人の女の子・ユズと、成り行きで小さなラーメン屋を始めることになったあなた。

注文に合った商品と正しい手順を選び、お客さんが満足する一杯を提供しましょう。

注文どおりの一杯を作ろう

・注文に合ったカップラーメンを選ぶ
・フタを開け、かやくやスープを正しい順番で入れる
・適切な量のお湯を注ぐ
・ちょうどよい時間まで待って提供する

調理手順、お湯の量、待ち時間などによって、一杯ごとの評価が変化します。

商品によって作り方も異なるため、手順書を確認しながら正確に仕上げましょう。

複数のお客さんを同時におもてなし

店内には3つの接客レーンがあり、複数のお客さんへの対応とカップラーメンの調理が並行して進みます。

ひとつのラーメンを待っている間に別の注文を進めたり、お客さんを待たせすぎないよう提供順を考えたり。

マウス中心のシンプルな操作で、複数の注文に対応しながらお店を営業していきます。

日ごとに変わる営業

営業を重ねるごとに、新しい種類のカップ麺が加わり、来店するお客さんの数や目標も変わっていきます。

特定の味が人気になる「ブーム」や、いつもどおりには調理できない日の制限など、状況は日によってさまざまです。

「今日の噂」を手掛かりに、その日の状況に合わせて営業しましょう。

営業の前後にはユズたちとの物語が進み、少し不思議な出来事や特別なお客さんも登場します。

成績や物語の中での選択によって、たどり着く結末が変化します。

store_data.about_the_game:
Someone keeps calling.

Five voices, one line, and a game neither of you agreed to play.

Each turn you take the next charge from the queue and choose where to aim it. A corrupted charge costs one signal. A clean one aimed at yourself costs nothing — and hands you another turn. That single rule turns every round into arithmetic under pressure.

The line degrades as you go.

By the last call you can no longer see how many charges are corrupted — only that some of them are. Information becomes a resource, and the Scanner in your hand is worth more than any weapon.

It remembers you.

Die on a line and come back, and the voice will mention it. Not as a script — it is reading your save file.

  • Five callers, each with its own way of playing against you
  • Items that buy information, not damage
  • Endless mode with a depth record to beat
  • A tutorial that teaches by playing, not by reading
  • Seven languages

content_descriptors.notes:
NO CARRIER is a psychological horror game built around a turn-based duel of risk. Its central mechanic lets the player direct a charge at themselves in order to gain an extra turn — presented as a tactical decision, not as despair or self-harm. Harm is abstract: a signal meter and a line of text. There is no blood, no injury, no weapons and no depicted violence.

The game is quiet and tense rather than graphic. Players sensitive to themes of self-directed risk, or to an antagonist that refers to their previous attempts, may wish to know this before playing.

Protect the Circle

Everything revolves around one simple objective: keep the circle alive.

Enemies approach from every direction, and they won't stop coming. Destroy them before they reach the circle and use what they drop to become stronger.

Upgrade Everything

More damage. Faster attacks. Better defenses. Stronger abilities.

Invest your resources into upgrades and watch small improvements compound into massive increases in power.

The stronger you become, the more you can earn. The more you earn, the faster you can grow.

Watch the Numbers Go Up

Start with almost nothing and gradually turn your circle into an unstoppable machine.

Push further, destroy stronger enemies, earn more resources, and find out just how far you can take your build.

Keep Going

The enemies get stronger.

Your numbers get bigger.

The screen gets more ridiculous.

Just keep the circle alive.

store_data.about_the_game:
Strictly speaking, this is not a "game", it is a small program for testing and training the human faculty of prediction.

It grew out of a simple thought: if a person truly possessed the ability to foresee, they could reliably beat the 50% probability line of a coin toss — and research suggests that, at moments of focus and life-or-death stakes, humans can indeed briefly break through probability. Yet humans also carry emotion and greed, which easily lead them to misjudge. And so, this was born:

Guess heads or tails, test your intuition and fortune, and earn points.

It tests neither reflexes nor speed — it tests one thing only: where your intuition points, before the answer is revealed.

Escape from Argos 7 is an incremental game about escaping a hostile alien planet using an old computer that probably shouldn't still work.

You are stranded on Argos 7. Your way out is somewhere inside this machine.

Gather resources, install programs, unlock new systems, automate your progress, and slowly turn a nearly useless computer into your best chance of getting home.

Explore the Computer

Everything happens through a retro desktop interface.

Open programs, discover files, manage resources, and uncover new tools hidden throughout the system.

Every new application gives you another way to push your escape forward.

Upgrade. Automate. Expand.

Start by doing everything yourself.

Generate resources, buy upgrades, unlock new programs, and gradually automate the work you used to do manually.

One small improvement leads to another, and soon your little computer is doing far more than it was ever designed for.

Find a Way Out

Argos 7 isn't going to make escaping easy.

Progress deeper into the system, discover what happened here, and unlock the technology you need to leave the planet behind.

Keep the Computer Running

Click things.

Make numbers go up.

Install suspicious software.

Automate everything.

And find a way off Argos 7.

store_data.about_the_game:
[h2]THE DEBT IS DUE TONIGHT[/h2]

You owe three hundred and twenty. The collector arrives when the night ends.

Between now and then there is a floor full of rooms, a clock that does not stop,

and a card table in every one of them.

Win it back. That is the whole plan, and it is not a good one.

[h2]THE GAME AT THE TABLE[/h2]

Match the colour or the value. That rule is true in every room in the building,

and everything else is built on top of it.

[list]

[*][b]Every card has a price.[/b] Before you commit, the table tells you exactly

what a play costs: the Pressure it deals, the Heat it puts on you, what it does

to your Chain, and how many answers it leaves the other side. Nothing is hidden

and nothing is a dice roll.

[*][b]Heat is the good stuff and the dangerous stuff.[/b] Playing hot makes you

hit harder and makes everything they do land harder too. Braking costs you the

turn. Deciding when to cool down is most of the game.

[*][b]Chain links across the whole night.[/b] Keep matching and you build toward

Fever, the moment the table turns over and starts working for you.

[*][b]Break them or empty your hand.[/b] Two ways to take a round, and they want

completely different decks.

[/list]

[h2]TWENTY-THREE PEOPLE, NOT TWENTY-THREE STAT BLOCKS[/h2]

Nobody across the table is a bag of numbers with a portrait on it. Each one has

a habit they cannot help, a mistake that habit leads them into, and a tell that

fires a beat before they do it.

[list]

[*][b]They have a plan and it has a hole in it.[/b] The Barkeep never watches his

own temperature. The Counter reads a small card as weakness and commits to being

wrong. The Bouncer spends his best cards first because he always has.

[*][b]They watch you back.[/b] Sit down bleeding, or wealthy, or armed, and the

room notices - and reacts by playing differently, in the open, never by a hidden

modifier.

[*][b]They remember.[/b] Break your own chain in front of the Usher and he stops

guarding it. Finish a round hot in front of the Whale and he starts respecting

heat, which ruins him, because recklessness was the only thing he was good at.

[/list]

[h2]THE NIGHT IS THE RESOURCE[/h2]

Twelve rooms are open and you have hours for about five. The bar, the presses,

the fence, the office where a man will lend you more than you should take. What

you did not have time for is the thing you gave up to do something else.

[h2]BRING SOMETHING TO THE TABLE[/h2]

Objects you put on the felt, where everyone can see them. A ceramic pink pig

that hides money from the collector. A brass bell wired to nothing at all. A

small hammer for the card that will not move. Some of them are jokes. Some of

them are a very bad idea. A few are both.

And yes, you can cheat. The room will notice before it acts - you get a glance,

then a stare, then the moment their tell goes quiet. That silence is your last

chance to put it away.

[h2]HIGH TABLES[/h2]

Some rooms are not harder. They are a different game.

[list]

[*][b]THE COLD TABLE[/b] - the brake only works while you are cold.

[*][b]THE PRIVATE ROOM[/b] - the night runs while you sit here.

[*][b]THE DOG TABLE[/b] - the pot shrinks every turn it stays on the table.

[*][b]THE GLASS TABLE[/b] - both hands face up, and nobody here guesses.

[*][b]THE SPLIT TABLE[/b] - one Tempo pool. Spending it is also taking it.

[/list]

[h2]THE HOUSE[/h2]

At the end of the night somebody is waiting who does not play a bigger version

of the same game. He watches how you play, says out loud what he thinks you are,

and then spends the rest of the fight making that true.

He is also certain. Once he has decided who you are, he never revises it - so

the way past him is to stop being the man he named.

[h2]ALSO[/h2]

[list]

[*][b]Play together.[/b] Two to four at one table over the network, taking turns

on one shared deck.

[*][b]Seeded and shareable.[/b] Daily runs, challenges, and an endless table.

[*][b]Drawn by the game itself.[/b] There is not a single image file in this

project. Every card, every face, every mark on the felt is generated at runtime.

[*][b]Built to be read.[/b] Colourblind palettes, text scaling, reduced motion,

screen shake and filter controls, and a full keyboard path through every screen.

[/list]

[i]An original card game. The ruleset is colour-and-value matching, which is

older than any trademark on it, and it shares no names, art or text with any

commercial card game.[/i]

content_descriptors.notes:
DUE TONIGHT contains stylized violence, blood, injuries, threats, and depictions of physical harm. Characters may be shown with bruises, cuts, blood, bandages, broken fingers, cracked ribs, damaged eyes/ears, and other injuries. Some debt-collection and defeat sequences involve intimidation, beatings, injury, and threats of further violence. Firearms may be displayed as part of the game's fictional social interactions.

The game may also depict smoking and alcohol-related table props.

There is no sexual content, nudity, sexual violence, or drug-use content.

The violence is stylized and presented as part of the game's dark-comedy, gambling, and narrative setting.

store_data.about_the_game:
A 2.5D territorial survival ARPG. RTS command, deep crafting and tower defense in one persistent world, with the whole shard standing in it beside you.

Pick a class. Grow a hero. Rent land and raise a fortress on it. Tame pets, break mounts, build a ship and sail for islands nobody has named yet. Then come home at nightfall, because the whole server has somewhere to be.

Hand-drawn sprites in real, lit terrain, and the camera is yours: tilted overhead, over the shoulder, or all the way down into first person. Switch at any moment.

[H] Defend the Tree of Life

One Tree stands at the centre of the world, and everyone depends on it. It bleeds when it's attacked. When it falls, the world enters a Blight. Never a wipe, always something to climb back out of. Assaults arrive on a published calendar, so the server shows up together.

[H] Hold Luciania

The walled city is besieged after dark. Man a gate cannon, hammer the rampart back together between waves, and hold four gates against a horde that gets heavier every night. The city belongs to nobody, which is why everybody defends it.

[H] Build Your Power

Classes. Four of them, with 276 skill-tree nodes, over 130 abilities and mastery schools that change how you fight, not just how hard you hit.

Loot. 550 items, 400 of them gear, dropping constantly with real affixes. Enhance, socket gems, slot runes, chase set bonuses.

Professions. At level 100 you commit to one calling: Blacksmith, Chemist, Miner or Builder.

Companions. 27 pets that level and evolve, and 13 mounts to carry you further. 6 ships open the sea, and the sea has teeth.

[H] Make the World Yours

Buy land and build on it. 47 kinds of building: houses, forges, sawmills, barracks, walls. Train workers to gather while you're away and guards to keep what they bring back. Join a guild, take a town, defend it in scheduled windows so nobody loses a fortress in their sleep.

[H] The World Is Bigger Than the Map

Ring rivers, mountain ranges, deserts, snowfields, volcanic waste, four great isles, hundreds of smaller islands, caves beneath all of it, and dungeons under those. Catch 26 fish species, farm, cook, dig up buried treasure, and fill a bestiary of 189 monster kinds.

Fight Death itself, the Hunter Minotaur that comes looking for you at night, and bosses that surface from the open ocean. Flag for PvP when you want it, never before.

[H] Alone or Together

Two shapes. The shared world, and a single-player version of the same game: same classes, same land, same Tree, with the schedule yours to keep. Nine languages.

Ring rivers, mountain ranges, deserts, snowfields, volcanic waste, four great isles, hundreds of smaller islands, caves beneath all of it, and dungeons under those. Catch 26 fish species, farm, cook, dig up buried treasure, and fill a bestiary of 189 monster kinds.

Fight Death itself, the Hunter Minotaur that comes looking for you at night, and bosses that surface from the open ocean. Flag for PvP when you want it, never before.

[H] Alone or Together

Two shapes. The shared world, and a single-player version of the same game: same classes, same land, same Tree, with the schedule yours to keep. Nine languages.

store_data.about_the_game:
Keep an eye on your wall

Every side belongs to somebody, one of them is yours, and you do not get to leave it. The orbs are loose in the middle.

Whatever you fail to catch eats your armor. When the armor is gone, the side is gone. Not damaged, gone: the arena throws it out and rebuilds tighter. That goes for everyone. Tear a wall off somebody else and the room shrinks just the same. Lose your last wall and you are out.

Four buttons

  • Steer along your wall. The deflector carries momentum. Where the orb lands on it, and how fast you are moving when it does, decides where it goes. You aim with your feet.

  • Parry inside a tight window. Land it and the orb charges. Only a charged orb breaks a core, cracks an armored sentinel or punches through an armored wall. The tighter you cut it, the harder it comes back.

  • Dash along the rail, with a moment of invulnerability, for when the trouble is at the wrong end of your seat.

  • Pulse, a shove in every direction. Costs energy, buys room.

36 levels across six zones

Signal, Fracture, Vortex, Ember, Null, Apex. Every zone ends on a multi phase reactor duel. All of it built by hand, none of it rolled by a generator, and hard on purpose. Outlast the clock, hold integrity, clear the swarm, break the core.

What is coming for you

  • Eight arena shapes from three sides to twelve: polygon, star, ring, superellipse, blossom, gear, spiral, lens. Some rotate. Some pulse. Some shrink while you are standing in them.

  • Eight kinds of orb. The heavy one only slows down when you block it. The splitter becomes two the moment you parry it. The phase orb passes straight through a deflector that did not parry.

  • Ten field devices: post, gravity well, repulsor, rotor, mine, brake field, accelerator, portal pair, charger, cutter.

  • Six machines, including weavers that patch a core faster than you can break it, and sentinels that nothing but a charged orb will touch.

  • Walls with opinions: armored, volatile, self healing, anchored. Each one changes which side is easiest to give up.

  • Run rules that take your tools away: no dash, no pulse, glass walls, blackout, high gravity, and a tempo that climbs for the whole run.

After the campaign

Arcade. Four endless arenas on an escalation ladder that keeps turning the room into a different room. Rivals sit all around you. How many of them you outlast is your score. With Steam leaderboards.

Versus. Two to four people on one machine, six arenas, and a pressure curve that settles it inside five minutes. Quiet open, waves that pack in closer, the chamber draws in, then sudden death.

Six rigs for the deflector, unlocked with stars. Each one moves length, speed, parry window, dash charges and scoring.

31 achievements. The last one asks for the other thirty and marks the game one hundred percent finished. Think you can get there?

Your eyes, your rules

Neon lines on black under an eighties tube: scanlines, curvature, colour fringing, grain. Every part of it has its own slider, and every slider goes to zero. So do shake, hit stop, impact flash and orb trails. Three graphics presets cover everything from an old laptop to the full spread.

store_data.about_the_game:
One ring. One gap.

PERIHELIA is an arcade dodger cut down to a single orbit. You hold one line around the center. Walls close in from the dark, each with one gap in it. Turn, thread it, survive the next one. That is the whole game, and it keeps asking for one more run.

Four ways to play the same ring

  • CLASSIC Pure reflex. The speed ramps up, the walls stack, nothing else gets in your way.
  • TIME The world moves only when you do. Rotation is the flow of time: turn forward to fast-forward, pull back to rewind. The music bends with you, and if you stop it sags into a drone.
  • COLOR The gap has a color, and you only pass if your ship matches it. Half a second of thought lands between you and the wall.
  • MUSIC The walls are not random. Each one sits on a beat, placed from the song's own clock, so the pattern you play is the track. Quiet sections are calm, the drop is a wave. Nothing kills you here: a miss costs energy and combo, and the song plays out.

Build the multiplier, tilt the world

Clean passes build a combo, and the combo drives a multiplier from x1 to x8. Every tier you reach shows. The play field tilts, the camera moves with it, the neon burns hotter. Break the combo and it settles back down. You can read your own run without looking at a single number.

Built to be replayed

  • A separate leaderboard for each mode, so every run counts somewhere.
  • Four difficulty levels. They change how wildly the gaps swing, not only how narrow they are.
  • Keyboard and gamepad, with prompts that match the pad you plugged in.
  • Windows and Linux, handhelds like the Steam Deck included.

Made by hand

No sprite sheets and no stock art. Every arc, ship and spark is drawn in code. The soundtrack is original, and every track carries its own beatmap and its own backdrop. The song is the level.

store_data.about_the_game:
Last time, I couldn't bring them home.

I died on the last day of a ruined world. When I opened my eyes, I was standing in the hotel corridor, days before the outbreak.
The lights were still on. The people I had watched die walked past me carrying breakfast trays.

I remember how each of them was lost. This time, I want to be standing next to them before that day comes.

Thirty days, one hotel, five people I refuse to lose again

Every morning you decide what today is for: go out for food and medicine, reinforce the hotel's doors, or stay behind and help someone finish one small thing.
Supplies are never enough and the horde gets closer every day. Every hour you spend comes back to you on some night later on.

What she mentioned is why you go out tomorrow

Nagisa's bedside lamp needs one battery. Mafuyu's backup radio only hisses.
Bring the part back, fix it together, or track down a missing delivery slip for her. Small things like these become new conversations, and on the day she is in danger, they may give you one more option.

You remember their endings, so you can prepare

Before trouble arrives, find the clues, gather the tools, and earn enough trust that she will follow your plan.
Whether everyone walks out, someone comes back hurt, or you lose her a second time depends on what you did on the way there. And when the rescue is over, the real story starts: you finally hear what she couldn't say that day.

Five heroines, five ways to get close

  • Nagisa — The hotel part-timer who always smiles first. Some nights she quietly asks if you could stay.
  • Mafuyu — The front desk manager who never seems tired. After one night shift together, you see her lean against the wall and close her eyes for the first time.
  • Yua — A stubborn heiress. It starts with checking the ledgers together and ends with the day she finally says "help me."
  • Seira — A gracious socialite. You remember what she did in your last life, which makes trusting her this time the hardest thing of all.
  • Chihiro — The doctor you were too late to save. Bring her and her research back to the hotel, and this city may still have another way out.

Relationships don't end when a choice pops up. They grow through dedicated events and everyday life, and you can be close to more than one of them in the same playthrough.

The rooms at night

This is an adult game. Every heroine has a full set of intimate events, and the H scenes are fully animated, unlocking stage by stage from the first night together to the deeper nights that follow.
The people you saved will choose, in the middle of the end of the world, to give themselves to you.

Make this time end differently

Five character routes, branching events, and multiple endings keep track of every decision you make in thirty days. The memories gallery lets you revisit any scene, including the nights that made you stop.

There are still lights on in the city. This time, bring them home.

store_data.about_the_game:
■ Contact is commitment.

A unit that ends its move inside an enemy Zone of Control does not get to wait and see. It attacks. That single rule removes the safest move in most wargames — the one where you sit still and let the other side commit first — and it changes what every step across the map is worth.

There are no quiet flanks here. Where the two armies touch, a battle happens. So the real decision is made earlier, in the movement phase: what you choose to touch, and what you choose to leave alone.

■ Fight for the line, not for the kill

Ground is taken by movement. Combat exists to push the line forward, and the opposing commander knows it. The AI is built to hold a continuous front, to seal the gaps you open, and to spend its units where the line needs weight — not to farm favourable odds in a corner of the map while its centre collapses.

■ Not won or lost — how far you got

Every battle is scored on seven levels, from Decisive Victory to Total Defeat, and the two sides are not judged by the same standard. At Gettysburg the attacker has to break through in the time it has; the defender only has to still be standing. Holding a hopeless position one turn longer than history did is a result the game will recognise.

■ Six battlefields, seventeen centuries

・Guandu, 200 — outnumbered, with the enemy's grain within reach

・Nancy, 1477 — five turns, and the Duke of Burgundy's last day

・Okehazama, 1560 — Nobunaga wins by taking one head, and nothing else will do

・Sekigahara, 1600 — the largest field in the game, and the battle the game is named for

・Shiloh, 1862 — a surprise that has to be converted before the reinforcements land

・Gettysburg, 1863 — three days, 107 units, and a fishhook that has to hold

The free demo includes three of them: Nancy, Sekigahara and Gettysburg.

■ Open the opponent up

The AI here is not one thing. "Use the river as a defensive line." "Avoid encirclement." "Read what the enemy is trying to do." Forty-eight separate routines stack into one commander's judgement.

And you can switch them off one at a time, from a list inside the game. Build a general who never uses rivers, or who never reads your intent, and watch what changes. Whatever makes this AI difficult, you can take apart and check.

There are nine temperaments: standard, defensive, offensive, delaying, manoeuvre, ultra-cautious and seizing - plus relentless assault, and plain incompetence.

■ Build your own battlefields

A full scenario editor is included. Lay the hex grid, paint the terrain, run the rivers and the roads, place the counters, set the victory conditions. The battlefields in this game were built with the same editor.

■ Features

・Mandatory combat — any unit in an enemy Zone of Control must attack

・Combat groups resolve as 1-vs-N or N-vs-1; never a shapeless N-vs-M brawl

・Artillery with range and line of sight

・Terrain that decides things: river crossings, fortifications, ridges, woods, marsh

・Seven-level graded victory, with separate win conditions for each side

・Opposing generals with distinct temperaments — from relentless assault to plain incompetence

・Night turns, held-back reserves, sudden-death objectives, reinforcement schedules, defection

・A full scenario editor, included — build and share your own battlefields

・Interactive tutorial and an in-game rulebook

・English and Japanese

■ An advisor, if you want one

Hex-and-counter games are not hard because the rules are complicated. They are hard because nothing tells you which of forty legal moves is the one that matters. Ask the advisor and it will show you what it would do and why — or hand it a phase and let it play. Turn it off when you no longer need it.

・Nancy, 1477 — five turns, and the Duke of Burgundy's last day

・Okehazama, 1560 — Nobunaga wins by taking one head, and nothing else will do

・Sekigahara, 1600 — the largest field in the game, and the battle the game is named for

・Shiloh, 1862 — a surprise that has to be converted before the reinforcements land

・Gettysburg, 1863 — three days, 107 units, and a fishhook that has to hold

The free demo includes three of them: Nancy, Sekigahara and Gettysburg.

■ Open the opponent up

The AI here is not one thing. "Use the river as a defensive line." "Avoid encirclement." "Read what the enemy is trying to do." Forty-eight separate routines stack into one commander's judgement.

And you can switch them off one at a time, from a list inside the game. Build a general who never uses rivers, or who never reads your intent, and watch what changes. Whatever makes this AI difficult, you can take apart and check.

There are nine temperaments: standard, defensive, offensive, delaying, manoeuvre, ultra-cautious and seizing - plus relentless assault, and plain incompetence.

■ Build your own battlefields

A full scenario editor is included. Lay the hex grid, paint the terrain, run the rivers and the roads, place the counters, set the victory conditions. The battlefields in this game were built with the same editor.

■ Features

・Mandatory combat — any unit in an enemy Zone of Control must attack

・Combat groups resolve as 1-vs-N or N-vs-1; never a shapeless N-vs-M brawl

・Artillery with range and line of sight

・Terrain that decides things: river crossings, fortifications, ridges, woods, marsh

・Seven-level graded victory, with separate win conditions for each side

・Opposing generals with distinct temperaments — from relentless assault to plain incompetence

・Night turns, held-back reserves, sudden-death objectives, reinforcement schedules, defection

・A full scenario editor, included — build and share your own battlefields

・Interactive tutorial and an in-game rulebook

・English and Japanese

■ An advisor, if you want one

Hex-and-counter games are not hard because the rules are complicated. They are hard because nothing tells you which of forty legal moves is the one that matters. Ask the advisor and it will show you what it would do and why — or hand it a phase and let it play. Turn it off when you no longer need it.
store_data.short_description: Sekigahara, 1600 - and battlefields East and West, 200 AD to 1863. Contact is commitment: thread the ZOC puzzle, and any unit left in an enemy zone of control must attack. No quiet flanks, nothing held back. Pushing the line is the game. A hex-and-counter wargame tuned by a wargamer.

store_data.about_the_game:
A city builder focused on the fun part: building roads and solving traffic problems!

Deep traffic simulation

Your creations are stress tested against a smart agent-based microscopic traffic simulation. Cars take the best route factoring in traffic. They pull into slip lanes and out to avoid queues into junctions. Realistic road hierarchy and interchange design is a necessity to keep traffic moving.

Build a realistic road network

Simple but flexible road tools let you lay out your city your way. Realistic road hierarchies, traffic lights, bypass routes, roundabouts, highways, and interchanges become essential just like in a real life city.

A simple city economy

We kept just enough city economics to give rise to meaningful traffic challenges. Residents need access to shops and workplaces, and hate industrial pollution and road noise. Factories need workers and raw materials. Shops need customers and things to sell. Each time your city levels up you get a batch of buildings to place. The road network must grow!

A never ending supply of maps

Four biomes, each with a unique playstyle, three difficulty levels, and a procedural map generator means you never run out of city to build.

This is a forum-battling game featuring bullet-hell combat.

The protagonist, Su Shihe, thrives on mediating disputes and making waves across online forums. But life rarely goes according to plan. Before he knows it, he finds himself standing against everyone...

Faced with a choice between progress and salvation, which path will he take?

-------------------------------------------------

Xiao Su | Su Shihe

An ordinary office worker drained by his day job. At night, he slips into his pajamas and becomes “A-He” on the forums. Rather than winning arguments, he prefers uncovering the common ground buried beneath the sparks of heated debate.

Easygoing, warm, and composed, he passes through countless clashes without getting caught in the crossfire. But when the real storm arrives, he has no idea what awaits him...

??? | Mysterious Forum Observer

A cyber girl of unknown origin. She excels at breaking chaotic arguments down into positions, emotions, and logic, then reviewing each clash with a deadpan yet playful touch. Occasionally, she leaves notes that only the most observant can discover—as though she can always see just a little more than the person behind the screen.

---------------------------------------------------

store_data.about_the_game:
ONE LAST MACHINE

Earth, 2087.

Humanity is running out of accessible raw materials.

In a desperate attempt to find new resources, the world's remaining scientific teams created Project New Horizon — an experiment designed to open a gateway beyond Earth.

It worked.

Then the gateway refused to close.

The experiment collapsed, the research program was abandoned, and the gateway became an unstable Rift. During the day it lies dormant. Every night, it opens again — and creatures cross into our world.

You were the lead scientist behind the project.

You stayed behind.

Now, from a small workshop near one of the surviving settlements, you have one final objective:

Build the machine. Close the Rift.

Explore deep underground and recover the materials humanity desperately needs. Dig through different geological layers, discover hidden caves, caches and valuable resource deposits, and bring everything you find back to your workshop.

Raw material alone won't save anyone.

Process resources through an expanding production chain. Smelt metals in the furnace, cast components, roll plates and conductors, manufacture advanced parts at the workbench, and gradually construct the Rift Closure Machine.

Every major module physically appears as the machine takes shape.

25%. 50%. 75%. 100%.

But the underground isn't the only threat.

When darkness falls, creatures emerge from the Rift and attack the surface. Fight them yourself, improve your equipment, build defensive turrets and keep enough power running to survive the night.

The people nearby are trying to survive too. Complete manufacturing orders, help the settlement, improve your equipment and prepare for increasingly dangerous expeditions underground.

Your workshop will grow.

Your mine will go deeper.

And piece by piece, the last machine will rise.

Features

  • Mine a large underground world with multiple geological layers and increasingly valuable resources.

  • Discover hidden caves, resource veins, buried crates and rare caches.

  • Build ladders, platforms and tunnel lighting to expand your mining network.

  • Refine raw resources through a complete manufacturing chain.

  • Operate a Furnace, Casting Table, Rolling Mill and Workbench.

  • Manufacture products and complete orders for the nearby settlement.

  • Manage electricity for machines, lighting and automated defenses.

  • Upgrade production equipment to manufacture components faster.

  • Fight underground creatures and survive attacks from the Rift at night.

  • Build and load automated defensive turrets.

  • Upgrade your gear and obtain the powerful Powered Suit with special abilities.

  • Plant trees and gradually restore part of the devastated surface.

  • Construct four major modules of the Rift Closure Machine and watch it physically grow in your workshop.

  • Experience a story-driven progression where everything you mine and manufacture contributes toward one final objective.

MINE. BUILD. CLOSE THE RIFT.

Humanity opened the gateway.

Now you have to close it.

store_data.about_the_game:
OLD SCHOOL SHOOTER, OPEN WORLD MINI-DOOM

Yeah, that's how we define Warslave. An old school linear shooter set in a beautifully handcrafted open world alien world. No skill trees, no perks, no roguelite elements; just pure action.

You are a convict who was sent to a hostile alien planet to serve your sentence. If you can survive till the end and reach the shuttle, you'll be free.

RUN!

This alien world has a dangerous feature. Randomly, it's sun is blocked and all creatures go crazy. When this happens, all you can do is to run and survive as your weapons don't work until you see the sun again. So run, dash, slide, double jump, you do whatever you have to do to survive the madness.

DEADLY ARSENAL

Fight your way through the exotic landscape with 8 weapons and 5 modifications for each where you can find in the world. Don't worry, you can collect plenty of ammunition from the aliens you're gonna kill. You'll only focus on becoming a terminator, a ravager in a hostile world.

DIFFERENT DIFFICULTIES

The standard mod is just for introduction. You die, you respawn from checkpoint and advance. The real deal starts in the others:

  • Ravager: Same game but with 4 respawn chances. And you have to find these "chances" across the world to claim them.

  • Heretic: Enemies have more accuracy and damage. You have 3 respawn chances.

  • Quaker: Enemies have maximum accuracy and damage. You have 1 respawn chance.

  • Fatality: Enemies have maximum accuracy and damage. Increased enemy numbers. Perma-death.

SERVE YOUR SENTENCE & BECOME FREE

store_data.about_the_game:
Zombies aren't Real is a top-down strategy game where you attempt to quell a quick-spreading zombie infection in real-world cities by commanding military forces.

When a level begins you're given a bird's eye view of a city and shown where the infection will begin, but you have time to plan.  With limited resources, carefully choose how you will respond to the infection and establish a plan to save as many civilians as possible.

Once you're ready the chaos begins. The zombies will fan out and begin to infect the population.  You are able to adapt your plan on the fly.  If the zombies break through your perimeter you can reposition forces on the fly and even call in air support such as bombers or gatling gun helicopters to attempt to stop the spread before it gets out of control.

If you're able to eliminate all the zombies you win and your score is determined by how many civilians you saved.

Eventually you'll gain access to the loadout screen where you can specialize and upgrade your forces for future encounters.

Features

  • Play in real-world cities such as New York, Paris, and LA

  • Deploy specialized ground forces against the spreading horde, such as snipers, tanks, and armored personnel carriers

  • Call in air strikes when things get out of hand, but be careful to aim them well to minimize civilian casualties

  • Place down barricades and evacuation stations to control the flow of the spreading infection

  • Spec into your favorite strategy by investing in upgrades for particular units and vehicles

Pick up weapons, magnets, and special powers along the way. Use them at the right moment to attack, pull, push, or sabotage rival teams.

Race through chaotic courses filled with obstacles, dangerous sections, and plenty of opportunities to knock your rivals out of the way.

Play With Friends

Play online with up to 10 players in teams of two. Work together, cause chaos, and be the first team to reach the finish line.

store_data.about_the_game:
Demons of the Dread Sea is a pirate-themed dice-builder roguelite set in a dark fantasy version of the 17th century Baltic Sea.  

Driven by a great purpose, you have accepted a devil's bargain for the power to manipulate luck to your advantage.  As the Captain, gather your crew and equip your ship, customize your dice, and set sail to build your notoriety by defeating ships traveling on the Dread Sea and taking their precious cargo.

But beware - pushing luck to the breaking point has its cost.  Your dice will degrade, corrupt, and eventually betray you.  And when they do, Misfortune will be near to have her vengeance on you for altering the laws of nature.

Gather Your Crew

The synergy of your customized dice with your selected crew makes you a force to be reckoned with.  Each privateer clan has their own distinctive characteristics and play style:

  • Rauðr (the Red Clan) - anarchic berserkers, quick to violence and prone to frenzy.  Damage focused.

  • Grǿnn (the Green Clan) - nomadic and feral wanderers, fiercely loyal to each other.  Strong defense.

  • Svartr (the Black Clan) - Enigmatic, chaotic, and secretive mystics.  Known for corrosion and decay.

Features

  • Alter the Odds: your Captain Abilities allow you to cheat luck itself

  • Upgrade your Dice: convert souls of defeated captains into powerful effects

  • Customize your Crew: from whatever miscreants happen to come by the tavern

  • Equip Your Ship: the Shipwright provides powerful cannons and cannonballs if you can pay in gold

  • Grow Your Haven: Captains perish or retire - the Haven persists and grows ever stronger

  • Collect Story Fragments: discover the sea's darkest mysteries, if you're willing to risk your crew to do so

  • Leave a Legacy: Haven tells the tales of the most famous (and infamous) captains

  • Roguelite Progression: Unlock new content each successful run, discover new synergies and exploit them

store_data.about_the_game:
You wake up, only to be named the new Librarian of Heart‑Lib in a daze.

A young girl named Ye Luoqiu introduces herself as the "Town Mayor" and tasks you with fending off Heart‑Lib’s enemies. A formidable squire, a gentle chef, and a deranged artist all offer their assistance, while the invaders of Heart‑Lib press forward relentlessly.

Unique Combat Feature: Plots

Your cards shift their positions across Plots in sequence. Play your cards in the correct order to satisfy the Plot requirements printed on each card.

The path traced by every card defines its effect, letting you repel enemies across every Plot it passes through.

Unique Deck‑Building Feature: Books

Instead of building your deck from individual cards, you construct it around Books.

Each Book is a card pack containing a set of related cards: Illustrations that chain cards together, Pages that deliver varied effects, and Powerful Reflection cards that require charging‑up. This lowers the learning barrier for deck‑building.

Distinct deck‑building archetypes are determined by different allies, each with uniquely‑styled passives that heavily shape your gameplay experience.

store_data.about_the_game:
Experience a true indie fantasy RPG: no shortcuts, no ads, just the game.

Born from the pages of a fantasy novel and crafted over 500+ hours of passion, this is the RPG for anyone who misses the golden age of strategic turn-based combat. Play as 20+ unique characters and dive into a world where skill and strategy still matter.

[H2] 100% OFFLINE, NO ADS
No internet? No problem. Play anywhere, anytime. No intrusive ads, no energy bars to wait on, no hidden in-app purchases.

[H2] A BATTLE-DRIVEN JOURNEY
Over 35 hours of content set in an original fantasy universe. Your journey is only beginning.

[H2] MASTER OVER 300 SKILLS
Customize your party from a vast pool of abilities. Progress through 3 skill tiers as you level your heroes up to the max level of 20.

[H2] WEAPON SYSTEM — NO DUPLICATES
Unlock 70+ legendary weapons through gameplay. No real-money cost: earn tokens by defeating bosses, and you'll never pull a duplicate. Every token grants new powers.

[H2] 53 EPIC BOSS BATTLES
Face 53+ unique bosses, including 18+ high-level endgame encounters that will test your tactics.

[H2] EXPANSION MODULES INCLUDED
The adventure keeps growing with new characters, weapon banners and boss events.

[H2] A NOTE FROM THE DEVELOPER
I'm an independent developer and author. To bring a world of 100+ unique monsters to life, I used AI for most of the creature illustrations. This let me focus all my energy on what truly matters: a balanced, deep and rewarding gameplay experience.

[H2] THIS IS AN OLD-SCHOOL RPG

  • Everything the game contains is listed here. Nothing is hidden, nothing is missing.

  • No auto-battle. No "win" button. If you lose, you lose because you played badly.

  • Some fights are brutal by design. You're expected to think, plan, fail and try again.

  • Progress comes from understanding the systems, not from waiting.

If you're looking for a modern idle or casual experience, this isn't for you — and that's exactly the point. It's built for players who miss RPGs that asked for real effort.

If you want an honest, high-quality RPG made by a fan of the genre for fans of the genre, this one's for you.

Join the legend. Master the skills. Defeat the bosses. Offline.
