store_data.about_the_game:
Cut their string before they cut yours.

Kite fighting is a real sport, played across South Asia, East Asia and the Middle East, and the rule is the same everywhere. You do not shoot anybody down. You bring your line across their line, and you cut.

Yakko Tako Royale plays by that rule, then fills the sky. Every kite hangs from a string that runs a long way straight down, and that string is the only thing anybody can take from you. Fly above a rival and their string is right there in front of you. So is yours, to them. Now put sixteen of those in one arena.

Sixteen kites, one sky

Online play runs through Steam. Host a lobby and your friends drop straight in, or browse the open lobbies and join a stranger's storm. Up to 16 players fight in the same sky at once, and it is exactly the kind of gorgeous chaos that number promises: strings everywhere, cuts landing in threes, the crowd thinning until two kites circle each other over the water. One button rematches the whole lobby.

Or fight on the couch

Two to four players, one screen, one machine. Everybody picks a stall at the night market, picks a kite and presses START. No accounts, no waiting, because everybody is already sitting in the room. Empty seats take bots, at four skill levels you can mix in the same match.

Easy to fly, wicked to master

  • Hold to fly. Release and your kite glides down. The floor bounces you back up.

  • Steer with the shoulders, or tilt the pad if gyro is on. Your kite goes where the nose points.

  • Lunge to cut. Flying through a string does nothing on its own. The lunge is a short committed dart with a cooldown, and it is the only thing that cuts.

  • Two passes cut a string. Damage stays until somebody clears it, so a rival you caught once is a rival one pass from falling.

From Edo to the patang

The roster runs from the yakkodako of Edo Japan to the fighter kites of the Indian subcontinent. Patang, chand, addha and dabba fly alongside oni, kitsune, tanuki, hannya, kappa and a long line of yokai.

Four arenas, six formats

  • Batsu: An island on an open sea. Room to run, nowhere to hide.

  • Shinkai: the deep sea. Schools of fish cross the board and the anchor splits the arena.

  • Back to Edo: the great wave, in woodblock with Fuji behind. The busiest sky of the four.

  • Yume: the dream, which puts on a different look every single time you enter.

Play a timed round where the most cuts wins, a first to 3, 7 or 12, a battle royale where a cut is final, or last survivor. Set the speed and the whole board changes character. With sixteen in the sky, last survivor is a tournament and a comedy at the same time.

The seven lucky gods, armed

Daruma drift across the board and open on contact. Fukurokuju makes one pass enough. Jurojin makes rivals need four. Benzaiten makes you uncuttable and wipes the passes banked against you. Bishamonten makes you invulnerable and armed, so two rams take a rival out with no string work at all. Hotei clears your own damage. Ebisu casts your lunge far past its normal reach, and Daikokuten hands you the mallet, so you can lunge again almost at once. In a sixteen-kite sky, a god in the right hands turns the whole match.

Learn it in one sitting

A hands-on tutorial runs inside a real arena with real physics, not a slideshow. The game checks you did each thing before moving on, and button prompts show the pad actually in your hands.

Built for the Steam Deck

Developed and tested on the Deck, with gyro steering and its own Steam Input configuration. Runs on Linux and Windows. On the couch, the Deck's own controls count as one of the four players, so a Deck plus one pad is already a two-player match.

Steam achievements climb from your first match to Royale with Cheese, and every takedown you land online counts on the global Takedowns leaderboard.

store_data.about_the_game:
A short, atmospheric narrative experience about choosing to go on when you have no proof it matters.

You are no hero. You're an exhausted soul trudging through crumbling worlds, pulled apart by two voices: one urging you to carry on, one demanding you give up and walk away. Still, you write. Letter after letter, addressed to The Evaluators, seemingly omnipresent beings who might, someday, grant you the peace you're desperate for.

Explore surreal, decaying environments in first person, at your own pace. Write and send letters that open new paths forward. Navigate tense, hands-on trials that test not your skill, but your endurance.

You won't know if your choices matter. And yet, you choose.

One More Letter is a narrative walking simulator with light interactive mechanics. A full playthrough takes under an hour. No combat, no fail states, no branching endings, just a single, honest path through the story.

Features

  • A short, atmospheric narrative walking simulator (under 1 hour playtime)

  • Explore surreal, decaying environments in first-person

  • Write and send letters as you push forward

  • Endure the Evaluators' trials, holding steady while they probe your every weakness

  • A single, linear story, no combat, no fail states, no branching endings

  • Striking visuals paired with ambient sound design

A Personal Note from the Developer

Inspired by my days as an unemployed game maker, One More Letter is for anyone who kept going when they weren't sure why.

store_data.about_the_game:
"...Can you hear my voice?"

A faint voice reaches an old communication terminal. You are the only one connected to a child trapped in a closed-off world.

Explore together, in your own words

Instead of choosing from fixed responses, you speak to the children in your own words. Talk, encourage them, solve puzzles together, and search for a way out. Sometimes, the words you exchange can open a path that was once closed.

A small world hiding a greater truth

The story unfolds across three chapters: the Boy's Chapter, the Girl's Chapter, and the Final Chapter. As you explore, the nature of this closed world — and the truth left behind within it — is gradually revealed.

About the use of generative AI

Some in-game images, including backgrounds and props, were created using generative AI and then edited and adjusted.

Google Vertex AI is used to generate the children's responses during conversations.

Further details are provided in the "AI Generated Content Disclosure" section on this page.

Character illustrations and key art are hand-drawn, while the story and music are created by their respective creators.

How Signals work (please read)

  • An internet connection is required to play.
  • Exploring and talking consume Signals.
  • The full game includes 500 Signals, which are expected to be enough to complete the entire story in a typical playthrough without purchasing additional Signal Packs.
  • Signals do not regenerate over time in the full game.
  • Additional Signal Packs are optional purchases for owners of the full game who want to spend more time talking with the children and explore conversations more deeply.

English language support is planned as a free post-launch update.

LoHa Beta Bot is a 2D action-adventure Metroidvania set in a destroyed world where technology, ancient civilizations, and mysterious life forms are connected.

Play as LoHa Beta Bot, a small but powerful robot cat who wakes up in a world she no longer recognizes. Destroyed cities, robotic creatures, and unknown forces now control what was once a peaceful civilization.

But LoHa is not alone.

As you explore this world, you will meet new characters, face dangerous enemies, discover secrets, and visit places that hide pieces of a much bigger story.

EXPLORE, FIGHT AND DISCOVER

Explore connected 2D areas, fight different enemies, and discover new abilities that will help you reach places you could not access before.

The world of LoHa Beta Bot rewards exploration and curiosity. A path that looks closed may hide a secret, a new route, or something that changes what you thought you knew about this world.

NOT EVERY BATTLE BELONGS TO LOHA

During some parts of the adventure, you will be able to play as other characters, each with their own abilities and gameplay style.

Their stories will connect with LoHa's journey and let you discover important events from different points of view.

A WORLD WITH MORE QUESTIONS THAN ANSWERS

What happened to this world?

Who is behind the machines that now control it?

And why does LoHa seem to be connected to something much bigger?

The answers will not be waiting in one place.

You will have to find them.

Explore. Fight. Discover.

LoHa Beta Bot's adventure is just beginning.

As an amnesiac commander, you lead soul companions shown as battle cards through twenty story chapters. • Full-body dating / Live2D romance routes (visual strategy is cards + key art)

store_data.about_the_game:
Break history into elements. Piece civilization back together.

Hist Maker: ReMake is a level-based element-combination puzzle game about history. As a restorer of history, you begin with myths, legends and the origins of civilization, reconnecting people, the natural world, technology, institutions and culture.

For each combination, choose two elements you have already discovered in the current level and work out how they relate within its era. A successful combination reveals new objects, technologies, people or ideas. Those discoveries join your available elements, ready to become part of the next combination.

At its simplest, a connection can be as intuitive as combining "human" and "stone" to discover "stone tool". As a level unfolds, there is more to consider than what can be made from what: how natural conditions shape daily life, how technology changes production, how writing connects with institutions, and how people, ideas and events influence one another.

These connections draw on human work and daily life, as well as the legends and cultures of different civilizations. Familiar historical knowledge can offer a clue; an unexpected discovery may help you see a connection you had never considered.

Every level has its own historical logic

Each level centers on a particular era or civilization, with its own set of elements, combination results, objectives and completion conditions.

The same two elements may lead to different discoveries in different historical settings. Even a familiar formula needs to be understood in the context of a new era. The level's theme, element descriptions, connections you have already found and current objectives all contribute clues to its puzzles.

From China's ancient legends to prehistoric East Asian societies, river valley civilizations and the early civilizations of the Mediterranean, each region's natural conditions, ways of life and paths of social development become part of the puzzle. The changing roles of tools and food, the growth of production and settlements, and the legacies of people and ideas take different forms in each level.

Every level has a clear goal to work toward, with room to discover other connections along the way. You can focus on its objectives, or follow a new discovery to see what else it might connect with among the elements you already know.

From scattered discoveries to a picture of civilization

The connections you uncover do more than fill an element list or a record of your progress.

At the bottom of the screen, a civilization panorama remains in view: an illustrated historical scroll that gradually fills in as the level progresses. Complete the objectives tied to the panorama, and tools, everyday structures, cultural achievements and symbols of the era appear in the scene, bringing that civilization into view.

New discoveries expand your available elements and open up further combinations. As they add up to completed milestones, the corresponding parts of the panorama appear. The connections you work out gain a visible form, showing not only what you have discovered, but how it fits into this civilization.

What begins as a few isolated clues grows into an illustrated scroll of the era's life and culture. As you solve its puzzles, you build up both the connections you have found and a picture of the civilization restored through your discoveries.

Room to experiment, clues to build on

There is no move limit, so you can try different combinations as often as you like. The game records the pairs you have already tested, so you do not have to remember every attempt.

Element descriptions, the level's setting and the connections you have uncovered all inform your next choice. A new description may make an overlooked element worth another look. Sometimes a clue only becomes useful after you discover something else. An element you could not use before might connect with your latest find.

The hint system takes your progress and previous attempts into account, drawing your attention to new elements you have not yet used or suggesting a direction worth investigating. It offers clues rather than carrying out the combination for you. You still choose the elements and test the connection yourself.

Remaking the original and taking it further

Hist Maker: ReMake includes all of the original Hist Maker's level content, with a remade interface and civilization panoramas.

Inspired by historical archives, the interface brings elements, combination records and level progress into a consistent visual style. The new scrolls give completed milestones a richer visual presence. Element management, combination feedback and progress-aware hints have also been refined around the flow of play. Familiar connections and puzzles from the original return with this new presentation.

You do not need to have played the original. Get to know an element, discover a connection, then use your new find to work out what comes next. That is how each journey to restore history begins.

Beyond remaking the original levels, we are also developing levels across more regions, eras and civilizations. We plan to move beyond civilization's origins into further periods of history, bringing new historical puzzles with their own elements, objectives and combination logic.

store_data.about_the_game:
From the Creator of Turn Based Boxing: Tactics, fight in playground scraps to packed stadiums in a gory, tactics-driven Mixed Martial Arts simulation. Use real MMA strategy, experience MMA history, discover and challenge fighters inspired by the living, the dead, and the legendary.

Step into the violent world of underground Mixed Martial Arts. A realistic turn-based MMA simulation with (optional auto-battle) and perma-death.

Recruit Fighters, Assign Perks, Train Stats, Build Synergies, Manage Injuries, Unlock strategies, Upgrade your Gym, Bribe the Commission and create a roster of MMA Champions.

The Most Savage MMA Game:

This is a hard game. Some fighters will die.

Create Your Gym:

Assemble a diverse team of fighters with unique skills and styles. Each fighter contributes to earning cash for the gym. Use cash to train your fighters and bribe the commission.

Recruit and Customize Talent:

Scour the globe for the most talented fighters to join your gym. From seasoned veterans to up and coming young studs, every fighter has unique strengths, weaknesses, and personalities.

Dozens of Perks / Endless Fighter Builds:

Perks are special abilities that enhance a fighter's performance in different aspects of the game. These can range from increased stamina and power to improved defensive maneuvers or tactical advantages in the ring. As the manager,  choose which perks to enable. Synergize perks with each fighter's talents, weaknesses, fighting style, and the gyms overall goals.

Increasing Stats by Training:

Each stat contributes to a fighter's overall performance in the ring and can be improved. Some stats have stars, meaning the fighter is talented, granting a higher skill ceiling.

Death:

When a fighter sustains injuries during matches they risk death. Fighters age over time. At 60 years old one is vulnerable to death from injuries. At 100 they will die.

Complete Quests and Unlock Strategies:

Meet quest criteria to unlock strategies that any fighter in your gym can utilize. Strategies can be changed before each round of fighting.

Climb the Ranking and win the Undisputed Championship:

With perseverance, strategy, and a little bit of luck, you'll lead your gym to greatness and cement your legacy as one of the greatest MMA managers of all time.

Join the community and share your fighters and compete in tournaments.

Choose between classic pixel art or the new HD remastered textures.

About the Developer:

This game was made by an MMA fan.

Supports 11 languages! (English, German, French, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Russian, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi)

store_data.about_the_game:
Spend your gold each round, none of it carries over. Buy and combine powerful minions, then level up for another board slot and better odds on the rare minions. Discover trinkets, each one bends a rule the rest of your run plays around.

A minion's faction says what it scales, not who can use it. Every one of them does something on any board. Commit to a single faction and push it as far as it goes, or draft a bridge minion: it runs on one faction's engine and pays out in another's, making two halves into one.

Every gold spent, every merge, every trinket, every faction call — it all comes down to one row you can no longer touch. Placement locks, nothing moves, and every synergy on the field is standing on a body that can die. Build an engine that takes your opponents apart.

Key Features

  • Asynchronous PvP Auto Battler

  • Fast runs that take between 15min - 45min

  • Over 70+ unique minions split across 5 factions

  • Deeply synergistic combos, open to be interrupted in unique ways

  • Co-op, play with your friends

  • Champion mode, compete to become the Grand Champion

store_data.about_the_game:
✦ Steam Playtest Announcement

The Steam Playtest for “What’s Wrong with My Drawing?” is scheduled to run for two weeks.

Your bug reports and feedback during the playtest will help us fine-tune the game’s balance, make it more fun, and further polish its content.

※ Important: All progress data and save files from the playtest version will be reset after the test ends and will not carry over to the full release.

-------------------------------------------------------------

From this moment on, your drawing comes to life.

It’s okay if you’re not good at drawing.
Crooked lines and unusual colors become a one-of-a-kind hero in this world.

《What’s Wrong with My Drawing?》 is a free-to-play 2D hack-and-slash idle RPG where you raise a character you drew and venture across horizontal and vertical stages.

Explore diverse regions and combine items, runes, and skills to create your own build. Your progress continues even while you’re away.

■ Emergency! Emergency!

Pink Pig, the mascot of Lillikin Village, has been kidnapped by Red Pig.

Set out on an adventure, defeat countless monsters, and rescue Pink Pig!

■ A Special Hero

  • No matter what it looks like, it becomes the only hero of its kind in the world.

  • Watch the familiar figure you drew embark on an adventure with unique animations.

  • Share a variety of images with your friends.

■ Battles Across Horizontal and Vertical Stages

  • Enjoy 2D hack-and-slash combat as you journey through horizontal and vertical stages.

  • Combine various items with exclusive runes and skills to create your own strategic build.

  • Make the right choices to enhance your character’s strengths and exploit your enemies’ weaknesses.

  • Don’t let the idle gameplay fool you. Sometimes, you’ll need to take direct control.

■ Time Is Gold!

  • Your adventure continues automatically while you’re away or busy with something else.

  • Your character keeps fighting and growing even while offline.

  • Keep this compact desktop RPG at the side of your screen and check in whenever you like.

  • Its lightweight design lets you enjoy it alongside other programs.

■ Key Features

  • More than 500 different items

The Steam Playtest for “What’s Wrong with My Drawing?” is scheduled to run for two weeks.

Your bug reports and feedback during the playtest will help us fine-tune the game’s balance, make it more fun, and further polish its content.

※ Important: All progress data and save files from the playtest version will be reset after the test ends and will not carry over to the full release.

-------------------------------------------------------------

From this moment on, your drawing comes to life.

It’s okay if you’re not good at drawing.
Crooked lines and unusual colors become a one-of-a-kind hero in this world.

《What’s Wrong with My Drawing?》 is a free-to-play 2D hack-and-slash idle RPG where you raise a character you drew and venture across horizontal and vertical stages.

Explore diverse regions and combine items, runes, and skills to create your own build. Your progress continues even while you’re away.

■ Emergency! Emergency!

Pink Pig, the mascot of Lillikin Village, has been kidnapped by Red Pig.

Set out on an adventure, defeat countless monsters, and rescue Pink Pig!

store_data.about_the_game:
《修真从轮回开始》是一款文字驱动的修仙策略角色扮演游戏：淡彩水墨画卷之中，以战前布阵、自动推演的斗法定生死，以跨越轮回的因果传承改写命数。单人单机，无内购。

死亡不是终点，是又一世的起点

本作以「双线轮回」为骨：

纵线——你跨越轮回的因果。功法以灵魂烙印封存，感悟以残忆留存，功德业力与天道亲和随轮回累进；肉身虽陨，灵魂根基不灭，带着修为转世。

横线——世界自有岁月。宗门兴衰，旧识老去，一代代修士来了又去；你当世的抉择化作因果种子，在后世的世间兑现为同道命运与机缘线索。

一世的悟道不会随灰飞烟灭，而世间的变迁从不为你停留。

寿元有尽，战前定生死

凡人寿八十载，修士寿元随境界递增，至渡劫期凡三万年。战斗不拼手速——战前运筹功法神通、法宝丹药、出手先后，布阵既定，胜负自行推演。

游戏特色

  • 双线轮回：跨世因果 + 世界岁月，两线交织方为修真

  • 策略角色扮演：战前布局定生死，斗法自动推演

  • 修真百艺：炼丹 · 炼器 · 阵法 · 符箓

  • 悠闲悟道 / 挑战逆天，双途由你择

  • 渡劫超脱、功德飞升、融入天道，结局万千

  • 文字驱动 · 淡彩水墨 · 剧情丰富 · 多结局

  • 单人单机 · 无内购 · 每一世皆为新的起点

store_data.about_the_game:
Sumi Archery is fifty levels of target archery drawn in the style a sumi-e painting. You stand at a shooting line, hold to draw, and let go. The arrow is affected by the wind and by how long you held; everything else is up to your aim.

The fifty pages are grouped into eight chapters,  the practice ground, a wandering wood, an iron gate, the high passes, an ascension, a mirror lake, a frozen vigil, and a dreaming sky.

When you have had enough of pages, there is an endless run that tours the same backdrops with generated procedural waves, and a quick-play field of five marks that refills as they fall, for as long as you care to stay. You can just mindlessly  play the quick play for hours, there no arrow or time limit, I will add more info and update the entire page in the coming days.

I made this game for myself—just something simple to relax with after work.

store_data.about_the_game:
William Wallace is back. This is unfortunate.

Two Scottish scientists accidentally resurrected William Wallace and an entire 13th-century army. Now they're marching south to liberate Scotland, raising the dead and possessing just about everything on the way.

You're an ordinary British soldier sent to rescue some reporters.

Things deteriorate rapidly.

YOUR GUNS ARE CURSED

Graveheart is a fast retro FPS where you don't choose your next weapon — the curse does. Hurt enemies, fill the Curse Bar, and your weapon automatically changes. Shotgun. Musket. Rocket launcher. Sword. Snowballs. Poo. Deal with it.

FIGHT AN EXTREMELY STUPID INVASION

Undead Scots. Knights. Archers. Zombie civilians. Haunted trees. Possessed statues. Murderous pigeons. Cursed military hardware. Even the bloody trains aren't safe.

THEY ACTUALLY REACT TO YOUR NONSENSE

Set enemies on fire and they'll run around screaming. Terrify them. Make them vomit. Knock them about with ridiculous weapons. The battlefield is half FPS, half slapstick disaster.

WILLIAM WALLACE HAS BECOME A PROBLEM

William Wallace is back from the dead, shouting about freedom and bringing a bigger weapon every time you beat him. Somehow, he has still kept all his hair.

Graveheart is coming to PC in Q1 2027.

Add it to your wishlist if you enjoy retro FPS games, British comedy, undead armies, cursed weapons and the occasional weapon made entirely of poo.

store_data.about_the_game:
ANTE INFERNO is a roguelite card battler where the hand you play is the attack you make. Form a poker hand, unleash a class ability, and stack multipliers until the damage counter gives up on digits.

Your hand is your weapon

Pick up to five cards and attack. A Pair jabs. A Flush devastates. Four of a Kind ends the conversation. Every turn is the same question: cash in the hand you have, or discard and hold out for something obscene.

Four classes

Every class reads the same ten poker hands differently. A Flush is the Warrior's WHIRLWIND, the Cleric's DIVINE JUDGMENT, the Rogue's SHADOW DANCE, the Mage's METEOR.

  • Warrior - block attacks, and hit hard with WHIRLWIND

  • Cleric - heal off the damage you deal, stun with WRATH OF HEAVEN

  • Rogue - flurries, crits, dodges, and ASSASSINATE to finish

  • Mage - the fattest multipliers in the game, and echoes that cast twice

Hold out for a Straight Flush and it is RAGNAROK, APOCALYPSE, DEATH'S HAND or BLACK HOLE. Land a Royal Flush and it is GODSLAYER, RAPTURE, PERFECT CRIME or BIG BANG.

Descend

Burn through The Ashfall and put down CERBERUS. Drop into The Iron City and face LILITH, THE SUCCUBUS QUEEN. Drop again into The Pit, where FATE, THE ETERNAL DRAGON deals the last hand of the run.

Break the numbers

  • Win a fight, multiply your Power, take 1 of 3 boons

  • Level individual poker hands until a Flush outclasses a Straight

  • Chain Court Favor, Ace Lore, Killer Instinct and Echo Chamber into combos that snowball

  • Take OVERWHELMING POWER and double all of it

  • Watch the damage roll past K, past M, past B, into T

Beginner Friendly

  • No poker knowledge needed. The full hand ranking is one button away.

  • Stuck? Sit still and the game lights up your best play. Hit attack and it plays itself.

  • Runs save automatically. Walk away mid fight, pick it back up later.

Poker's ante. Dante's inferno. The stakes only go one way.

shrinking. An eraser chews inward from the edge, day after day, and whatever it reaches is simply gone.

No weapon, no tools, no camp. You have a sketchbook. That is the whole plan.

YOU DRAW WHAT YOU NEED

There is no crafting menu. You open your sketchbook, and on the page are grey guide lines in the shape

of an axe. You trace them by hand. And then you are holding an axe.

Nothing snaps your line onto the guide. That part is you, and the page can tell how well you did.

INK IS EVERYTHING

One resource, and it is inside all of it. Every stroke drinks it. Every glyph. Every obelisk costs a

lot. Enemies splash ink when you land a hit. At night it rains ink, which tops you up and chills you at

the same time.

PUSH THE ERASER BACK

Nine obelisks stand on the page. Walk up, hold the key, pay the ink, and the eraser gives up thirty

metres. That is the only language it understands. Let a day pass without re-inking one and it comes

closer.

SURVIVE THE NIGHTS

Hunger, thirst and warmth drain the whole time. Your tools crack, then break. The Unfinished come out

after dark, and nobody coloured them in. Build a shelter that holds, or draw yourself a bed and sleep

through it.

store_data.about_the_game:
Build Your Research Career

The Next Paper is a card-based idle simulation and management game about building a long-term academic career.

Begin your academic career, develop your abilities, work across different research fields, improve your equipment and research conditions, publish papers, take on projects, and gradually build a career shaped by the choices you make.

As your career develops, you can move into academic positions, mentor students, expand into new fields, and build a body of work that grows over time.

One paper is never the end. There is always another question to pursue, another result to develop, and another paper ahead.

Read and Discover

Read textbooks, journals, and academic papers to gain inspiration and discover new directions for your research.

Different fields, journals, and papers offer different opportunities. Decide what to read, which work to follow, and where your limited research time is best spent.

Reading is not an isolated activity. The inspiration and discoveries you gain from reading can shape the research you choose to pursue next.

Conduct Research

Turn inspiration into research.

Choose a research action, prepare the abilities, equipment, consumables, and other research assets it requires, and decide how to use the resources available to you.

Different kinds of research demand different conditions. Some rely mainly on your own time, while others require specialized equipment or continue running in the background after preparation is complete.

As your research proficiency, abilities, and equipment improve, you can take on more demanding work and produce higher-quality results under the right conditions.

The game is built around decisions rather than constant clicking. You choose what to pursue and what to commit; time carries the work forward.

Turn Results into Papers

Successful research produces research results that can become the foundation of a manuscript.

Choose which results belong in a paper, improve your writing, select references, and build manuscripts for different journals.

Once your manuscript is ready, submit it for review. It may be accepted, rejected, or returned for revision.

Published papers become lasting parts of your academic record and continue to matter as your career develops.

Manage Equipment, Money, and Projects

Research grows beyond individual papers.

Use personal funds and project funding to improve your research conditions, purchase equipment, and expand what kinds of work you can carry out.

As your publication record develops, you can apply for research projects that provide funding and longer-term goals. Published work, completed projects, and the research environment you build can open the way to more ambitious projects and further career progression.

Choosing where to spend money, equipment capacity, and research time is part of building a sustainable academic career.

Build a Team and Advance Your Career

Your academic career develops over time.

Move from doctoral training into formal academic positions, establish yourself in different research fields, and gradually take on greater responsibilities.

Later, you can mentor students of your own. Students have their own fields, abilities, talents, and development paths, and gradually become part of the research environment you build around yourself.

Leave a Record in a Shared Academic World

Published research does not disappear when a progress bar finishes.

Papers enter a shared online academic world of journals, authors, reading, citations, collaboration, and academic history.

Other players contribute to the same world. Fields grow, journals accumulate real publication histories, papers are read and cited, and the academic landscape changes over time.

Your papers, projects, students, collaborations, citations, and the fields you help develop gradually become a record of your own research career.

Progress at Your Own Pace

The Next Paper is designed around long-term planning rather than constant input.

Make your decisions, start your work, and let time pass. Return to completed research, new papers, available equipment, project decisions, and new opportunities.

You can focus deeply on one field or gradually expand into others.

You do not need to watch every progress bar.

There will always be something worth coming back to.

store_data.about_the_game:
FIGHT OR DIE

A hero set out to slay the Demon Lord. He returned cursed. His life bleeds away with every heartbeat, and his body craves blood.

Most action games teach you to retreat when your health runs low. GraveFeast teaches you the opposite. The curse doesn't care how carefully you play. The only way to live is to kill.

GATHER. SLAUGHTER. FEAST.

Don't fight enemies one at a time. Pull them into a single mass, then wipe them out together for a massive surge of stolen life.

  • Gather Drag
    scattered enemies into one killing ground

  • Rush
    Charge forward, dragging foes along with you

  • Execute
    Narrow, devastating strikes with heavy lifesteal

  • Screen
    Clear Erase everything you've gathered at once

BLOOD RAGE & OVERBLOOD

Drop below a threshold and the berserker awakens. Attack speed, movement, and lifesteal all surge. You are most dangerous when you are closest to death.

Feed well enough and your health climbs past its own limit. Overblood grants further power, but it bleeds away fast. Keep the cycle going or lose it.

HAND-DRAWN CARNAGE

Every frame is drawn by hand. Ash-choked skies, fields of impaled bone, and blood that floods the screen when the slaughter peaks.

store_data.about_the_game:
A forest grows slowly as you, a visitor, quietly observe and protect. 

Trees is a quiet background idle game for your desktop about patience and growth. Start with nothing but open ground, and over real time, watch as thousands of trees take root across a sprawling wilderness - one at a time, in their own time, needing nothing but a little patience.

Wind rolls through the canopy, and the forest slowly fills in around you. There's no race here or meter to fill - just a let it grow, check in, and see how far things have come.

But growing isn't the only thing you can do. What you choose to do with a forest you've spent real time building is entirely up to you.

No combat. No fail state. No clock to beat. Just a forest and a kind visitor that'll never do any harm.

store_data.about_the_game:
One gun. One bullet. Six chambers. Somebody's not making it out of this snowbank.

Gather 2 to 6 players, load the revolver, and pass it around — because someone always has to pull the trigger. Every round comes down to nerve: do you trust the duck standing next to you, or do you make sure they go down first?

Talk your way out of it, or don't

Between shots, the round doesn't stop. Team up with another player and watch each other's backs — until one of you decides the alliance has run its course. Slap someone enough times and they'll go down stunned, gun or no gun. Duck into a hiding spot when the pressure's too much, or just shove someone's unconscious body around because you can.

Chaos on the side

When the shooting stops, the snow doesn't. A round of bad weather can turn the map into a rockslide with zero warning. Bored of the roulette table? There's a full blackjack table on the side if you'd rather risk it differently for a while. Random side objectives keep every match from playing out the same way twice.

Stick around, get better gear

Survive rounds, rack up kills, and win matches to earn coins — synced to your Steam account, so your stash carries over. Spend them on hats, accessories, and shirts to make your duck stand out (or blend in, before it matters).

Key Features

  • 6-player Steam lobbies — party up with friends or fill the table with strangers

  • One gun, one bullet, real stakes — a turn-based revolver mechanic where every pass of the gun is a decision

  • Betrayal built in — form temporary alliances and break them whenever it suits you

  • Physical comedy — slap opponents into a stun, shove ragdolled bodies around, get knocked out cold

  • A snowy playground with teeth — ice to slide on, sudden weather that turns hostile

  • A side table for when the roulette isn't enough — a full blackjack minigame you can sit down and play

  • Built-in Steam voice chat — talk trash or coordinate, your call

  • Coin-based duck customization — earn cosmetics through play, saved to your Steam account

store_data.about_the_game:
Compression Quota is an active incremental game about a hydraulic press. Items come down the line, you put them in the press, and the press turns them into scrap cubes. Management grades the cubes. Nobody has told you why.

THE PRESS IS THE JOB

Grab items off the assembly line and drop them on the plate. Hold to build compression, release to slam. Denser items take longer and pay more, and everything that goes in comes out as a spray of scrap cubes. The color tells you what you made before the number does.

THE BELT DOES NOT WAIT

Items keep coming. Anything that reaches the end of the line goes into the incinerator, and the fine comes out of your pay. Grab several at once, decide what's worth pressing and what's worth letting burn, and keep the plate moving. Standing around is a write-up.

SCRAP BUYS UPGRADES

Spend scrap on a branching upgrade tree. Faster press, heavier slams, more hands, a slower belt, payouts that trigger on events you'll learn to fish for. Six tiers of scrap, from common gray to the stuff you'll only see when the press really earns it. Common scrap buys capacity. Rare scrap buys capability.

MANAGEMENT IS WATCHING

Work is organized in shifts. Every shift ends with a report, every week ends with a quota, and every missed quota ends with a write-up. Stack enough write-ups and you'll find out what the press is actually for. Memos arrive on company letterhead. Posters on the wall encourage you to compress harder.

store_data.about_the_game:
Grimhold is the last fortress standing between the living world and everything that wants to end it. Wave after wave, the dark throws its legions at your wall — goblins, undead, dragons, demons, and worse — and only your heroes stand in the way. Build your line, master each hero's powers, chain devastating synergies, and push deeper into five acts of escalating siege. You will fall. And when you do, you'll rise stronger, unlock new champions, and try again — because in Grimhold, every defeat is the start of a better run.

◆ HOLD THE WALL ◆

The dark does not negotiate. It comes in waves — each larger, faster, and crueler than the last — and Grimhold's wall is all that stands against it. Place your heroes with intent, read the battlefield, and turn back the tide before it reaches the gate. Five acts, each with its own horde and its own boss, escalate from goblin raids to the end of the world itself. Every wave you survive brings the next one closer. Every wall you hold is one the dark has to break again.

◆ COMMAND 21 HEROES ◆

From the fire-mage Krash to the merciless executioner Zylvara to Malachar himself, Grimhold gives you 21 distinct heroes — each with their own class, abilities, and role in the line. Unlock them through conquest by meeting brutal challenges, then shape them with a 211-node skill tree, relics, and forge-crafted gear. No two defenders play alike, and no two runs demand the same team. The right hero in the right place turns a losing wall into an unbreakable one.

◆ CHAIN YOUR SYNERGIES ◆

Heroes are stronger together. With 33 synergies to discover, the way you build your line matters as much as who's in it — stack the right champions and watch a modest defense erupt into a machine that shreds entire waves before they land a hit. Draft, experiment, and find the combinations that break the game in your favor. The dark adapts. So must you.

◆ DIE, LEARN, RISE ◆

Grimhold is a roguelike to its core: you will lose runs, and that's the point. Every defeat feeds a permanent account that unlocks heroes, relics, and mastery. Forge new gear between attempts, bank essence toward lasting power, and return to the wall sharper than before. The siege resets — you don't. Progress is never erased, only earned.

◆ CHOOSE YOUR SIEGE ◆

Play the way you want to be tested:

  • Normal — the full campaign across all acts, the intended Grimhold experience.

  • Hard — a punishing rebalance for defenders who've mastered the wall.

  • Infernal — the ultimate difficulty, where only the sharpest builds survive.

  • Endless — no final wave, no mercy. How deep can you hold before the dark drags you under?

With 75 achievements, a bestiary of 83 catalogued foes, weekly challenges, and a battle pass of unlockables, there is always one more wall to hold — and one more reason to return.

And when you do, you'll rise stronger, unlock new champions, and try again — because in Grimhold, every defeat is the start of a better run.

◆ HOLD THE WALL ◆

The dark does not negotiate. It comes in waves — each larger, faster, and crueler than the last — and Grimhold's wall is all that stands against it. Place your heroes with intent, read the battlefield, and turn back the tide before it reaches the gate. Five acts, each with its own horde and its own boss, escalate from goblin raids to the end of the world itself. Every wave you survive brings the next one closer. Every wall you hold is one the dark has to break again.

◆ COMMAND 21 HEROES ◆

From the fire-mage Krash to the merciless executioner Zylvara to Malachar himself, Grimhold gives you 21 distinct heroes — each with their own class, abilities, and role in the line. Unlock them through conquest by meeting brutal challenges, then shape them with a 211-node skill tree, relics, and forge-crafted gear. No two defenders play alike, and no two runs demand the same team. The right hero in the right place turns a losing wall into an unbreakable one.

◆ CHAIN YOUR SYNERGIES ◆

Heroes are stronger together. With 33 synergies to discover, the way you build your line matters as much as who's in it — stack the right champions and watch a modest defense erupt into a machine that shreds entire waves before they land a hit. Draft, experiment, and find the combinations that break the game in your favor. The dark adapts. So must you.

◆ DIE, LEARN, RISE ◆

Grimhold is a roguelike to its core: you will lose runs, and that's the point. Every defeat feeds a permanent account that unlocks heroes, relics, and mastery. Forge new gear between attempts, bank essence toward lasting power, and return to the wall sharper than before. The siege resets — you don't. Progress is never erased, only earned.

◆ CHOOSE YOUR SIEGE ◆

Play the way you want to be tested:

  • Normal — the full campaign across all acts, the intended Grimhold experience.

  • Hard — a punishing rebalance for defenders who've mastered the wall.

  • Infernal — the ultimate difficulty, where only the sharpest builds survive.

  • Endless — no final wave, no mercy. How deep can you hold before the dark drags you under?

With 75 achievements, a bestiary of 83 catalogued foes, weekly challenges, and a battle pass of unlockables, there is always one more wall to hold — and one more reason to return.
store_data.short_description: A dark-fantasy tower defense roguelike. Hold the wall against endless legions, command 21 unique heroes, and forge a run that's never the same twice. Every wave survived is a choice; every choice reshapes the siege. How long can Grimhold stand?

store_data.about_the_game:
A New Home. A Lost Way Back.

In 2247, humanity embarks on its first major interstellar colonization mission.

Shortly before reaching its destination, the journey ends in disaster. Only 50 people make it to the alien world of Elyra. Critical data and navigational information are lost — including the coordinates of Earth.

On Elyra, humanity begins to rebuild.

How far your new civilization will go is up to you.

Build a New Colony

Begin with 50 survivors, limited supplies, and a makeshift settlement.

Secure food and water, gather resources, and construct housing, production facilities, storage buildings, research centers, and essential infrastructure.

Expand roads and supply networks as you transform an improvised settlement into an increasingly complex colony.

Decide How Far Your Civilization Will Go

VALTERION lets you choose the focus of your game in Singleplayer.

Colony

Focus entirely on building and developing your new home for the long term.

Expand across large areas, develop complex production chains and infrastructure, and build a self-sustaining civilization.

Spaceflight and galactic expansion are not part of this mode.

Galactic Expansion

Begin as a small colony on Elyra as well, but continue far beyond the planetary settlement phase.

Research spaceflight technologies, build ships, explore other worlds and star systems, and lead humanity out into the galaxy.

In both ways of playing, your colony forms the foundation of your civilization.

Develop a Functioning Economy

Resources, production, storage, energy, transportation, and workforce management are all interconnected.

Extract natural resources and process them into materials and products. Build production chains, manage storage capacities, and adapt your economy to the needs of your population and industry.

As your colony grows, its economic systems become increasingly complex.

Research Opens New Possibilities

Much of the knowledge carried by the original expedition was lost.

Research new technologies and unlock more advanced buildings, production methods, energy sources, and infrastructure.

In Colony mode, your technological development remains focused entirely on your new home.

If you choose Galactic Expansion, your technological journey will eventually lead humanity back into space.

Assemble Your Own Advisory Council

As your civilization grows, so does the number of challenges you must manage.

Hire different advisors to support you in research, economics, colony development, and security.

In Galactic Expansion, additional areas such as trade, diplomacy, and fleet management become part of their responsibilities.

Not every candidate possesses the same skills. Decide who you hire and which areas you want to invest in.

Explore Elyra — and, If You Choose, the Galaxy

Survey Elyra, discover resource deposits, and expand into new regions.

If you choose Galactic Expansion, your civilization can eventually leave its new home and begin exploring the galaxy once again.

Build ships, discover other planets and star systems, establish new colonies, and secure resources far beyond Elyra.

And somewhere among the stars, there may still be a trail leading back to Earth.

You Are Not Alone

In Galactic Expansion, you will discover that other intelligent species and civilizations exist throughout the galaxy — and not all of them will react to humanity in the same way.

Some seek trade and diplomatic relations. Others simply want to be left alone. Some are territorial or openly hostile and may see your growing civilization as a threat.

Their levels of technological development also vary greatly.

Some command powerful interstellar empires. Others are only taking their first steps into space.

And some have never left their homeworld at all — perhaps unaware that intelligent life exists anywhere beyond their own planet.

For them, humanity may become their first encounter with an alien civilization.

Trade, Diplomacy, and Conflict

If you choose Galactic Expansion, you will build relationships with other civilizations, establish trade, and decide how humanity should find its place in the galaxy.

But interests can clash, and relationships can change.

If diplomacy fails, you must protect your colonies.

Develop ships, assemble fleets, and decide how your military forces should be used.

Something Is Out There

The farther humanity ventures into unexplored regions of the galaxy, the more often it encounters ancient stories, forgotten warnings, and traces of a power many believed had vanished long ago.

Perhaps they are only stories.

Perhaps they are not.

Because somewhere among the stars, something appears to have awakened once again.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------


Begin with 50 survivors.

Build a new civilization.

Build a new home — or reach for the stars.

Find the lost way back to Earth.

VALTERION: THE LOST EARTH

Survival is only the beginning.

store_data.about_the_game:
Automate a Baby’s First Year

CRADLE PLANT: First Year Operations is a factory automation simulation about caring for babies from birth to age one.

In a near future where dual-income households have become the norm, families can no longer easily manage the most demanding first year of childcare on their own.
The answer is the Cradle Plant—a facility that automates feeding, sleep, hygiene, and health care while parents continue working.

Your job is not to care for each baby by hand.
It is to design a system that keeps providing the right care even when you are no longer directly involved.

React After They Cry—or Route Them Before They Do

At first, you must check each crying baby yourself, identify whether they are hungry, tired, or need changing, and send them to the appropriate facility.

But as more babies arrive, manual care quickly becomes impossible.

Introduce sensors, routing gates, and care arms to gradually transfer the entire process—

observe → decide → transport

—from yourself to the production line.

Hungry? Send them to feeding.
Tired? Route them to a bed.
Sick? Direct them to treatment.

Turn the decisions you once made manually into part of the factory itself.

Your Factory Must Grow with the Babies

Babies grow inside the facility, and their needs change with age.

Newborns require frequent feeding and long periods of sleep. As they grow, they spend more time awake and begin to need play, stimulation, weaning, and protection from illness.

And no matter how efficient your factory becomes, you cannot make a baby turn one any faster.

What matters is not production speed, but:

How many babies can you care for reliably at the same time?

Expand yesterday’s stable line, add new routes without tearing everything down, and continuously reshape the same facility as the babies grow.

The Same Care Does Not Work the Same Way for Everyone

Some babies sleep better in quiet surroundings.
Some relax around others.
Others respond differently to rocking, movement, music, or physical contact.

Standardized facilities can care for many babies efficiently. Personalized care, however, costs more, takes more space, and handles fewer babies at once.

How much individuality can you accommodate without sacrificing efficiency?

The answer is built into the lines you design.

store_data.about_the_game:
You're It! is competitive TAG: a fast 2.5D party platformer where being chased is bad, and glowing is worse.

Run, wall-jump, slide, grapple, dodge, flop, and shove your way through crowded arenas filled with movement toys and unpredictable hazards. The controls are easy to pick up, but chaining everything together while seven other blobs are bouncing around takes practice.

Pass It Before It Pops

Hot Potato is the main event. One player starts with the glow, and an unpredictable fuse begins counting down. Tag someone to pass it. Whoever is holding it when time runs out explodes into a ball of goo and is eliminated.

The round continues until only one blob remains. Survive longer to earn more GOO, then do it again across a five-round tour of different arenas.

Movement Is the Game

Getting away is only half the job. Good players use the arena (and each other) to control the chase.

  • Grapple across gaps and swing around anchors

  • Wall-jump, boost, and slide to maintain speed

  • Spot-dodge an incoming tag at the last second

  • Use the Tactical Flop to change direction or drop quickly

  • Lunge and swell up when you're It to catch slippery targets

  • Shove players into danger and earn points for setting up a tag

  • Bounce off other blobs and turn collisions into shortcuts

40 Arenas That Change How You Play

Every round moves to a new enclosed arena with its own layout and gameplay quirk. Portals reroute chases, gravity changes direction, bumpers launch players across rooms, and moving platforms create routes that never stay safe for long.

Other arenas introduce wind tunnels, sticky floors, conveyor belts, magnetic fields, disappearing platforms, launch pads, low gravity, and plenty of bad places to stand when the glow starts beeping.

Four Ways to Make a Mess

  • Hot Potato: Pass the glow before its fuse runs out. Last blob standing wins.

  • Classic Tag: Catch another player, pass the problem, and score through quick tags and clean escapes.

  • Infection: The infected team grows with every tag, but rare powerups can turn infected players back.

  • Glow Chase: Hold the glow to score while everyone else tries to steal it.

Play Your Way

Create an online room, invite friends through Steam, join with a room code, or search for a public match in your chosen mode. You can also play locally with multiple controllers or fill open spaces with bots for solo practice.

Matches support up to eight blobs, including online players, local players, and AI opponents.

Make a Better Blob

Customize your blob with different colors, faces, finishes, and ridiculous hats. Playing matches earns profile XP, and every level unlocks another cosmetic until the complete collection is available.

All gameplay and cosmetic content is included in the base game.

store_data.about_the_game:
Disclaimer: Lost Liminal: Prologue is a free playable introduction to the Lost Liminal series. The game is currently in active development, and its content may be expanded and updated over time.      


       
Welcome to the Liminal World！

When you wake up after a car crash, you find yourself trapped in a world that should not exist.

You are George, an ordinary person with no memory of how you arrived here. To find your way home, you must explore this ever-changing realm, recover fragments of your past, and uncover the truth hidden behind the accident.

But this place has rules of its own. Break them, and you may not survive.   

                        

                                                                          Explore the unkown                                            

The Liminal World is made from countless spaces stitched together in impossible ways.

One moment, you are walking through the damp hallway of a cheap motel, surrounded by peeling wallpaper and flickering lights. The next, you step into a forgotten seventeenth-century library covered in dust and fading paintings.

                                                            Every corridor may lead somewhere new.                                                        
                      
   
     Find the exit        

          This unsettling world is more than a backdrop; it is a puzzle waiting to be uncovered. With your night vision guiding you through the darkness, you’ll search for hidden clues, interact with the environment, and unlock the mechanisms that stand between you and the truth. But the deeper you explore, the more the world around you begins to shift. The following list of features should help show what these ever-changing spaces have in store.

           （1）Your night vision reveals hidden markings, objects, and clues concealed in the darkness!

           （2）Interact with objects, machinery, and mechanisms throughout the environment to unlock new paths
           （3）Piece together clues and solve interconnected puzzles by carefully observing your surroundings
           （4）Familiar rooms may shift as you explore, revealing unseen places.



 





  



Something Is Watching You...






=======================================================================================
Lost Liminal: Prologue is the opening chapter of the multi-chapter Lost Liminal series and the beginning of the full Lost Liminal experience. It introduces George, the Liminal World, and the horrors lurking beyond its doors. As you venture deeper into the liminal spaces, you will gradually uncover the truth behind this mysterious world.

=======================================================================================

If you enjoy the prologue, please add Lost Liminal to your wishlist. Your support will help us continue building the complete Lost Liminal experience.

store_data.about_the_game:
Plan at the same time. Resolve together. Survive the bounce.

Bouncer is a compact competitive strategy game built around simultaneous decisions. Each player chooses a move, then both moves resolve together. That simple rule turns every turn into a prediction: where is your opponent going, what space are they trying to control, and what happens if your slimes collide?

COLLISIONS CHANGE THE BOARD

When slimes meet, Bouncer's collision rules send the action into a bounce. Pieces can be pushed back through previous spaces as the interaction resolves, creating situations where positioning matters just as much as the move you choose now. A move that looks safe can become dangerous when both players have the same idea.

REACH THE BASE — AND HOLD IT

Getting to the opposing base is only part of the challenge. To win, you need to occupy your opponent's base and still be there when the next turn begins. That gives your rival one last chance to knock you away and makes every attack a contest over both timing and position.

SMALL BOARDS, BIG DECISIONS

Bouncer keeps the play space compact so every move matters. Special board spaces and different layouts can change the safest routes, create new collision opportunities, and force both players to adapt.

FEATURES

• Simultaneous movement: both players commit before the turn resolves.

• Bounce-driven collisions that reward prediction and positioning.

• Compact grid-based boards designed around quick tactical decisions.

• A base-capture objective that gives the defending player a chance to respond.

• Special board spaces and layouts that change how you approach each match.

• Local two-player competitive play.

Every move is simple to make. The hard part is guessing what happens when your opponent moves too.

OTHERHOLD is a fantasy voxel sandbox action RPG where exploration, combat, and building are all part of the same adventure.

Your life in your old world has ended. Without knowing how or why, you awaken once more in a completely unfamiliar place: a world of magic, creatures, ancient civilizations, and dangers you have yet to understand.

You have been given a second life. And this new world is far from safe.

Explore freely, gather resources, grow stronger, venture into dangerous dungeons, and build a place to call your own.

BUILD AND DEFEND

Gather resources and shape the world around you to build bases, fortifications, and defenses. Prepare yourself against creatures and enemy forces that threaten everything you have built.

FORGE YOUR OWN HERO

Develop your character, acquire new equipment, and experiment with different weapons, abilities, and fighting styles as you face increasingly dangerous enemies.

Fight up close, attack from a distance, or wield extraordinary powers to overcome anything standing in your way.

EXPLORE A VOXEL FANTASY WORLD

Travel through forests, mountains, settlements, structures, and territories inhabited by different creatures and civilizations.

Explore from the ground or take to the skies and discover what lies beyond your home.

VENTURE INTO DUNGEONS

Discover dangerous places filled with enemies, rewards, and challenges. Enter prepared, defeat the creatures guarding them, and return with resources and equipment that will help you grow stronger.

SURVIVE THE INVASIONS

Your enemies will not always wait for you to find them.

Fortify your position, prepare your defenses, and fight alongside your allies when the dangers of the world arrive at your doorstep.

YOUR SECOND LIFE. YOUR FORTRESS. YOUR STORY.

Explore. Fight. Build. Grow stronger.

Your life ended once.

This world may have given you a second chance.

If you can save it.

store_data.about_the_game:
They reach the gate after dark. You decide who reaches the village.

You are the keeper of a mountain checkpoint said to stand on the road to the dead. Most travellers are human. Some are yokai concealed in human form.

Read the pass. Then read the person.

Every traveller brings a pass: name, age, home, destination, trade, issue date, and seal. Compare it with the face in front of you. A forged seal or an impossible village may send a human back down the road. Painted-black eyes, a hidden fang, a seam at the throat, or a sixth finger point to something else.

You may challenge two entries on each traveller's pass. Pick the fields that do not add up, listen to the answers, and decide what the discrepancy means before the incense burns out.

Pass. Turn away. Cut down.

A wrong judgment does not end at the gate. Cut down too many humans and you will be executed. Let too many yokai through and the village below is lost. At dawn, the cost of your judgments follows you home. Your wife writes, your son needs medicine, and food may cost more than you have.

Seven nights, and no rule stays simple.

New edicts arrive as the week wears on. The papers grow less trustworthy, and familiar travellers may return. A limited-use Demon Mirror can reveal what your eyes cannot, but it cannot make the judgment for you.

  • A complete seven-night story with 83 travellers and six endings
  • Runs last about 30–40 minutes; choices carry across the week
  • An endless Night Ledger mode unlocked after reaching an ending
  • A Yokai Ledger that records only tells you have encountered
  • Standard, Gentle, and No Limit timing; every ending remains available
  • Playable from start to finish with mouse and keyboard, or keyboard alone
  • Interface text in Japanese, English, Simplified Chinese, and Korean

store_data.about_the_game:
A cozy, casual ant farm

A red plastic tank, a few centimetres of sand, and one queen with her first few workers, just breaking out to the surface. You give them sugar, protein and a little water. They do everything else. There is nothing to win and nothing to lose, and no clock but the ants' own. It is the ant farm you had as a kid, except for one important difference - this colony has a queen, allowing you to see the full lifecycle of this wonderful creature.

Watch a nest grow

The colony starts sealed in a single chamber. The first workers cut their way up to the light, carry the sand out grain by grain, and heap it beside the door. Then they dig: a staging room under the entrance, nurseries for the eggs, the larvae and the cocoons, a larder for the food you bring, a royal chamber for the queen, and a midden for what is left over. Every room is dug to a plan the colony made when it was founded, and every tank's plan is its own. When those rooms are full, the ants keep digging. Keep playing long enough and the whole tank is honeycombed.

Real ants, doing real things

These are black garden ants, Lasius niger, the ant of every pavement and garden wall. The colony follows the real life cycle: a founding queen feeding her first brood from her own body, the small pale first generation, eggs and larvae carried to the damp end of the nursery, cocoons stacked where it is dry. Workers walk on whatever they are standing on, slip, fall, turn at the speed an ant can turn, and stop to touch antennae when they meet. The care booklet in the corner of the tank tells you what you are looking at, and where the game bends the biology, it says so.

Three tools

Sugar keeps the workers running. Protein grows the colony. Water goes where you put it, and the ants nest where the water is. That is the whole toolbar. You shape the world; the colony decides what to make of it.

It lives on your desk

The tank keeps going while you work, and it keeps going while you are away. Come back after a weekend and the colony has been busy. Leave it for a fortnight and the nest goes quiet, not dead.

What is in the tank today


  • One species, the black garden ant, with its full caste table: queen, the first small workers, workers and callows.
  • A nest laid out at founding and built in order, then a nest that keeps growing until the sand is honeycombed.
  • Sand that is conserved: every grain the ants cut comes out of the door and goes on the heap.
  • Water that falls, beads on the surface, soaks in and drains, and a colony that moves its brood to follow it.
  • The care booklet: a species sheet, the colony's story so far, and an encyclopedia of the species to come.

store_data.about_the_game:
A new genre of MMO.   A new world to explore in familiar ways.   Story rich lore with multiple Game types combined into one evolving adventure!

Plan of Tactics

Your story shapes your fate.

Plan of Tactics is a multi-genre online ( MGOG ) fantasy game that combines MMORPG exploration, real-time strategy, and MOBA-style combat into one connected experience.

Choose your allegiance, build your character, explore a persistent fantasy world, complete quests, discover hidden areas, gather resources, and fight for control of a world...

But your adventure doesn't stop with your character!

One World. Multiple Ways to Play.

Explore the World

Enter the world as one of 27 unique playable classes and experience Plan of Tactics as an MMORPG. Explore cities and wilderness zones, complete quests, fight enemies, collect equipment, uncover secrets, and build your character.

Play on your own or enter the larger multiplayer experience.

Command Armies

Step onto the battlefield in real-time strategy combat, where three major factions fight for dominance.

Build your forces, gather resources, expand your army, defend your territory, and pursue multiple paths to victory.

The results of these conflicts can influence the larger world.

Become a Champion

Take control of powerful heroes in MOBA-style battles where positioning, teamwork, abilities, objectives, and character play style determine the outcome.

The heroes you encounter throughout the world aren't disconnected characters, they are part of the same universe, factions, and ongoing conflict.

Three Sides.

The struggle for the world is divided between three sides, each with multiple political factions:

The Empire
Imperial • Arcane • Faithful

The Returned
Bone • Flesh • Blood Thirsty Vampires

The Guardians
Ants • Weres • Omni

Each brings its own identity, units, champions, locations, and approach to the conflict.

Your Actions Matter

Plan of Tactics is built around a simple idea:

Different styles of play should contribute to the group and be able to hold their own.

Fight for your faction in strategic battles.
Enter contested territories in the RPG world.
Take control of champions in arena combat.
Complete quests and influence locations.
Watch control of the world change as the conflict continues.

Whether you prefer exploring as an adventurer, commanding an army, or fighting as a champion, you're participating in the same larger struggle.

Play Your Way

  • Explore a connected fantasy RPG world

  • Choose from a large roster of playable classes

  • Complete quests and discover hidden locations

  • Battle creatures, enemies, and rival factions

  • Gather equipment and resources

  • Command armies in real-time strategy battles

  • Fight with powerful champions in MOBA-style combat

  • Experience multiple victory conditions and strategic approaches

  • Play single-player content at your own pace

  • Join the evolving multiplayer conflict when you're ready

This isn't three games sitting next to each other.

It's one world viewed from three different perspectives.

Welcome to Plan of Tactics.

Enter the world as one of 27 unique playable classes and experience Plan of Tactics as an MMORPG. Explore cities and wilderness zones, complete quests, fight enemies, collect equipment, uncover secrets, and build your character.

Play on your own or enter the larger multiplayer experience.

Command Armies

Step onto the battlefield in real-time strategy combat, where three major factions fight for dominance.

Build your forces, gather resources, expand your army, defend your territory, and pursue multiple paths to victory.

The results of these conflicts can influence the larger world.

Become a Champion

Take control of powerful heroes in MOBA-style battles where positioning, teamwork, abilities, objectives, and character play style determine the outcome.

The heroes you encounter throughout the world aren't disconnected characters, they are part of the same universe, factions, and ongoing conflict.

Three Sides.

The struggle for the world is divided between three sides, each with multiple political factions:

The Empire
Imperial • Arcane • Faithful

The Returned
Bone • Flesh • Blood Thirsty Vampires

The Guardians
Ants • Weres • Omni

Each brings its own identity, units, champions, locations, and approach to the conflict.

Your Actions Matter

Plan of Tactics is built around a simple idea:

Different styles of play should contribute to the group and be able to hold their own.

Fight for your faction in strategic battles.
Enter contested territories in the RPG world.
Take control of champions in arena combat.
Complete quests and influence locations.
Watch control of the world change as the conflict continues.

Whether you prefer exploring as an adventurer, commanding an army, or fighting as a champion, you're participating in the same larger struggle.

Play Your Way

  • Explore a connected fantasy RPG world

  • Choose from a large roster of playable classes

  • Complete quests and discover hidden locations

  • Battle creatures, enemies, and rival factions

  • Gather equipment and resources

  • Command armies in real-time strategy battles

  • Fight with powerful champions in MOBA-style combat

  • Experience multiple victory conditions and strategic approaches

  • Play single-player content at your own pace

  • Join the evolving multiplayer conflict when you're ready

This isn't three games sitting next to each other.

It's one world viewed from three different perspectives.

Welcome to Plan of Tactics.

store_data.about_the_game:
Pick from the gacha offer

Each round starts with a gacha offer. Take one sushi, spend coins to reroll, hold one for the next spin, or walk away with the coins instead. The roll is random; the choice after it is yours.

Build the four-slot line

Your counter has four slots in one line, and the piece at the front takes the first normal hit. Once you press Fight, the round is out of your hands. Taunt draws attacks. Pierce skips the front. Splash catches the next slot. Echo repeats a neighbour's skill. A lineup can lose, swap two places, and win.

Merge copies. Blend two pieces.

Copies merge and gain stars. Two pieces can be blended once per round into sushi that never appears in the gacha. There are 21 blend-only creations and 53 kinds to find in all.

Twelve rounds, twelve ranks

Clear twelve rounds to finish a run, one fight per round. Rounds 4, 8 and 12 are Chef Fights: a set opponent waits, and beating it earns a free pick next round. On other rounds the shop changes: fairs, sales, market, prep, regulars. Your opponents are lineups that other players left behind in the same round (asynchronous, like Backpack Battles: nobody waits for anybody). Offline, or when nobody is there yet, you fight lineups recorded from 24 bot runs. Higher ranks change more than enemy numbers: coins, offer size, star limits, and series-bonus rules can all tighten. The daily run uses the date as its seed, so everyone gets the same shop. The whole game also works offline. The chef's lineup is shown a round early, so you can build for it. Your last 30 runs stay in the Records.

store_data.about_the_game:
From Order to Chaos

Waking up from a short nap after feeling the earthquake, you realize your perfectly organized video game collection has been scattered all over the room. Your job is to sort every game back onto its proper shelf according to the saga and console it belongs to.

Different Consoles and Exclusives

Each console has its own exclusives — marked with a sticker on the back of the case — as well as multi-console titles that were released for it. Identify games by each console's distinctive style and return them to their shelf.

Unlock the Consoles

Once you've completed a shelf, that console will reappear under the TV. Unlock them all.

Abilities

As you progress through the game, new abilities will become available to speed up your organizing and complete the collection more efficiently.

Key Features

  • Organize 2,880 games by console

  • Unlock all 18 available consoles

  • Unlock abilities to speed up your organizing

  • Restore order and harmony to your game room

store_data.about_the_game:
A bar that is open whenever you are.

Push the door, take a stool, and talk. Mara is behind the counter — she has opinions about the weather, the regulars, and what you should be drinking. She is not a menu tree. Whatever you say, she answers.

She remembers you.

Not a save file with your name in it. After you leave, the conversation is distilled into what she actually retained: things about you, moments worth keeping, threads left open, and a slowly shifting read on how well she knows you. Come back next week and she picks it up — including how long you were gone.

Everything she remembers is visible to you, and anything you delete is gone from her head for good.

She actually tends bar.

Thirty-odd real builds behind the counter, and she knows them. Ask what goes into a sazerac and she will tell you truthfully. Ask for something bitter, or something to sip on, and she will pick something that fits. The whiskey classics are in her hands from years of practice; a drink she has made twice, you will watch her think through.

What you order goes on your tab at her prices, and settling up is its own small moment.

The bar is a place, not a backdrop.

  • Every night is its own night, decided by the date — weather the window actually shows, a crowd that comes and goes, small things that go wrong.
  • The regulars are a fixed cast, rolled once for your bar and permanent after that. The same faces in the same coats, arriving on their own schedule, holding their own seats.
  • Mara knows them in proportion to how long they have been coming — and how much she tells you about them depends on what she makes of you.

Talk out loud, if you like.

Hold a key and speak; she hears you. Drop your music into the jukebox in the corner and it plays from that corner — and she will have something to say about your taste.

It is yours.

The whole thing runs locally, the bartender included. There is no account, no server, and nothing leaves your machine. Play with the network unplugged and nothing changes.

No combat, no quests, no score, no way to lose.

Just a stool, a drink, and someone glad you came in. Some evenings that turns out to be plenty.

store_data.about_the_game:
In CaddiShack, you build a deck of genetically enhanced Caddisfly larvae to play into terrariums. Larvae make beads which form bracelets that are sold for cash. Beads synergize in bracelets that are sold every round. You then spend hard earned money on genetic abilities to keep up with the quota!

CaddiShack has 4 key components: The Deck, The Terrarium, The Shop, and The Quota

The Deck

The Deck is a collection of Caddisfly larvae that start as a blank slate. Abilities can be bought in the shop to genetically enhance larvae each round. As you play more and more rounds, you will acquire abilities to synergize for maximum points.

The Terrarium

In the Terrarium, you play 2 hands of 5 larva cards and watch the larvae collect materials. The larvae use these materials to create beads. Once 10 beads have been created, a bracelet is automatically assembled and scored for money.

The Shop

In the Shop, you spend money on genetic abilities to enhance your larva cards. Ability synergies are essential to keeping up with the ever-increasing quota.

You also have to choose 1 of 3 randomized Terrariums for the next round. Choose the optimal Terrarium for your deck to maximize score.

The Quota

A Quota check is performed every 3 rounds. Careful not to spend all of your money in the shop! The Larva Queen will collect the quota, or else you fail. Success only means a higher quota and higher shop prices, so make sure to plan your deck synergies wisely.

store_data.about_the_game:
A Rover's Journey is a 3D, narrative, exploration game, set in the final frontier: space! Play as Roo-ver, Australia's upcoming lunar rover, and help your astronaut companion discover all that the moon has to offer. Traverse difficult terrain, avoid crashing meteors, and uncover technology left from previous expeditions. Find out if the vast lunar landscape can sustain human life!

The Aim of the Game!

Your goal is to help Alex the Astronaut with her lunar duckweed growth program! If she can grow food in Space... humankind may soon visit the moon more often. Help her map out the surrounding area, and gather data from old expedition equipment scattered among the moon's surface. While you're exploring, you'll come across various hazards presented by the terrain, as well as some time challenges that will be sure to test your mettle!

Features Include:

  • Single player

  • Intriguing narrative featuring real-life events

  • Fun physics-based traversal

  • 8+ unique collectables 

  • 3 bonus time challenges

  • 3 distinct areas to explore

  • Accessibility features (volume control / key mapping/ brightness and video settings)

Short story: Bunch of underdog Gobbos gotta destroy countless waves of magical turds in the sewers under a mage city. It's Tower Defense, it's funny, silly, toilet humor, cute retro goblin vibes. 

Long story: Play as Goblinius Rex (G. Rex), the leader of a goblin band of specialists (your towers), Blastlin (wields a deadly magic wand), Boomlin (throws Dwarven bombs), Barflin (yea he barfs out poops to detstroy poops). Life in your goblin swamp village is rough and kinda toxic/sticky so you are so excited (you are, trust me) when the Mage's of nearby Mage City Falala-Kazam hires you Greenos to keep their ancient sewers flowing during their festival of Flippy-Bumpkis!

Embark 20 levels of non-stop silly fun and action as you arrange your towers to defend the Mage's parties, night after night. 

CRAZY (FUNNY) ENEMIES - They're poops, but MORE!

  • Merchant poops: The Merchant Mage's poops are full of gold Shitckles. You actually kinda want to keep this turd alive and click it as much as possible to get those, shiny, stinky coins. Oh, I'm sweatin'!

  • Excrementals: Air, Earth, Fire, Water. These are boss poops that are extra tough and emit and aura that buff surrounding poops. Better take them out before submitting a complaint to the Mage's Elemental Academy janitorial division. 

SPECIAL ACTIVE ABILITIES - Don't just passively watch your towers do all the work, get dirty and do some smushing too!

  • Smusher: You got a big green gobbo hand, use it to smush the poops!

  • Picker: Pick those poops up to feed to your Barflin tower! Once Barflin eats enough you can unleash his cone of toxic barf on your enemies! MUAHAHAA!

  • Builder: Build blockades in the poops paths and repair them to keep them in the sewers as your towers destroy them!

Cute heroes. Big weapons. Endless builds. ABSOLUTE MAYHEM.
