store_data.about_the_game:
About This Game

Deep in the minus 40-degree Antarctic interior, all communication with Chronos BioLab’s top-secret research facility, 'Amundsen-4', has been completely lost.
The final report sent to headquarters states that the entire crew has perished. The cause of this catastrophe? A ridiculous claim of an 'Emperor Penguin attack.'

You are a data archivist hired to clean up the mess.
While the corporation wants a 'plausible cover-up' to support this absurd official report, the truth you are about to face points in an entirely different direction.

You Know Nothing

  • There are no friendly guides or summarized clues.

  • Enter the provided access code and log into the station's database, where only an empty search bar awaits.

  • From now on, you must ask the right questions yourself.

Find and Combine Words from Texts

  • Carefully read through the remaining approval documents, corporate messengers, and time logs left in the system.

  • Spot suspicious words (names, places, objects) and drag & drop them into the search bar.

  • Combine two words to cross-reference and uncover hidden records and on-site audio logs that were meant to be concealed.

A Butterfly Effect Deadlier Than Monsters

This is not a simple creature thriller. It is a chilling black comedy where you observe how human selfishness and petty conflicts snowball within a confined space.

Trivial misunderstandings, greed, evasion of responsibility, and bizarre misjudgments.
You will witness every detail of how the crew's foolish mistakes—made to survive or simply to get a promotion—tangled together to drive the station to irreversible ruin.

A 2-Hour Time Attack and Multiple Endings

By the time you piece together the fragmented timeline, you will stand at a crossroads.
Based on the truth you have gathered during this short but intense 2-hour playthrough, you must make a final decision.

Will you permanently bury the traces of this absurd tragedy beneath the Antarctic ice?
Or will you accept the corporation's deceitful offer and claim a hefty reward?

The choice is yours.

store_data.about_the_game:
Something has awakened in the mountains — and the nightmare is spreading.

Nightmare Unleashed! is a fast-paced voxel FPS where every night throws you into a new fight for survival.

Fight through relentless waves of monsters, complete objectives under pressure, and adapt as the battlefield changes around you. Dash through enemy lines, dodge deadly attacks, grab powerful weapons, and survive long enough to face the horrors waiting at the end of the night.

But you won't always know what's coming next.

A deadly roulette system determines the enemies and events you'll have to face, mixing different monster factions together and forcing you to adapt your strategy from one wave to the next. Villagers, beasts, orcs and other creatures can invade the battlefield — sometimes all at once.

Between waves, survival isn't your only objective. Restore generators, search for key items, defend important locations, complete dangerous tasks and push deeper into the wilderness as the nightmare grows stronger.

And when the horde finally breaks... something much bigger may be waiting for you.

FEATURES

• Fast-paced voxel FPS combat — Keep moving, keep shooting, and fight your way through increasingly dangerous encounters.

• Dynamic monster waves — Different enemy factions can combine to create unpredictable battles.

• The Roulette — Enemy types, events and challenges can change from one encounter to the next.

• Objectives during the chaos — Restore machinery, recover items, defend locations and complete tasks while monsters hunt you down.

• Dash through danger — Evade attacks, escape surrounded positions and break through enemy lines.

• A growing arsenal — Fight back with pistols, shotguns and other powerful weapons.

• Deadly bosses — Survive the hordes long enough and you'll have to face something far worse.

• Solo or 2-player co-op — Experience the nightmare alone or survive alongside a friend through Steam online co-op.

• Voxel nightmare aesthetic — Explore dark forests and hostile environments filled with grotesque voxel creatures.

• English voice acting with text available in English, French, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish, German and Russian.

store_data.about_the_game:
About This Game

This is a relaxed 3D Sokoban puzzle game set among the ruins of ancient cultivators. It stays faithful to the classic rules: study the board, plan your route, and push every crate onto its target. The rules are easy to understand, but every push changes the space available to both the player and the crates. Because crates can be pushed but not pulled, a careless move can block a key passage, trap a crate in a corner, or turn a solvable layout into a deadlock.

Classic Sokoban, Thoughtful Planning

To solve a level, move all crates onto the marked target spaces. Success depends on more than pushing in the correct direction: consider whether there will still be room behind a crate, whether you can reach its other side, which narrow passages need to remain open, which crate should move first, and which positions may become impossible to recover from.

More Than 900 Levels

The game contains more than 900 Sokoban levels. Early stages are compact and approachable, while later stages introduce larger layouts, more crates, tighter passages, and situations that require several moves of advance planning. Some puzzles can be solved during a short break; others reward studying the entire board before making the first push.

Irregularly Shaped Crates

Later puzzles introduce one additional mechanic: irregularly shaped crates. Unlike ordinary single-cell crates, these can occupy multiple grid spaces in different shapes. Their geometry changes how much room is required to move them and how routes must be reserved around them. A passage that works for a normal crate may not work for an irregular one, adding another layer of spatial reasoning while keeping the traditional Sokoban rules intact.

Varied 3D Environments

As you progress, the scenery changes across island ruins, frozen snowfields, forests, bamboo groves, deserts, lava caverns, crystal caves, ancient temples, and other atmospheric environments. The visual themes provide variety while the board remains clear and readable, so the player, crates, walls, paths, and targets are easy to distinguish at a glance.

Play at Your Own Pace

Sokoban rewards thought rather than reaction speed. Take as much time as you need to inspect the board. If a route does not work, you can undo moves or restart the current level at any time and try a different approach.

Complete Buy-to-Play Experience

There are no advertisements, no energy system, and no microtransactions. A single purchase gives you the complete game experience. Play a few puzzles whenever you have time, or settle in for a longer session and progress at your own pace.

Features

  • Classic and easy-to-understand Sokoban gameplay
  • More than 900 levels
  • Full 3D presentation
  • A wide variety of environmental themes
  • Gradually increasing puzzle complexity
  • Irregularly shaped crates as the sole additional mechanic
  • Clear and readable boards
  • Undo and restart functions
  • No advertisements
  • No energy system
  • No microtransactions
  • Complete buy-to-play puzzle experience

store_data.about_the_game:
Master of Arms is a single-player Roguelike strategy game that deeply emphasizes "spatial layout" and "symbol synergy." In this world, weapons are not just arms; they are tactical symbols that you can freely combine. You must utilize limited resources to build your board and carefully select items across ever-changing levels to achieve transcendent scores!

[Core Features]

Build Your Exclusive Board – Space is Power

Break away from the traditional one-way card-playing mechanic! Freely place various functional blocks on the board to construct your tactical terrain. Different positional layouts will directly affect skill triggers between symbols and score multipliers.

Diverse Weapon Symbols, Trigger Massive Combos

From swords and longbows to sturdy shields and hidden weapons, each weapon symbol boasts a unique trigger mechanism. Place complementary symbols adjacent to each other to activate powerful "Synergies" and unleash exponentially growing scoring chains!

Dynamic Shop System – Test Your In-run Decisions

Visit the shop between levels and adapt to dynamic price fluctuations and inflation rules. Will you buy a core weapon at a high price, or reroll the shop for the perfect combo? Every use of gold will determine the direction of your build.

Hardcore Roguelike Level Challenges

Face progressively escalating target scores where luck alone won't guarantee victory. Random shop refreshes, rich symbol bonds, and unpredictable block combinations ensure that every run offers a unique gameplay experience.

[Gameplay Overview]

Purchase & Collect:​ Buy weapon symbols and blocks in the shop.

Build & Place:​ Lay out blocks to form your board and place weapon symbols on optimal nodes.

Chain Trigger:​ Start the turn to trigger individual symbol skills and combined effects with adjacent symbols.

Clear the Level:​ Score beyond the level's target to advance to the next, more challenging stage!

Can you master the art of combining these versatile symbols to build the ultimate high-scoring formation and become the true "Master of Arms"?

store_data.about_the_game:
Build your deck. Make your plays. Reach Worlds.

TOP CUT: Locals to Worlds brings the tactical battles of a head-to-head card game into a single-player roguelike tournament. Choose your starter, discover unexpected card combinations, and take on rivals with a deck that evolves between rounds.

Your road to Worlds starts at a folding table.

EVERY PLAY IS YOURS

Choose what to play, where to place it, and when to attack. Move creatures between your Prep and Plated zones, pick your targets, and hold the right response for your opponent’s next move.

Sacrifice ingredients to summon powerful Meals. Strengthen your board with tools and spices. Spring a hand trap when your rival thinks they have the advantage.

A strong deck matters. How you play it matters just as much.

SMALL CARDS. BIG PLAYS.

Food/animal-themed cards bring their own tricks to the table, and the best plays happen when those tricks work together.

Summon Firecracker Shrimp, take down a defender, then ping a threat in the back row. Move Polar Pot Pie Bear to the front line for a stat boost. Serve Strawberry Sharkcake to refill your hand and keep your options open.

Find the pieces. Build the interaction. Make it count.

BUILD YOUR NEXT WIN

Between matches, open reward packs and choose which cards join your deck. Browse the card counter for a missing combo piece or upgrade a favorite into a stronger, shimmering foil.

Every addition changes your options. Reinforce your strategy or discover a new one worth building around.

THE MATCH ENDS. THE RUN CONTINUES.

Your remaining life carries from round to round. Winning a match is only part of surviving the tournament.

Each tournament floor gives you one bye to spend on healing or a card upgrade. Recover for the next rival, or invest in a stronger deck for the matches ahead.

FIND YOUR PLAYSTYLE

  • Spicy: Seize the initiative with aggressive attacks and direct damage.

  • Hearty: Protect your key units, recover health, and build a board that lasts.

  • Sweet: Draw cards, disrupt opposing threats, and create opportunities through clever sequencing.

One starter deck. A tournament full of decisions. Your shot at the top cut.

Wishlist TOP CUT: Locals to Worlds and start your climb!

store_data.about_the_game:
You're not building a car. You're dropping a stone into a pond—and watching the entire surface erupt.


The year is 2000, in the fictional nation of C-country. You've acquired a failing car manufacturer with three million in capital, one assembly line, a few dozen workers, and zero brand recognition. Over the next thirty years, you'll decide every component under the hood—engine, chassis, seats—set the price, choose the channels, then hold your breath as review scores drop, influencers post takes, forums explode, sales numbers roll in, and rival CEOs take jabs at you in interviews.

Eight Core Modules, Over 300 Real Components


Chassis, powertrain, body, cockpit, safety, energy, electronics, and vehicle calibration—eight assembly modules with 300+ authentic parts spanning 2000's torsion-beam drum brakes to 2030's solid-state batteries and silicon-carbide controllers. Three distinct powertrain routes—combustion, hybrid, electric—each with independent component ecosystems. A V8 won't fit in a compact chassis; air suspension needs electric power steering to function. Compatibility rules prevent nonsensical mashups. Every part swap refreshes nine core performance metrics and five target-demographic match scores in real time. One platform can spawn a volume base trim, a profit-driving luxury trim, and a brand-building flagship.

NPC Consumers With Personalities, Not Spreadsheets


They aren't "+100 sales." Each has age, occupation, family status, salary—and eight hidden preference dimensions you can't see. Some care only about specs, others only about price; some are swayed by a single influencer video, others buy for status. Bargain hunters compare you line-by-line against rivals. Brand loyalists evangelize on forums. Angry owners either file complaints or ruin your reputation in owner groups. You can't see their weights directly—you infer them from behavior and posts. That's the black box.

Seven Layers of Ripples—Media Is the Lifeblood


After launch, feedback isn't a number popup—it's a weeks-long wave: enthusiast magazines publish review scores, portals rush breaking news, KOLs post video takes (for better or worse), forums erupt in arguments, owners post real-world impressions, rivals slash prices in response, national papers write year-end features. Nine media channels unlock progressively across five eras—from 2000's print newspapers and web forums to 2020's short video and livestreams—each with its own voice and personality. Print says "sources report," forums say "this workshop's at it again," short video says "guys, this car slaps." Your company title evolves too: from "that small factory" to "Motors Co., Ltd." to finally being called "the Group."

Five Eras, Three Powertrain Routes, Thirty Years


From the startup era's assembly survival, through brand awakening, domestic-vs-joint-venture warfare, the new-energy transition, to the full-intelligence era—change is gradual, not hard cuts. New media emerges, old media fades, new consumer segments appear, regulations mandate ABS then ESP, new components unlock via R&D. Stick with combustion and perfect it, go all-in on electric and bet the future, or run hybrid in parallel—each path has different challenges and endings.

More Than Building Cars—Running a Company


    [ ]R&D System: Seven parallel tech trees with generational iteration. Tech freshness decays yearly; fall behind and rivals surpass you. More funding accelerates research—but over-investment risks accidents.[ ]Supplier Network: Relationship levels Lv0–Lv3 affect pricing and stability. Both you and competitors can buy out exclusive components to execute supply-chain blockades.[ ]Production: Expand lines, hire and train workers, upgrade equipment—pure numeric constraints, no drag-and-drop minigames, but capacity, yield rate, and worker skill all affect delivery.[ ]Dealerships & Marketing: From dealer agents to 4S stores to direct experience centers; from print ads to short-video campaigns. Channels and marketing determine who sees your cars.[ ]Banking & Credit: Borrow to expand. Credit ratings from AAA to D determine interest rates and limits.[ ]After-Sales & Recalls: Corners cut on quality come back—with interest—in recall campaigns.

Six Starting Factories, Six Stories


From a one-star derelict plant to a five-star industry relic, six acquirable factories each offer different starting lines, worker quality, brand legacies, and difficulty. Hard starts have tight budgets but exclusive tech heritage; easier starts are stable but face fiercer competition. Every playthrough tells a different business story.

Six Endings, Graded S to F


Reach 2030 and be scored across six dimensions: market performance, brand building, R&D output, production scale, company tier, and financial health. You might become a "National Brand Legend" (S), achieve "Steady Operation" (C), or suffer an "Inglorious Exit" (F). Failure gets its own screen. Success gets no fireworks—because the next quarter is already here.

store_data.about_the_game:
Four in a row is the easy part. Earning each square is the game.

Every cell on the board shows a number. To claim it you have to build that number out of the cards in your hand — and there is always more than one way. First to line up four wins: across, down, or along either diagonal.

THE MATH IS THE MOVE

Your hand is five cards, worth 1 to 6. A cell reading 96 does not want a 96 — it wants a 9 and a 6 glued together. A cell reading 30 will take 5 × 6, or 6 × 5, or 2 & 4 + 6. You get up to three cards and six operations:

  • Concatenate — 9 & 6 = 96. The shortcut to the big two-digit targets.

  • Exponent — 4 ^ 2 = 16.

  • Multiply and Divide — division must come out exact. There are no fractions in this kingdom.

  • Add and Subtract — and dipping negative part-way through an expression is perfectly legal.

The board reads strictly left to right — no order of operations, ever. 2 + 3 × 4 is 20 here, not 14. That one rule turns plain arithmetic into a puzzle about sequence: the cards you hold matter less than the order you spend them in.

TWO KINGDOMS, TWO RULESETS

ROYALS 7 — the open game. One to three cards, any operations you like, two-digit targets across a 6×6 grid. Every number on the board is yours to shape.

DECREE — the board dictates the math. Every column flies a banner: + − × ÷ ^. That is the only operation permitted in that column. Targets are single digits, and every move is exactly two cards — never one, never three. You do not choose the operation. You choose two cards and go hunting for the column that will accept them.

And once per match, you may issue an EDICT.

An Edict demolishes an entire column. Everything standing in it is destroyed, every column to its right slides one place left, and a freshly rolled column — new law, new targets — marches in at the far end. Pulling a column out makes its neighbours adjacent, which means the slide can complete a line of four that nobody ever actually played. Those lines count.

Demolish at your own peril: if the shift completes a line for both players at once, the victory goes to the player who did not call the Edict.

THE DECK NEVER RUNS OUT

Forty-eight cards, eight copies each of 1 through 6. Spend them and they leave your hand at once, but replacements only arrive at the start of your next turn — so a three-card play leaves you thin for a round. That is the real cost of a clever move.

Nothing is ever destroyed, though. When the last card leaves the deck, the discard pile is shuffled and becomes the deck again. You can always draw. You just cannot always draw well.

WAYS TO PLAY

  • Same Device — two players, one screen, taking turns.

  • Vs Computer — face the court's strategist at three strengths.

  • Online — host a match or join a friend's across the network.

  • The Proving Grounds — eight short trials, one move each, teaching the ways of both kingdoms. Replay any of them freely.

CHOOSE YOUR BATTLEFIELD

  • Standard — the hand-tuned layout, identical every game. Each number appears exactly twice, at opposite ends of the grid, so no corner favors either player.

  • Mirrored — a fresh board every match under the same fairness rules: every number twice, the grid symmetric about its centre.

  • Random — every cell drawn on its own. Common numbers land often, awkward ones rarely. No symmetry, no promises.

Every printed number is reachable with the deck. There are no dead cells.

THE SUMS ARE NOT THE TEST

Select your cards and every cell you can currently claim lights up. Stuck? All results lists every number your hand can reach and flags the ones sitting on an open cell right now — click a row and the operations drop straight onto the play line.

The game will happily do the arithmetic. It will not tell you which square to take.

AT A GLANCE

  • Two complete rulesets — Royals 7 and Decree — each with its own board, its own maths, and its own tutorial trials

  • Local two-player, three AI strengths, and online play against a friend

  • Three board generators, from a hand-balanced fixed layout to a weighted random draw

  • Eight one-move challenges in the Proving Grounds

  • Six operations including concatenation and exponents, with strict left-to-right evaluation

  • A 48-card cycle that recirculates forever — no dead hands, no unwinnable draws

  • Fullscreen, reduced-motion, and brisk-animation options

store_data.about_the_game:
⏹︎ Summer Homework!?

As summer vacation is almost over, schoolgirl Rina still has one final assignment left: part-time job experience.

Not knowing where to look, she spots a delivery job ad that says “No age limit, flexible hours!”

So Rina decides to start her delivery work…!

⏹︎ Check Your Gear

Before heading out, equip all kinds of helpful items to make your deliveries go smoother than ever.

⏹︎ Dangerous Enemies on the Route!

Along the way you’ll pass through quiet, empty areas where enemies are waiting.

Dodge these enemies and get the order safely to the customer!

When a enemy grabs you, it’s time for a desperate escape struggle!

Press at the perfect moment to shove them away with all your strength!

store_data.about_the_game:
Command the Board. Cast the Cards.

Century of Conquest is a single-player turn-based tactics game where you are both commander and mage. On the board, your troop stacks clash in initiative order; above it, elemental spell cards let you rewrite the battle at any moment. Pick a hero, march across a perilous campaign map, recruit an army, hunt for relics — and take the fight to the overlord's gate.

Initiative-Driven Hex Tactics

  • One hex, one army — stack size is power: a single dragon can hold a line, a hundred skeletons can drown a champion

  • Initiative decides who moves first; morale grants extra actions. Counterattacks, splash damage, knockback, piercing and multi-strikes give every unit its own rhythm

  • Deploy freely before each battle — your formation is remembered. Terrain, fortifications and positioning are weapons too

Four Schools of Elemental Magic

  • Energy builds up as the battle rages, drawing spell cards in real time — 75 spells across fire, water, air, earth and neutral magic

  • Spells scale with your hero's mastery: the same card lights a torch for a novice and burns a city for a master

  • Summon reinforcements, raise the dead, conjure mirror images, enchant your troops — the deck is full of comebacks

Heroes and Expeditions

  • 20+ heroes and 20 hero skills — every level-up is a pick-one-of-two dilemma, and 8 skill slots are never enough

  • 30+ relics scattered across the journey, feeding offense, magic or greed builds

  • A three-layer node map: recruitment, supplies, treasure vaults, garrisons and bosses — seeded runs, autosaves

Sieges and Wilderness

  • Siege battles: breach walls, burn gates, and survive tower ballistae — attack and defense play completely differently

  • Six weather states and a day-night cycle shape every fight — thunderstorms suppress archers, moonlit nights awaken the beasts

  • 59 recruitable units across four races, each with signature passives: flight, undead resilience, rebirth from ashes, moonlight frenzy and more

Collect Everything

Creature and spell codices record everything you have encountered. Every run is a new army composition, a new school of magic, a new hero build worth trying.

store_data.about_the_game:
Forty-Eight Days Behind the Fence


For five weeks each year, Han Do-jin disappears into the Chunmyeong valley to secure the nation's college entrance exam. He counts every sheet, seals every box, and helps keep the test honest by keeping forty-one professionals locked inside a remote training resort.

This year, the Institute orders the writers to create an exam no machine can pass. Then an unwritten question appears in a cram school's mock paper. The scheduled thirty-five-day lockdown becomes forty-eight days of audits, interviews, fatigue, and mounting institutional pressure.

Do-jin cannot call the seventeen-year-old niece waiting at home. He cannot leave the resort. And he cannot avoid three women who pull him toward three different futures.

Choose a Relationship




Bae Yeo-reum — The Prep List

The resort's site manager is local to the valley, practical, playful, and unimpressed by Institute authority. She keeps an aging facility running with a wipe-board, inherited infrastructure, and sheer nerve. Helping her may cost more than either of you expects.



Ahn Mi-ran — The Interview Chair

An Assessment Integrity investigator arrives with a case number and a calm, literal method. She tells Do-jin exactly what she will do, then waits until the truth surfaces. Every interview can change the inquiry—and the relationship forming across the table.



Noh Seon-a — The Weather Radio

A brilliant senior item writer and Do-jin's estranged wife, Seon-a must perform flawless public professionalism while their history remains unresolved. Inside the fence, they must decide whether separation was the end or only an interruption.

Features


  • Choose from three complete romance routes with distinct conflicts and endings.
  • Navigate a sealed institutional setting built around surrendered phones, monitored mail, logged calls, security procedures, and a fixed release hour.
  • Investigate the leaked exam question while managing Do-jin's duties as head of paper security.
  • Make relationship choices that determine who Do-jin leaves the valley with.
  • Each romance route includes three explicit adult scenes, for nine adult scenes total.

store_data.about_the_game:
You wake up in a mechanical body, with memories of being human. The robots in this facility don't believe you. To find out what happened, you'll have to find a way out.

ROBOT DRAFT: LAST HUMAN is a single-player, first-person sci-fi adventure. Explore the facility, work out how its machinery operates, and deal with the robots standing in your way. Look around before you move on: something in the room might help.

Puzzles, machinery, and a few things to throw

Move objects, operate mechanisms, and open a route to the next room. When a robot gets in the way, take it on with melee or ranged weapons—or pick up a nearby barrel and throw it.


Records and conversations offer clues to your past. The choices you make along the way lead the story toward different endings.

Make an escape room of your own

The full game includes a level editor. Connect rooms, place props, and decide which doors hide an enemy encounter. Jump in to try it yourself, then adjust a puzzle that doesn't quite work or a fight that's too difficult.


Export your level as a file and send it to a friend, or import a level made by another player. Sharing currently uses level files; Steam Workshop is not supported.

English and Simplified Chinese interface and subtitles. Keyboard and mouse controls.

store_data.about_the_game:
Write real code in a Python-like language to control one machine that copies itself. Then watch a thousand copies of your program eat a world. A single-player programming incremental game about self-replicating machines.

You are handed one machine on a dead rock and a text editor. The machine can move, dig, sense the ground under it and read the colony's energy. Around lesson four it learns to do the one thing that changes everything: build a copy of itself. The copy runs your code. From the top. Exactly as written.

ONE MACHINE BUILDS ONE MACHINE


That is the entire game. Nothing else scales. There are no stat upgrades, no multipliers, no currency to spend on being stronger. Every unit of progress is a new function in your vocabulary - seventeen of them, from move() through sense() and spawn(). Fifteen arrive across the first ten lessons. The last two, send() and recv() for machine-to-machine messaging, open at lesson eleven. Your code is the only thing that scales.

CODE THAT WORKS FOR FOUR MACHINES FAILS AT FOUR HUNDRED


Not because of an artificial difficulty gate. Because a hundred machines converge on the same ore vein and starve. Because the swarm's own bodies block the only corridor. Because one event wakes every machine on the same tick. Because each machine gets a fixed instruction budget per tick, and naive code burns it and stalls where you can watch it happen.

Growth is the reward and the pressure at the same time. The machine count is the difficulty curve, so the late game never plays itself.

FIFTY LEVELS, AND THE HARD ONES TAKE THINGS AWAY


Eleven guided lessons introduce one idea each and never hand you a blank buffer. Thirty-nine scenarios across four tiers escalate from "one machine, five lines" to a radius-sixty world where the best program we know of puts four hundred machines on the map inside a hundred ticks. The pro tier is built by subtraction: no sensors, no price readout, no position, no identity. Ten levels switch an instrument off and tell you in-fiction why your sensor array is slag.

Then there is a sandbox with about thirty dials - world radius, ore density and hardness, radiation, volatile ore, turrets, holes, machine lifespan, upkeep, the instruction budget, and the API calls you can individually disable - and no goals at all.

THE ERRORS ARE THE TUTORIAL


The errors you will actually hit have a plain-English translation that points at the line and names the concept: "After a line ending in :, the next line must be indented 4 spaces - that's how the machine knows it belongs inside." The full API reference is one keystroke away, searchable, with a worked example on every call, and it tells you which calls are locked and which the level has taken away from you before you deploy. A Field Guide names every symbol on screen.

WHAT IT DOESN'T HAVE


No microtransactions. No PvP, no matchmaking, no ranked queue. No random numbers the game keeps to itself - the simulation is deterministic to the tick, so the same seed and the same program always produce the same run, right down to the machine that dies.

[hr][/hr]

Programming is done in a small language similar to Python. The first lessons introduce every concept you need, one at a time, and you edit working code rather than filling an empty file.

It will not hold your hand once the concepts are in. Figuring out how to actually solve a level is the game, and that can be genuinely hard if you have never programmed before.

And if you already write code for a living: the first ten lessons will take you under an hour, and then the interesting problems start, because they are the ones you have already met at work.

store_data.about_the_game:
We March as One is an incremental-style auto battler about building a massive army of shapes.

Paint Your Army

Paint your troops directly onto the battlefield, positioning them to counter the enemy force. Experiment with formations before sending your army into battle against increasingly large enemy hordes.

Expand Your Army

Earn gold from defeated enemies, whether you win or lose the battle. Recruit more troops, unlock new unit types, and return with a stronger army. Fallen troops return for the next battle, so you keep the army you’ve built.

Upgrade Your Army

Upgrade your troops through a branching skill tree, improving their stats and unlocking powerful new effects.

Watch Massive Battles Unfold

Watch formations collide, charges break through the ranks, and artillery tear into enemy hordes. Battles grow to tens of thousands of units, with every soldier and projectile individually simulated. Isometric, top-down, or fly-through modes give you multiple ways to view the action.

Sandbox Mode

Experiment with unusual army compositions and enormous matchups across different battlefield layouts. Build both sides and see what happens when they collide.

store_data.about_the_game:
Wishlist today if you want to become the master katana swordsmith!

Begin as an unknown swordsmith and forge your legacy one blade at a time. Craft, customize, display, and sell unique katana in an approachable first-person experience inspired by Japanese swordsmithing as you fulfill contracts and earn renown.

About This Game

Katanakaji is an approachable first-person crafting game about the journey from an unknown artisan to a renowned Japanese swordsmith.

Within the warmth of your forge, every new piece of tamahagane is an opportunity to prove your skill. Accept commissions, create blades that meet the needs of your clients, and build a reputation through the quality of your work. As your name becomes known, more prestigious contracts and greater challenges await.

Guide each katana through a hands-on sequence inspired by traditional Japanese swordsmithing. Manage the forge, hammer heated steel into shape, select a hamon style, apply clay, quench the blade, polish its surface, and complete it with your choice of decorative fittings.

The experience captures the atmosphere and satisfaction of the craft through accessible timing, movement, and decision-based minigames. Katanakaji is not intended to be a hardcore metallurgical simulation. Your performance still matters: every stage contributes to the finished sword’s quality, appearance, identity, and value, while serious mistakes can damage or even destroy a blade.

store_data.about_the_game:
See the land of the free from a whole new angle — from the sky.

Get in the pilot seat and explore the United States from coast to coast. Skim the canyon floor in the Grand Canyon, pull off daring aerobatics over Los Angeles, or simply cruise along and watch the country unfold beneath your wings. The sky is yours.

Put your skills to the test. Challenges are waiting all across the country — and those stars won't earn themselves. Master each run, level up, and unlock new aircraft and new places to fly, from red-rock country and sprawling cities to wide-open plains. There's a whole lot of America out there.

Built from the real world. United Skies of America uses real-world elevation data and satellite imagery to recreate the landscape in stunning detail, from every ridgeline and river bend to every canyon wall. Our signature art style transforms it into something you've never quite seen before — a country you know, seen in a whole new light.

And the best part? It all runs offline.

Just you, your plane, and the whole country. A game like they used to make ’em.

FEATURES

  • Explore the entire United States, from the Pacific coast to the Atlantic

  • Heart-pounding challenges, including low passes, canyon slaloms, and more

  • Level up to unlock new aircraft and challenges

  • Real-world elevation data and satellite imagery

  • A distinctive art style that turns every flight into a postcard

  • 100% offline — no internet required

store_data.about_the_game:
Harvest Crops Like You’re Mowing Grass

Most farmers start by sowing seeds. Not you—the fields are already ripe, and all that’s left is to reap.

Unfortunately, some uninvited monsters have taken over the farm. Weave through the hordes while your auto-firing weapons fight enemies and harvest crops at the same time. Homing shots, spread fire, piercing attacks, explosions, poison, ice, lightning... Clear the path and take the nearby crops with them.

Crops Have Skills, Too

Dozens of crops grow on the farm, each with a unique ability.

Some explode when harvested. Some freeze enemies, summon helpers, or continue harvesting nearby crops. Find the right combination, and taking down a single crop can set off half the field.

The Farm Is Your Build

After each round, shop for weapons, seeds, magic scrolls, animals, facilities, and more.

Buying seeds changes how often each crop appears. Fill the field with chili peppers, or save space for the crops your build depends on—the choice is yours. Harvested plots regrow according to your current seed setup, gradually reshaping the farm after every visit to the shop.

You can also take cultivation orders, gather the requested ingredients, and upgrade specific crops. Complete enough orders and an ordinary crop can grow into a super crop that occupies a huge patch of land—more valuable, with an even wilder ability.

No slow watering. No waiting until autumn.

The fields are ripe. Grab your gear and let the harvest frenzy begin.

movies.name: Strange Absurdity: DOG STAR - Official Trailer

store_data.about_the_game:
Deep in a wood near Hollow Creek, Washington, in the year 1977.

A rendezvous first set in motion decades ago is finally coming to its apex.

You are responsible for ensuring all goes according to plan. You are staying in a tower equipped with the necessary instruments to receive, decode, and transmit vital signals expected to reach the area as the Arrival draws near.

The tower is your home. It provides all that you need; a stove to warm yourself and cook supper, a place to brew a hot cup of coffee to help you through the night, and even means to defend yourself against those unfortunate things which do not take kindly to the presence of life in our realm.

  • The provided RDF detector is a special tool which allows you to track most entities that rise deep in the black of the surrounding forest.

  • Make use of the spirit lamps placed along the tower catwalk to burn away the things before they can reach your domain.

  • Some things don't mind the light - they instead respond to the song of your vesper horn, but the melody that wards them off changes by night. Ensure you have the correct notes in mind before sounding off the horn.

  • Some things do not mind any of these methods. For these, you will have to rely on the strength of the door and hatch bolts, and pouches of salt which you may line the window sills and entry points with. Keep an eye on the bolts. They have a tendency to recuse themselves. 

The tower has been specifically built around where the veil separating us from the other side has ripped open. Navigate the catwalk all the way around to reach the Still. Go back - or go around once more - to return home. The Still and home alike contain dangers only detectable in their respective side, but letting things from either place get too close will allow them to reach across the veil. Keep your eyes and ears keen at all times.

You have a dog, as provided by the Company. Take care of it, and it will take care of you. Its heightened senses allow awareness of coming things from either realm - and even those invisible to your RDF detector - alerting you to incoming sieges in advance. But a neglected friend does not stay a friend.

Stay on top of your duties and transmit decoded signals back to the Company, and you will be provided with credits to purchase necessary requisitions. The Company will deliver these to the supply cache in the nearby shed the following night; ensure you are planning for needed supplies in advance.

Falling behind on your work will result in an unacceptable outcome for the Company, and more than likely, a permanent end for yourself.

Good luck.

Strange Absurdity: DOG STAR is a follow-up to the niche adventure game Strange Absurdity: ANCIENTS' ASYLUM.

store_data.about_the_game:
Take control of the mortal world as you compete against other warring civilizations in Irkalla — a turn-based 4X strategy game centered on conquest, faith, and governance.

Lead your armies, forge alliances, and decide whether your empire will rule by the sword, through treaties, or by faith in the Truth that will change the very world itself.

Lead one of four races, split into eight facitons:

Each faction has been inspired by clear real world civilisation when it comes to aesthethic, and come with unique roster of units, starting spell schools and technologies.

  • Recruit and command heroes: your heroes level up, learn skills, lead your armies, and explore the world to uncover its secrets.

  • Journey through five historical eras: the Ancient, Classical, Middle, High, and Mythical eras — scientific discoveries allow you to build and upgrade new structures and units, and unlock new paths to victory.

  • Devote yourself to magic and the discovery of forgotten knowledge; choose your Truth and summon its wonders through faith, or focus on technological superiority. Or perhaps you’ll combine all three?

Three ways for victory:

  • Conquest is not the only path to victory. Eliminate all rivals to become the undisputed ruler of Irkalla, or control all lands alongside your allies to achieve a alliance victory. Or choose and spread one of the Seven Truths — competing philosophies regarding the nature of reality itself, until it defines the world.

  • An AI that remembers: Political decisions are driven not only by calculation but also by memory. Each AI leader approaches them differently. Gifts, alliances, betrayals, and wars leave a lasting mark that will be more significant and endure longer in the memory of some leaders than in others.

Gameplay:

  • Provinces: The world is divided into provinces, and every conquered territory must be maintained, managed, and defended against enemies.

  • Automatic Battles: Battles are fast-paced and tactical, and their outcome is determined by strategy and proper preparation — not by quick reflexes. Watch animated battle replays influenced by unit traits, composition, and the heroes commanding the battle.

  • Script your heroes to cast a specific spells in battles, or summon devasting spells on world map.

  • Procedurally Generated Maps: Choose from four map types and rediscover the world as you explore provinces, fight for legendary locations, and face off against new enemies.

Rule as an undead, immortal Sorcerer-King, lead as a commander with a dragon’s temperament, or take on any other role you choose — all that matters is victory.

store_data.about_the_game:
Your grandfather's new auto-sorting spell backfired.

Every potion in the apothecary tipped off its shelf. Every finished potion unravelled back into raw essence, and the loose colors pooled together in one enormous pile in the middle of the lab.

He chuckled. "Ah, it does that sometimes." Then he pulled on his coat for the annual Alchemists Gathering and asked you to mind the place while he is away.

He'll be gone about a month. There is no rush at all.

Two puzzles

Every potion needs two things done to it.

Decant. Pour the scrambled liquids from bottle to bottle until each one holds a single pure color. If you have ever played a water-sort puzzle, your hands already know this part.

Shelve. Carry the finished potion across the lab to the shelf it belongs on. Color gets you to the right wall. The sigil on its label picks the exact shelf.

You can only levitate a few bottles at a time, so the two puzzles compete for the same hands. Pour greedily and you have nothing free to carry with. Carry too much and you have nothing free to pour into. Deciding what to hold is the game.

One laboratory. 4,160 potions.

A gothic stone rotunda, two floors, tall arched windows and warm afternoon light. 52 shelved sections across thirteen families of potion.

Every one of the 4,160 potions is in that pile from the moment you start. Nothing respawns, nothing refills, nothing quietly re-stirs itself behind your back. The mess only ever gets smaller.

The room is the progress bar. The floor clears. The shelves fill and light up. A dark, dusty laboratory slowly becomes a glowing apothecary.

Relaxing is the whole point

No timers. No pressure. No penalties. No fail state. There is nothing here you can lose.

Warm window light, a quiet score, and the sound of glass and liquid. Put a potion on the wrong shelf and nothing scolds you. No buzzer, no shake, nothing taken away. Set a bottle down mid-pour, walk off, and come back next week to exactly where you left it.

Skills make the work easier. They never make it disappear.

Sorting earns XP, XP earns levels, and every level buys a skill point. There are 47 of them, across a board of 24 nodes.

A wider hand. A longer reach. Deeper buffers to work into, and sight that pulls a workable set out of the pile.

What none of them do is play for you. Nothing pours, carries or shelves on your behalf, and nothing sits on a cooldown. You get better tools and a bigger workspace. The satisfying part stays yours.

Three numbers, counted all the way down

52 sections. 364 shelf rows. 4,160 potions.

The game keeps all three counters and you can switch them on or off. No hidden progress and no rounding. Every potion you finish and shelve moves a number you can watch.

The lab is done when the pile is gone and all 52 cabinets are full. A finite game with a real ending, not a loop that farms you.

Features

  • Two interlocking puzzles: water-sort decanting and tidy-up shelving

  • 4,160 potions across 52 sections and 364 shelf rows, in one continuous laboratory of 2 floors

store_data.detailed_description:
Your grandfather's new auto-sorting spell backfired.

Every potion in the apothecary tipped off its shelf. Every finished potion unravelled back into raw essence, and the loose colors pooled together in one enormous pile in the middle of the lab.

He chuckled. "Ah, it does that sometimes." Then he pulled on his coat for the annual Alchemists Gathering and asked you to mind the place while he is away.

He'll be gone about a month. There is no rush at all.

Two puzzles

Every potion needs two things done to it.

Decant. Pour the scrambled liquids from bottle to bottle until each one holds a single pure color. If you have ever played a water-sort puzzle, your hands already know this part.

Shelve. Carry the finished potion across the lab to the shelf it belongs on. Color gets you to the right wall. The sigil on its label picks the exact shelf.

You can only levitate a few bottles at a time, so the two puzzles compete for the same hands. Pour greedily and you have nothing free to carry with. Carry too much and you have nothing free to pour into. Deciding what to hold is the game.

One laboratory. 4,160 potions.

A gothic stone rotunda, two floors, tall arched windows and warm afternoon light. 52 shelved sections across thirteen families of potion.

Every one of the 4,160 potions is in that pile from the moment you start. Nothing respawns, nothing refills, nothing quietly re-stirs itself behind your back. The mess only ever gets smaller.

The room is the progress bar. The floor clears. The shelves fill and light up. A dark, dusty laboratory slowly becomes a glowing apothecary.

Relaxing is the whole point

No timers. No pressure. No penalties. No fail state. There is nothing here you can lose.

Warm window light, a quiet score, and the sound of glass and liquid. Put a potion on the wrong shelf and nothing scolds you. No buzzer, no shake, nothing taken away. Set a bottle down mid-pour, walk off, and come back next week to exactly where you left it.

Skills make the work easier. They never make it disappear.

Sorting earns XP, XP earns levels, and every level buys a skill point. There are 47 of them, across a board of 24 nodes.

A wider hand. A longer reach. Deeper buffers to work into, and sight that pulls a workable set out of the pile.

What none of them do is play for you. Nothing pours, carries or shelves on your behalf, and nothing sits on a cooldown. You get better tools and a bigger workspace. The satisfying part stays yours.

Three numbers, counted all the way down

52 sections. 364 shelf rows. 4,160 potions.

The game keeps all three counters and you can switch them on or off. No hidden progress and no rounding. Every potion you finish and shelve moves a number you can watch.

The lab is done when the pile is gone and all 52 cabinets are full. A finite game with a real ending, not a loop that farms you.

store_data.about_the_game:
🀄 About the Game

UnlimitedMahjong‌ is a single-player light roguelike mahjong game. Here, you are no longer bound by the rigid rules of traditional mahjong — those legendary, once-in-a-lifetime mega hands will come true one by one under your fingertips.

🎮 Core Gameplay

  • ‌Tap to Build Hands‌: Each round presents you with a scattered tile pool. Precisely tap to collect tiles and freely combine them into rare, high-scoring patterns

  • ‌Dream Big Hands Come True‌: Thirteen Orphans, All Honors, Big Three Dragons… those top-tier hands that seem impossible in real life? Here, as long as you're clever and bold enough to make tough calls, you can pull them off yourself

  • ‌Level by Level Escalation‌: Every stage sets a higher target score than the last. An easy win today doesn't guarantee tomorrow — stay sharp and strategize every step of the way

🔄 Strategic Choices

  • ‌Boost Multipliers‌: Actively raise your hand multiplier to double — or more — the scoring potential of every combo

  • ‌Expand Tile Pool‌: Unlock more tiles to pick from, giving you a wider canvas to craft your dream hand

  • ‌Discard Boldly‌: When the draw isn't cooperating, don't hesitate — dump the dead tiles and reshuffle to make room for something bigger

✨ Key Features

  • ‌Relaxing Roguelike Loop‌: Start fresh after every round, accumulate experience, and figure out the best strategy through repeated runs — losing never feels punishing

  • ‌Wits Over Luck‌: Sure, a dash of luck helps, but what truly decides the outcome is your judgment — when to go for the big hand, when to play it safe, when to cut your losses and discard

  • ‌That "I Can't Believe I Pulled It Off" Rush‌: The moment you tap the final tile and watch the score explode across the screen — that pure, satisfying of "I actually made it" — is the heart of this game

store_data.about_the_game:
Build your city, one tile at a time


TileCity is a city-building simulation where every road, zone, and service matters. Start with open land, lay out your streets, zone districts, and guide your city as it grows from a small town into a bustling metropolis.

Plan, zone, and expand


Paint residential, commercial, and industrial zones and watch buildings develop along your roads. Shape the land with terrain tools, connect districts with roads and footpaths, and expand your map as your budget allows. Name districts, place parks, and add landmarks that make your city feel unique.

Keep the city running


Your citizens need more than buildings — they need working infrastructure.

  • Generate power with wind turbines, solar panels, and coal plants

  • Build water pumps, pipes, sewage systems, and treatment stations

  • Provide healthcare, education, police, fire protection, and deathcare

  • Manage garbage collection, noise pollution, and citizen happiness

Balance service funding, set tax rates, take loans when needed, and keep your weekly budget in the green.

A living economy


TileCity goes beyond basic zoning. Farms produce wheat, oil fields and ore deposits fuel industry, and factories and shops form supply chains that feed your commercial districts. Track production, imports, exports, and demand as your city evolves.

Move people around


Reduce traffic and connect your city with public transport:

  • Bus lines with terminals and stops

  • Ferry routes across water

  • Train networks for regional travel

  • Airports for city-wide connectivity

Plan routes, manage capacity, and help citizens get where they need to go.

Two ways to play


Normal Mode — Build within your budget, respond to demand, and grow your city step by step.

Sandbox Mode — Experiment freely with fewer financial limits and focus on creativity.

Made for builders


  • Detailed city stats: population, jobs, happiness, demand, and income

  • Save and load with manual and auto-save slots

  • English and Thai language support

  • Guided tutorial quests to help you get started

Whether you want a relaxing sandbox or a challenging city management sim, TileCity gives you the tools to build the city you imagine.

store_data.about_the_game:
You buy the army. You do not fight it.

Each round the shelf offers three fighters and three weapons. You buy what the levy covers, hang a weapon on a body, order six slots, and send them. The siege is resolved before you see it and then played back: sixty seconds, sudden death at thirty, at one, two or three times speed. There is no skip, and nothing to press once it starts.

Fifteen wins takes a campaign, and a loss takes none of them back

A loss costs wall instead. Your castle starts at 5,000 and carries its damage from round to round, won or lost, while the enemy's is rebuilt to full every time. Repair buys 500 back for 120 gold, which is two fighters you will now not muster. No round can take more than a quarter of your maximum, and across 6,215 measured rounds, 95.2 per cent of losses took exactly that.

An Aspect is not a perk

Three of the ten are offered at the start, less what your last two finished runs spent. An Aspect decides what your army does with the openings it already has: Pyre sets your blows alight, Void executes the wounded, Aegis pays back what it blocks. Feed it and it tiers twice, and at the top you may hire its champion, one to a run, who arrives with an ultimate no shop sells. Hold two Aspects, each banking a quarter of the experience, and the pair always fuses: fifteen of the forty-five pairings have a name of their own, written twice, so which you took first matters.

Three of a kind, and what falls out of it

Four characters ever reach the shelf, knight, ranger, enchanter and mechanic, with eight weapons to start and four more forged by challenges. Grades are rolled when the shelf stocks, so the card shows the true price before you commit. Three copies at one grade fold into the next, five grades deep to Mythic, and a weapon that folds drops a chest of two charms out of fifty as well. Charms come through no other door. A reroll costs 20, and 20 more each time you do it again that round.

Two holes in your own wall

The masons cut up to two mountings, 30 gold then 60, and the gun to fill one costs 50 to 60 more: a Wall Cannon, a Keeper's Brazier, a Lavastorm Obelisk. Your Aspect's power runs through their fire as it runs through a sword. They reach two thirds of the field, so soldiers still decide a siege, and on the harder rungs the enemy arms its wall too.

The caravan deals in rule-breakers

Every second round, or every round under Tempest, the caravan parks one of thirty-six relics on the shelf at 80 gold, yours for the rest of that run. The Hungry Gate eats the first two attackers to reach it. The Cracked Bell refuses, once, to let the keep fall. The Turncoat Shroud turns every sixth corpse to your side, where it fell.

The enemy learns nothing, and does not need to

One rival Aspect comes out of the run's seed and holds every round but each third, when a challenger visits instead. It keeps no economy and adapts to nothing; its strength is the round number. store_data.detailed_description:
You buy the army. You do not fight it.

Each round the shelf offers three fighters and three weapons. You buy what the levy covers, hang a weapon on a body, order six slots, and send them. The siege is resolved before you see it and then played back: sixty seconds, sudden death at thirty, at one, two or three times speed. There is no skip, and nothing to press once it starts.

Fifteen wins takes a campaign, and a loss takes none of them back

A loss costs wall instead. Your castle starts at 5,000 and carries its damage from round to round, won or lost, while the enemy's is rebuilt to full every time. Repair buys 500 back for 120 gold, which is two fighters you will now not muster. No round can take more than a quarter of your maximum, and across 6,215 measured rounds, 95.2 per cent of losses took exactly that.

An Aspect is not a perk

Three of the ten are offered at the start, less what your last two finished runs spent. An Aspect decides what your army does with the openings it already has: Pyre sets your blows alight, Void executes the wounded, Aegis pays back what it blocks. Feed it and it tiers twice, and at the top you may hire its champion, one to a run, who arrives with an ultimate no shop sells. Hold two Aspects, each banking a quarter of the experience, and the pair always fuses: fifteen of the forty-five pairings have a name of their own, written twice, so which you took first matters.

Three of a kind, and what falls out of it

Four characters ever reach the shelf, knight, ranger, enchanter and mechanic, with eight weapons to start and four more forged by challenges. Grades are rolled when the shelf stocks, so the card shows the true price before you commit. Three copies at one grade fold into the next, five grades deep to Mythic, and a weapon that folds drops a chest of two charms out of fifty as well. Charms come through no other door. A reroll costs 20, and 20 more each time you do it again that round.

The masons cut up to two mountings, 30 gold then 60, and the gun to fill one costs 50 to 60 more: a Wall Cannon, a Keeper's Brazier, a Lavastorm Obelisk. Your Aspect's power runs through their fire as it runs through a sword. They reach two thirds of the field, so soldiers still decide a siege, and on the harder rungs the enemy arms its wall too.

You’ll control Minya as she takes on the graduation exam at Sky Magic Academy, aiming to pass the exam and graduate. If you mow down countless enemies and defeat the final boss, Minya will graduate successfully.

Features of Minya in the Sky

  • The main character, Minya, is cute.

  • This is a third-person game where you use weapons, magic, and items to defeat monsters.

  • You can switch weapons while running.

  • You can check Minya’s stats in the status window.

  • By defeating monsters, Minya gains experience points and levels up.

  • Some spells feature auto-aim. In these cases, the spell locks onto the nearest enemy, so simply pressing a key or pulling the joypad trigger will fire the spell at the locked-on monster.

  • Minya can perform various actions, such as sitting on the ground, double-jumping, and running around.

  • Treasure chests contain items. Collect plenty of items to strengthen Minya.

  • There are locked doors and locked treasure chests.

  • Monsters may be lurking inside treasure chests.

  • You can purchase items at the Item Shop.

  • This game focuses primarily on hack-and-slash action and treasure hunting.

Control the adorable Minya and guide her safely to graduation!

store_data.about_the_game:
Push Through the Darkness and Complete Your Mission.

The facility is almost completely dark, but you still have missions to complete. With only a single light to guide you, you’ll have to make your way through the darkness and find what you need. But you’re not alone. Something is lurking in the dark, waiting to get in your way.

Swing, Throw, and Sabotage!

Don’t let the other team finish their missions first. They’re your competition. Pick up the various items scattered throughout the facility and use them against your opponents. Stun them, trap them, and blow them up!

People Aren’t the Only Threat

For some reason, things that aren’t human are wandering around the facility. Some may help you, and some may put you in danger. Use them, attack them, push them toward your enemies, or run away from them. The choice is yours.

Something Feels... Strange

Every time you enter the facility, strange effects will make your mission even harder. But these effects apply to everyone equally. Work together with your team and find a way to overcome them.

Online Multiplayer for Up to 9 Players

Team up with your friends—or strangers—or become enemies and compete against each other in online multiplayer. Recommended for 3–6 players, but supports up to 9 players.

store_data.about_the_game:
About This Game

The tide is out. Time to head for the shore.

After leaving an exhausting job behind, you return to the coast you know by heart and begin again with a newly bought shovel. Each low tide lasts only a few minutes: watch for sand mounds, air holes, muddy patches, and gaps between rocks. Dig open a hiding place, then grab its occupant before it escapes.

Bring home as much as you can before the water returns


The beach, tidal flats, and rocky shore each have their own terrain and wildlife. Clams, razor clams, fiddler crabs, mudskippers, starfish, small octopuses, and more hide along the coast in different ways. Your stamina is limited, and you decide when to keep searching and when to call it a day early.

Turn every catch into confidence for the next trip


Every catch is valued by species, weight, and special traits. Spend shell coins on a branching upgrade path to improve stamina, shovel efficiency, luck, and the value of your haul. New prerequisites reveal new branches, so you can shape your progress around the way you like to play.

Keep the discoveries that are worth more than money


Your catalog records each catch's value, usual size, largest record, scientific notes, and special traits. Drift bottles contain letters from the sea and permanently reduce a small part of upgrade costs. Natural treasures can be identified and sold, or placed in limited display slots to grant bonuses for later low tides.

  • Dig and pick up catches directly with the mouse
  • Three coastal maps with distinct ecosystems and visual styles
  • Coastal creatures with weight-based size and special variants
  • A branching upgrade path that unfolds as you progress
  • A catalog, size records, drift-bottle letters, and natural-treasure displays
  • Short low-tide runs of about three minutes, with the option to finish early
  • Local autosave

store_data.about_the_game:
LUCK IT is the classic Star Battle puzzle — the same kind you know from LinkedIn's daily Queens. Stars become four-leaf clovers; the rules are identical.

How to play

The board is divided into irregular colored regions. Plant clovers so that all four of these are true:

One clover in every row

One clover in every column

One clover in every colored region

No two clovers may touch — not side by side, not even corner to corner

Right-click an empty square to mark it with an X, so you can keep track of the positions you have ruled out.

Every board has exactly one solution, and every solution can be reached by pure deduction. You will never have to guess.

Modes

Campaign — 500 levels

Boards grow from 5×5 to 9×9, and the reasoning grows with them: from a single square forced into place, to region confinement, to set exclusion. Clear a level for bronze, finish with half the clock left for silver, and 70% left for gold.

Endless

A constant supply of puzzles, every one of them new. Solve for as long as you like.

Relax — no clock

The same puzzles with the timer removed. Sit with a hard board for twenty minutes if you want to.

Daily Challenge

One board a day, and everyone in the world solves the same one.

Also included

60 achievements — 30 tiered medal goals plus 30 one-offs

12 languages, fully translated interface

A warm paper-and-ink art style with hand-drawn clovers

Hints when you are stuck, and an undo that goes back 300 moves

Plays offline. Steam is only needed to sync achievements.

store_data.about_the_game:
This is your empire. Every decision is yours.

You don't just manage a racing team. You build an empire from the ground up.

A small garage. A single car. A dream. From weekend karting to the absolute pinnacle of motorsport — you control every part of the journey.

While you're reading this, your rivals are already developing new parts, signing the next star, and preparing to take what you want. The world never stops. Neither can you.

🏁 ONE WORLD. EVERY CATEGORY.

Automotive Empire simulates the entire motorsport pyramid as a living ecosystem across 7 disciplines and 21 championships running simultaneously:

• Karting — Where every legend begins

• Rally — Gravel, tarmac, snow. Survive the stages or be forgotten

• Touring Cars — Door-to-door combat where millimetres decide champions

• Stock Cars — Thunder on the ovals. Drafting, aggression, pure spectacle

• Endurance Prototypes — Hours of relentless pressure. Machines and men pushed to the limit

• Open Wheel — Precision, aerodynamics, and pure speed

• GP — The summit of motorsport. Only the best survive

Every team has ambitions. Every driver has a price. Every decision you make ripples across the entire world.

🔧 BUILD THE CAR THAT WINS

Races are not won on Sunday. They are won weeks earlier in the design office.

• Research and develop every component — aero, chassis, engine, suspension, gearbox

• Launch Special R&D projects that can change the balance of power

• Manage a realistic supply chain and homologate with the World Racing Association

• Every upgrade is a choice. Every choice has consequences.

👥 THE PEOPLE BEHIND THE WINS

Great cars don't win championships. Great organisations do.

• Sign drivers at every level of the pyramid — develop them or steal them

• Build your technical empire: Designers, Team Principals, Strategists, Pit Crew, CFO and more

• Staff have personalities, ambition and loyalty. Treat them well… or lose them to your rivals

📊 RACE DAY IS ONLY THE RESULT

Every lap time is the consequence of hundreds of decisions made before the lights go out.

• Deep lap-by-lap simulation with real strategic depth

• Live calls: pit windows, tyre strategy, safety car reactions

• Mechanical failures, unpredictable events and on-track chaos mean no two races are ever the same

💰 MORE THAN A RACING TEAM

Your empire is a global business.

• Live Global Commercial Cars Market — manufacture and sell road cars to fund your racing ambitions

• Live Economy & Racing Parts Market — buy, sell and trade components in a dynamic market

• Campus with 20 Buildings — construct and upgrade everything from wind tunnels to driver academies

• Deep R&D System — Design, Upgrade, Reverse Engineer, pursue Special Projects, and develop Commercial Car lines

• Negotiate sponsorships, manage your brand, and control the finances

• Scale from scrappy privateer to global automotive powerhouse

🎵 AN EMPIRE DESERVES ITS OWN SOUND

Automotive Empire features an original electronic soundtrack — pulsing beats and high-energy compositions crafted to match the tension of race day, the grind of the design office, and the thrill of building something from nothing.

MOD-FRIENDLY DESIGN

The game is built to support community modification.

WHY AUTOMOTIVE EMPIRE IS DIFFERENT

Most motorsport management games let you run one team in one championship.

Automotive Empire simulates the entire world.

While you focus on your next race, legends are being born, teams are going bankrupt, and your future rivals are already planning to destroy you.

This is not a game about managing a car. This is a game about controlling a world.

The only question is: Will you build an empire… or become a footnote?

store_data.about_the_game:
Blind Shaman is a first-person alchemy simulator where you play as Grak, a blind goblin shaman.

Step into his workshop, make and sell your own potions, and meet the characters who come seeking your help. Put your unusual perception to work and discover what it means to be an alchemist.

A different way to see

Experience Grak’s unusual perception as your surroundings take shape out of darkness. Sound, touch, and scent come to life through a distinctive visual style, revealing different aspects of your surroundings and the things you hold. Learn to trust your senses and notice what others overlook.

Alchemy in your hands

Take up your tools and settle into the life of an alchemist. Crush ingredients in a mortar, work at your cauldron, and fill bottles with potions you’ve made yourself. Handle the tools and ingredients directly, enjoying the satisfaction of turning an experiment into a creation you can hold in your hands.

Those who come to your door

Welcome a varied cast of characters into your workshop. Some arrive to buy a potion. Others need help with a strange problem or bring something they want you to examine. Listen to their stories, discover what they need, and put your skills to use. Your workshop is where their troubles meet your curiosity.

Discover what alchemy can do

Alchemy reaches far beyond potion making. Unfamiliar substances and unexplained objects invite you to experiment, test your ideas, and find a way to help. What you create can become part of the investigation itself.

Keep a personal journal of your discoveries, give unfamiliar ingredients your own names, and develop your own theories. A successful experiment may resolve a problem. An unexpected reaction may complicate it—or reveal something you would never have discovered otherwise.

With each encounter, build the experience to face something stranger next time.

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to the City of Rats!

Every Merchant has their own story, their own tricks, and their own way of doing business. Some play fair, some take risks, and some might have a little something hidden in their cart. Merchants must carry the city's goods through the gates, and every cart has to face the Inspector before it can enter. And don't expect every Inspector to be a good rat either. Coins can be very persuasive. Load your cart, declare your goods, bluff, negotiate, and do whatever it takes to make a profit

The real question is, Are You an Honest Merchant?

The Rule of Business!

A 2-8 player card game where you play as real Merchants and Inspectors, and being honest isn’t always the best way to do business. The player with the most coins at the end wins.

Here How you Deal:

Phase 1 - Resupply

The market is hungry for fresh goods, and your hand is probably terrible. Luckily, you may discard any number of cards once, then draw back up to a full hand—like restocking your stall before the city gates open. When you’re done blaming the supplier, press Ready.

Phase 2 - Pack Your Wagon

Packing 1-6 goods and load them into your wagon. Then declare one type of legal good.

You must tell the truth about the number of cards. What those cards actually are, however, is between you, your conscience, and the suspiciously heavy wagon.

Phase 3 - Inspection

The Inspector chooses what happens to each wagon:

  • Release it and let everything inside enter the city.

  • Inspect it and reveal every card.

  • Make a Deal because justice is important, but coins are also quite persuasive.

If the declaration was honest, the Inspector pays compensation. If forbidden or undeclared goods are found, the Merchant pays the penalty.

store_data.about_the_game:
Da Capo is a musical puzzle game where you reshape the world with sound. Follow Aria Coda, and rediscover your lost inspiration amidst the rise and fall of notes.

She once wrote the world in notes. Now, she is silent.

Core Gameplay

Reshape the World with SoundMechanic Origin: The Life Cycle of Sound (ADSR) & Delay EffectsJust like a real synthesizer or a host software (DAW), every note has its own life cycle. In Da Capo, you will master the Attack, Decay, Sustain, and Release of sound. This is not only the key to reclaiming your musical memory, but also the only tool to reshape terrain and solve puzzles.

A Genuine DAW-Like Interaction

We utilized interaction logic highly consistent with professional audio workstations (DAWs). You can directly drag and adjust the Envelope, Delay Time, and Feedback parameters in the game. As you turn the knobs, the platform beneath your feet changes along with your parameters. True "what you see is what you get"—tweak the sound, change the world.

Story

Long ago, Aria Coda measured the entire world with notes. Until one day, those melodies suddenly vanished, and she lost her creative inspiration and her voice.All that was left for her was a profound silence, and a maze built out of sound spectrums.To find herself, she must step into the afterimages composed of sound. Along this journey, she will relearn the true essence of sound—how it Attacks, how it Decays, how it Sustains, and how it Releases.Follow her steps, and let the sound carry you through lost memories. Until at last, she must answer the question: Why do we create music?

Key Features

Synesthesia: Perfect synchronization of music and visuals. Every sound you make is perfectly matched to the parameters you adjust.Minimalist Aesthetic: Alternating between minimalist geometry and cool/warm tones, delivering a cinematic experience.Original Soundtrack: Original music runs through the entire game, guiding you through the ebb and flow of emotions within the flow of notes.

She forgot how to speak, but the sound never forgot her.

Da Capo.

store_data.about_the_game:
Looking cool starts with a clean dodge.

FLEX KING is an arcade action game built around four-direction dodging. Read the enemy's aim, react before the bullet hits, and survive the volley to enjoy a stylish bullet-time counterattack. Test your reflexes and judgment solo, or team up with a friend in local two-player co-op.

Four directions. Every move counts.

An enemy aims at your left side? Dodge right. A shot to the head? Duck. The rules are simple, but last-second feints, spread shots, and sniper fire will keep you guessing. Read the target, time your move, and keep your cool as the attacks come closer together.

Survive the volley. Steal the spotlight.

Dodge every shot in a volley and watch the action shift into a bullet-time counterattack sequence. See the bullets brush past and savor the payoff for a string of good decisions. Feeling bold? Dodge closer to the moment of impact to pull off a clutch dodge.

Bring a friend. Keep it together.

Local two-player co-op features its own stages and difficulty progression. Handle your own incoming fire, dodge together side by side, and coordinate while stacked vertically. As formations change, work out who needs to move, when to act together, and when to dodge in different directions. Your reflexes and your teamwork both face the next volley.

Clear stages, practice, or go endless.

Fight your way through Arcade mode and take on higher difficulties. Head to Practice to work on a stage that's giving you trouble, or enter solo or co-op Endless mode to see how many waves you can survive. After a failed run, the report helps you understand the fatal shot and turn your last mistake into progress.

Pick your look. Bring your battle music.

Unlock and choose your character, preview and unlock music, and take your favorite tracks into the next challenge. Make a clean escape, and look good doing it.

store_data.about_the_game:
Your Beat Is Your Firepower

Only a single attack button is needed. You don't have to aim manually—just hit the beats accurately. Tapping out different rhythm patterns unleashes distinct skills; the more intricate the rhythm, the more powerful the move. Focus entirely on the groove: as long as you stay on beat, your firepower will automatically track and strike down targets.

Build Momentum & Strike Back

Every rhythm pattern you complete builds up your [Groove]. Once your [Groove] is fully charged, you can activate it anytime to enter [Flow State]. Inside [Flow State], the surrounding swarm is forced to a near-complete halt right around you. Skills executed during [Flow] are banked, then discharged in an explosive barrage when the window closes.

Ride the Ebb and Flow of the Music

When the horde closes in and when you get breathing room to regroup—every surge and lull is seamlessly tied to the structure and progression of the soundtrack.

A Cozy Return to Nature

StickerScout is a relaxing, stress-free wildlife observation game set in the serene wilderness of Beaver Falls. With no timers, no fail states, and no combat, you can sit back, listen to the soothing ambient sounds of the forest, and watch the ecosystem come alive.

Photograph & Collect

Patience is rewarded! Hidden animals will naturally appear as you passively observe your surroundings. Snap their photos using your in-game camera then visit the Ranger Station's Sticker Press to turn your shots into adorable, high-quality stickers.

Features

  • Three Relaxing Dioramas: Observe the bustling Beaver Dam, process film at the Ranger Station, and unwind inside your cozy Tent Interior.

  • Immersive Audio: Enjoy rich, dynamic ambient soundscapes—like rushing river water, gentle rain, and birdsong—with no distracting background music.

  • Sticker Album: Collect over 30 unique stickers and arrange them in your customizable nature journal.

  • Pure Pixel Art: Hand-crafted, crisp pixel art environments full of hidden details and charming animations.

store_data.about_the_game:
What it is

One More Floor is a solo dungeon crawler. It plays the way a small box board game plays: a deck of room cards, dice for fighting, and a character with four numbers on it.

How a run goes

The dungeon is fourteen areas across five floors. Each area deals nine cards from a deck of twenty. When the area is finished, you climb down and see what the next area has in store for you.

What carries over

Your character does not carry over runs. What changes is the dungeon itself. At the end of each floor you are offered cards to permanently change what you will encounter on the way down next time.

Features

  • Fourteen areas, five floors, five bosses

  • A living twenty card dungeon deck

  • Four spells and two slots to carry them in

  • One life per run

  • Runs save as you play

Hidden sticky notes, little secrets, and mini-games are waiting to be discovered as you explore the world.
