5194310.name: Divine Wrath: Blessing of the Gods

store_data.about_the_game:
Divine Wrath: Blessing of the Gods is a dark fantasy top down magic shooter. There are no guns here and no bullets. Every projectile on screen is a spell you assembled yourself: chain lightning that arcs through a dozen corpses, poison pools that eat armor, frost novas that lock a wave in place so your blades can shatter it. You don't shoot. You cast, and you keep casting, until the screen stops being a battlefield and becomes a light show.

Build the Spellbook, Not the Character

Your power lives inside a physical grimoire. Skills, runes and sigils are objects you place into the pages of your book, and where you place them matters as much as what you place. Space is limited. Every slot you spend on raw damage is a slot you didn't spend on cooldown, mana economy, or the rune that turns a mediocre spell into a build defining engine.

There is no character sheet to fill in. There is only the book, the grid and the constant pressure of deciding what to cut.

Elemental Reactions That Actually Cascade

Elements are not damage types. They are ingredients.

Freeze a pack and shatter it for burst damage. Overload a frozen target with lightning for a Static Freeze that locks down everything nearby. Detonate stacked poison into a Toxic Burst that chains to whatever it touches. Push bleed high enough and the whole group goes off in a Blood Surge.

At low stages you trigger reactions by accident. By stage 20, a well built book chains them automatically and the screen fills with overlapping shockwaves, blooming poison clouds, spiraling vortices and damage numbers in the tens of thousands. The spectacle is not decoration. It is the readout of a build working exactly as designed.

Over 120 Skills, Runes and Sigils

The Codex holds more than 120 discoverable pieces and you will not see them all in one run. Fireball, Frost Shard, Lightning Slash, Blade Dance, Plague Brand, Chakram, Cleansing Light, Spark Shards, Vortex, and dozens more waiting behind locked pages.

Better still, spells combine. Arc Bolt fused with Whirling Blade collapses into a Vortex. Poison Pool fused with a Vortex becomes a Plague Brand that turns every kill into an expanding cloud of rot. Discovering a recipe is permanent knowledge, so every run you lose still makes the next one deeper.

Every Stage Asks You to Gamble

Between waves, the shop opens. Coins are always short. Do you buy the rune you need, reroll for the recipe you want, or save for the sigil two stages from now?

Wandering the forest are things that are not shops. The Forest Hermit does not sell blessings, he trades them: enemies move 40% slower, but they also gain 50% more health. All your cooldowns drop 25%, but so does your survivability. He offers one, or both, and both is always tempting and rarely wise.

Run speed is yours to control. Play at 1x to read every reaction, or push to 5x when your build has already won and you just want to watch the world come apart.

Kill the Thing at the End

Stages escalate into bosses, and bosses do not care how pretty your spell chain looks. Dragons that blot out the canopy and set the forest burning behind them. Horrors that outrange you, outlast you, and punish a book built for clearing trash instead of killing something that fights back.

Beating the game means beating them. Every run is a question: is this book good enough yet, or are you about to find out exactly where it breaks?

The gods gave you their power. They did not promise you would survive holding it.

Wandering the forest are things that are not shops. The Forest Hermit does not sell blessings, he trades them: enemies move 40% slower, but they also gain 50% more health. All your cooldowns drop 25%, but so does your survivability. He offers one, or both, and both is always tempting and rarely wise.

Run speed is yours to control. Play at 1x to read every reaction, or push to 5x when your build has already won and you just want to watch the world come apart.

Kill the Thing at the End

Stages escalate into bosses, and bosses do not care how pretty your spell chain looks. Dragons that blot out the canopy and set the forest burning behind them. Horrors that outrange you, outlast you, and punish a book built for clearing trash instead of killing something that fights back.

Beating the game means beating them. Every run is a question: is this book good enough yet, or are you about to find out exactly where it breaks?

The gods gave you their power. They did not promise you would survive holding it.
store_data.short_description: A dark fantasy magic shooter where you build your own spellbook. Claim the blessings of the Greek gods, fuse over 120 skills, runes and sigils inside a living grimoire, and drown endless hordes in screen filling arcane VFX. Survive the stages. Kill the god beasts. Or become one more corpse.

store_data.about_the_game:
About This Game

Fuel Burn is a fast-paced zombie survival shooter set on the back of a moving car. Your goal is simple: survive the road, fight through increasingly dangerous zombie hordes, and make it to the 20-kilometer mark, where a station with other survivors is rumored to exist.

You are not exploring the apocalypse on foot. The entire game revolves around defending a moving vehicle while managing your firepower and improving your chances of surviving the next stretch of road.

Fight From a Moving Vehicle

You ride in the back of a car and shoot zombies before they can reach and damage the vehicle. Enemies approach from different directions and become more dangerous as you progress.

Accuracy matters. Missing too many shots gives enemies more time to close the distance, while stronger enemy types require you to react differently and prioritize your targets.

Upgrade Your Weapons and Vehicle

Defeated enemies provide scrap, which can be used to improve your chances of survival.

Upgrades include:

  • Weapon improvements

  • Vehicle speed

  • Acceleration

  • Nitro

  • Additional combat and survival upgrades

Choosing the right upgrades changes how effectively you can handle larger and stronger hordes later in a run.

Multiple Enemy Types

The apocalypse is not filled with only one kind of zombie.

You will encounter different enemies with their own strengths and behavior, including regular zombies, fast aerial attackers, and heavily armored brute enemies that can absorb much more damage.

As you travel farther, the pressure increases and encounters become progressively harder.

Reach the Survivors

Your main objective is to survive the full 20-kilometer journey.

Somewhere ahead is supposedly a safe station occupied by survivors. Along the way, the game gradually introduces more questions about the world, the zombies, and what is waiting for you at your destination.

Survival

Fuel Burn is designed around short, action-focused survival runs. Each attempt lets you fight through hordes, collect resources, improve your build, and try to travel farther than before.

A current playthrough provides approximately 40–60 minutes of gameplay, depending on your performance and playstyle.

Current Features

The current version includes vehicle-based zombie combat, multiple enemy types, weapon and vehicle upgrades, scrap collection, increasing difficulty, progression across a 20-kilometer route, and a complete playable survival experience.

Fuel Burn is in active development, with additional enemies, bosses, weapons, upgrades, story content, helpers, and other features planned for future updates.

store_data.about_the_game:
AN IDLE RPG THAT RUNS LIKE AN OPERATING SYSTEM

AFK does not ask for your attention. It gives you a desktop. Your battle plays out live in a 990x76 strip inside the taskbar while you keep windows open, compare gear and plan the next build. Click the strip and the fight goes fullscreen. Close it and your army keeps going.

BUILD AN ARMY, NOT AN APM SCORE

Nine heroes, three on the field. Weapons, off-hands and elements are class-locked, so a party is a decision rather than a slot machine. Skill trees, rune allocations and prestige nodes stack into a build you can actually read.

YOU WRITE THE LOOT RULES

In an idle game loot is a stream, not a sequence of events. Instead of turning hundreds of overnight drops into hundreds of decisions, you write the rules once: ask me about legendaries, send runes to the cube, melt the rest. The pipeline enforces them and only the exceptions reach you. The decision queue holds at most fifty items and never touches your bag.

LOOT YOU DECIDE ON

Ten rarity tiers from Bit to Yotta. Implicit lines, affixes, enhancement from +0 to +25 with real downgrade risk, sockets, and runes that carry three candidate stats. The roll happens when you socket them, not when they drop.

THE CUBE

Turn runes into gems and gems back into runes. Every enhancement shows you its true success chance before you commit anything.

FIVE ACTS, FOUR DIFFICULTIES, ONE ENDLESS TOWER

Normal, Nightmare, Hell and Torment, each one unlocked by clearing the last. A stage map that mutates weekly, a tower with no ceiling, and timed Boss Rush races with a real reward ladder and a leaderboard.

ASYNCHRONOUS PVP THAT REPLAYS

Send your army to the arena. The server re-simulates the fight with the same deterministic engine your client runs, then hands you the replay. No lag, no waiting for an opponent, no arguments about what happened.

CLANS AND CHAT

A clan headquarters with members, contributions, a shared development tree, announcements and applications. Channels, direct messages and mentions.

SOUND WITH NO SAMPLES

Every effect and the background music are synthesised in code from waveform functions - no audio files ship with the game. Effects and music have separate volume controls.

PLAYS IN TWELVE LANGUAGES

Full interface in English, Turkish, German, French, Italian, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Polish, Russian, Japanese, Korean and Simplified Chinese.

store_data.about_the_game:
Post Show Cleanup is a relaxing first-person cleanup game about restoring a public park after a huge concert.

The crowds are gone, the music has stopped, and the park is covered in cans, bottles, cups, and everything else left behind. Start with your bare hands, collect what you can carry, recycle it for money, and gradually improve the way you work.

Clean at your own pace

There is no rush. Pick a section of the park, clear the rubbish, make piles, plan your route, and watch the environment gradually return to normal.

Upgrade how you clean

Spend the money you earn on practical equipment and upgrades:

  • Carry more rubbish at once.

  • Pick up and transfer items faster.

  • Use a push broom to gather large piles.

  • Upgrade the broom’s width, strength, and capacity.

  • Unlock a cart for transporting much larger loads.

  • Improve recycling infrastructure and bring additional recycling points back online.

Turn cleanup into logistics

As the park opens up, cleaning becomes more than simply picking things up. Stage piles where they are useful, decide when to use the broom or cart, work around recycling downtime, and choose which upgrades make your current route easier.

Restore more than just the ground

Some objects are not rubbish. You may find items that belong somewhere in the park and choose to return them to their proper place, helping restore small details of the environment along the way.

From chaos to calm

What starts as an overwhelming post-concert mess gradually becomes a clean, peaceful park again. The main reward is seeing the space transform because of the work you have done.

store_data.about_the_game:
A little café. A clever crew. Your instructions.

Aunt Ada has handed you the keys to her neighborhood café—and a robot waiting for its first instructions. In Byte Bistro, you turn that modest beginning into a working kitchen, one recipe, one routine, and one satisfied guest at a time.

This single-player café-management and automation game pairs warm pixel art with a very practical question: can you teach your little crew to handle the next rush?

Build the program. Watch dinner happen.

Your robots follow the programs you create. Arrange actions to gather ingredients, cook, plate, serve, and clean. Start with a simple sequence, then expand your toolkit with conditions, loops, variables, and reusable functions as you progress.

Give different robots different jobs, test your logic, and refine the routine when an empty shelf or a busy station interrupts the plan. Up to four programmable robots share one kitchen, so coordination matters as much as speed.

Run the café your way.

Choose the menu, set prices, order supplies, and invest your earnings in equipment and upgrades. Unlock 30 recipes using 25 ingredients across a 24-service campaign. Keep an eye on waiting guests, clean tables, and shared cooking stations as your café grows.

Want to lend a hand? Step into recipe-specific cooking and table-cleaning minigames while your robots handle their own instructions.

Keep the kitchen humming.

Continue in endless mode after the campaign, or switch to Desktop Companion for a compact café window. Your real robot programs keep serving guests, using ingredients, and earning money while the game remains open. Companion service does not advance campaign days.

  • Visual programming that grows from simple actions to reusable routines.

  • Up to four robots, one shared café, and plenty of ways to divide the work.

  • Menu planning, stock management, equipment upgrades, and hands-on minigames.

  • Warm pixel-art surroundings and an original soundtrack.

  • English, Spanish, French, and Simplified Chinese language options.

store_data.about_the_game:
Seven years ago the Void opened over the Rim. Nobody knows who built the gates around it. Everybody knows the Rim would starve without them.

You are a pilot with a debt and a ship that has seen better decades. Then your onboard AI picks a signal out of the static. It repeats every 402 seconds. It is using your hull number.

FLATBED is a single-player space action RPG. Fly, trade, fight, take contracts, hunt bounties and follow a story that never explains itself. Nobody tells you what the Void is. You piece it together from wrecks, logs and people who lie to you.

Build the ship you want. Cannons, missiles, shields, armour, engines, reactors, drones: every piece has a role and a power cost, so a build is a choice, not a bigger number. Start in a rusted tug. End up in something the pirates run from.

Combat is fast and built for the mouse. Click to fly, click to lock, and your guns track the target while you pick your angle. Missiles chase. Shields flicker and fail. Capital ships open their batteries and the screen fills with fire.

Get hit and you feel it: sparks, debris, hull fires, and a ship that goes down in a chain of explosions instead of a puff of smoke.

Hand-built sectors that play differently, not just look different. Rock belts where a shortcut costs hull. Nebulae where the radar lies. Radiation that eats your ship unless you keep the shield up. Wreck fields where the dead block the line of fire.

Factions you recognise by colour before you read the name. Raiders, scavengers, a cartel with something to hide, harvesters with drills instead of guns, and the Keepers, who do not dodge. They correct course. Like they are counting.

A story where every choice has a price. Dock masters, patrol captains and brokers all want something from you, and none of them are telling the whole truth. By the end you decide who gets left behind.

  • Single-player space action RPG in pixel art
  • Mouse-driven flight and combat: click to fly, click to lock, your guns do the rest
  • Build your ship: cannons, missiles, shields, armour, engines, reactors, drones
  • Hulls to earn, from a worn-out tug to a heavy cruiser
  • Hand-built sectors with their own rules: radiation, fog, drift, rocks, wrecks
  • Factions at war with each other, not just with you
  • A story with choices that cost and endings that remember them
  • Trade, mine, run contracts, hunt bounties
  • Death costs credits and trust, never your progress

Add FLATBED to your wishlist. The signal repeats every 402 seconds. It is already counting.

Little Groves is a peaceful strategy-puzzle game about growing a forest and protecting it from the forces that threaten it. Place tiles, discover more than 50 hidden groves, chain together Harmonies and bend the changing wind to keep fire, drought and blight at bay.

Grow Your Forest.

In Little Groves, you take turns placing tiles to create groves. Each new grove scores points, with rarer groves offering up more tiles so your forest can continue to grow.

Be the Forest’s Guardian

Your forest won’t always stay peaceful. Drought, Bramble, Blight and Fire can spread through what you’ve built. Bend the wind, contain threats and find ways to turn danger into opportunity.

Chain Together Harmonies

Build scoring chains across your forest. Blooms reward neighbouring groves, Deer roam across connected meadows, and clever placement can trigger cascades of Harmonies.

Rebuild the Lost Grove Book

Discover more than 50 hidden groves and rebuild the Grove Book. Each discovery can reward you with points, new tiles or ancient powers, including the ability to summon rain and end a drought.

  • Forest bathing sounds

  • Chain Harmonies for enormous scores

  • Every forest grows differently

  • Unlock new tiles and forest themes

  • 'Your Forest' diorama editor

  • Daily competitive challenges

store_data.about_the_game:
Fifty-three games. One disc. Four friends.

Neon vector arcade in the spirit of the machines that ran on line drawings and nothing else. Every game here is short, sharp and meant to be replayed until someone on the couch demands revenge.

The party board

Three big maps: a synthwave city, a rave club and a seaside hotel. You roll, you move, you land on a square, and the square throws all of you into a mini-game. Batteries win the party; money, weapons and dirty tricks decide who gets them. The board keeps score, the mini-games decide the mood.

Play together, however you sit

Up to four players on a single screen, gamepads or keyboard shared between you. Or online, running the same lockstep simulation the local game uses, so a race stays a race and not a slideshow. Missing a fourth? Bots take the empty seats.

Your own character

Draw one. Head, body, arms, colours. The editor is part of the game, not a side app, and the character you make walks into every game that uses figures.

Bring your own games

The collection is open. An add-on is a folder with two text files, and the game checks a stranger's work before it ever runs it.

store_data.about_the_game:
Primal Heir: The Mortal Realm is a story-driven, nostalgic 2D JRPG built in the spirit of classic 16-bit console adventures.

When the celestial Heart of Equilibrium shattered, its fragments rained upon the Mortal Realm, altering the fates of two chosen heirs.

Follow Kain, a warrior bound to shadow, and Eldora, a maiden tied to light, as their paths cross in a fracturing world. Explore vibrant towns, delve into dangerous dungeons, battle strange creatures, and uncover secrets hidden throughout the land.

The Mortal Realm is the first installment in the larger Primal Heir story, concluding at Haven Port. The journey will continue in future chapters.

Key Features

  • Story-driven retro JRPG adventure

  • Classic party-based combat with old-school RPG mechanics

  • A growing cast of playable companions

  • Handcrafted pixel-art environments

  • Villages, forests, caves, ruins and ports to explore

  • Side quests, secrets and optional activities

  • Equipment and crafting systems

  • Fishing and other world activities

  • Single-player adventure

store_data.about_the_game:
SCORE 80

“80 points. That’s the minimum you need to survive.”

You wake up in a cold, unfamiliar room.

Standing before you is a bear wearing an unsettling grin.

The rules it gives you are simple:

Score 80 points or more before time runs out.

SCORE 80 is a death game × brain-training game that puts a wide range of your abilities to the test, including judgment, calculation, memory, and spatial awareness.

A variety of mini-games await, each with its own unique rules.

Guide an object to the goal in “SLIDE.”
Quickly interpret the instructions and choose the correct hand in “RSP.”
Search through countless numbers to find the specified one, complete equations from a given answer, test your judgment in a poker-style card game, and challenge your spatial awareness in “CUBE.”

No matter the game, the objective remains the same:

Score 80 points or more.

As you progress, the difficulty increases, and simple knowledge alone will no longer be enough to overcome the challenges ahead.

You’ll need quick judgment, calm thinking, and the concentration to perform under pressure.

For those seeking an even greater challenge, HARD MODE awaits with even more demanding rules and increased difficulty.

Can you overcome every game and make it all the way to the end?

Think. Decide. Score 80.

—All you need to clear the game is SCORE 80.

store_data.about_the_game:
An epic auto-battling RPG unveils right in the corner of your desktop!

Watch your slime push through endless floors and crush giant bosses—or dive into thrilling 4-player idle co-op! Combine deep star charts, class trees, and loyal buddies to craft your ultimate build. Endless progression and adventure start right here!

High-Octane Action in the Corner of Your Screen!

Enjoy flashy, fast-paced combat right on your desktop without ever disrupting your mouse or work! Watch powerful ultimates and visually striking skills wipe out hordes of enemies in real time while you sit back and idle.

Thrilling 4-Player Co-Op! Team Up for Blazing-Fast Leveling

Jump straight into rooms and join the action! Head to the same floor with friends for chaotic, high-energy multiplayer. Stack buffs together to skyrocket your EXP and efficiency—reach heights you could never achieve alone!

Overcome Massive Bosses Standing in Your Way!

Towering, powerful bosses await as you climb the tower! This isn't just mindlessly idling—synergize your build, class, and team coordination to crush tough foes and experience an adrenaline-pumping surge of victory!

Deep Star Charts! Craft Your One-of-a-Kind Ultimate Build

Explore a massive star chart packed with 251 nodes. Critical hit specialization, super regeneration, screen-wiping magic... where you light up the stars is entirely up to you! Reset anytime to experiment and forge an unbeatable build no one else can copy!

Journey Alongside Your Unique Buddies!

The buddies joining your adventure are far more than mere pets! Feed them, name them, and watch them evolve into powerful companions that dramatically boost your stats and combat abilities. Aim for the top of the infinite tower with your favorite companions!

10 Base Paths & Deep Class Branching! Reincarnate to Reach New Heights

Start with 10 fundamental class paths and branch out into higher tiers! Change classes or unleash "Reincarnation" to reset your level for a permanent EXP boost. Accelerate your growth exponentially with each rebirth and build an unstoppable slime!

store_data.about_the_game:
Welcome to Potion Nook! Step into the role of a witch and run your very own charming shop filled with magic potions and amulets. Keep in mind that being a great witch requires some cleverness - sometimes you won't have the necessary ingredients on hand to fulfill an order, and that's when the real challenge begins!

Serving Demanding Customers

Customers visiting your shop start off in a great mood. If you serve them fast, they’ll gladly leave a generous tip. Watch the clock, though - if they have to wait too long, they’ll lose their patience and leave in a huff!

Brewing Potions and Crafting Amulets

Combine a wide variety of magical ingredients to fulfill orders. Gather toadstools, magical seaweed, and even... unicorn hair, to brew the perfect potions and craft powerful amulets!

Trading and Growing Plants

Missing an ingredient for your recipe? First thing in the morning, you can visit the wandering merchant to buy the necessary supplies. If you prefer to be self-sufficient, grab your tools and grow the missing ingredients in your garden patches out back!

Play Solo or in Co-op (Local and Online)

Is running a shop too much for one pair of hands? You can experience the entire game solo or invite your friends to help! Potion Nook supports both local (shared screen) and online multiplayer. Divide the chores and master the potion-making chaos!

store_data.about_the_game:
EARN EVERYTHING. RISK EVERYTHING.

Tarnish Online is a full-loot sandbox MMORPG built around risk, progression, exploration, trade, and player choice.

There are no traditional character levels to grind. Your power comes from the equipment you earn, the weapons you master, the skills you develop, and the decisions you make throughout your journey.

Explore a vibrant fantasy world filled with dangerous creatures, powerful bosses, valuable resources, hidden locations, challenging dungeons, and other adventurers.

Leave the safety of town and the stakes change.

The gear you carry can be lost.
The loot you discover can become someone else's reward.
The companion you bring into the wilderness can become part of your greatest victory — or your greatest loss.

How much are you willing to risk?

Explore. Fight. Trade. Survive — or become someone else's loot.

A SANDBOX MMORPG BUILT AROUND CONSEQUENCES

Tarnish Online is designed around meaningful decisions.

Instead of following a traditional theme-park MMO structure, Tarnish gives you multiple ways to progress, build wealth, master your equipment, and interact with the world.

Become a powerful fighter.

Master a profession.

Gather rare resources.

Craft valuable equipment.

Hunt powerful creatures.

Build a guild.

Compete against other players.

Trade your way to wealth.

Or simply explore the world and discover what lies beyond the next horizon.

Your character is not defined by a level number.

Your equipment, mastery, skills, reputation, wealth, and choices define your journey.

FULL-LOOT OPEN-WORLD PVP

The wilderness is dangerous by design.

Outside protected towns and designated safe areas, every journey carries a risk.

In full-loot PvP zones, defeat can have real consequences. The equipment and resources you carry are part of the risk you choose to take.

• Full-loot PvP in designated open-world areas
• Real inventory loss when defeated in full-loot zones
• PK and player conflict
• Duels and structured PvP
• Guild conflicts and territorial struggles
• Safe towns and protected areas for storage, preparation, and trade

Your bank protects what you have already earned.

What remains in your inventory is a decision.

How much should you carry?

How much can you safely bring home?

When should you turn back?

In Tarnish, knowing when to take a risk can be just as important as knowing how to fight.

PROGRESSION WITHOUT TRADITIONAL LEVELS

Tarnish Online removes the traditional character-level treadmill.

There is no endless cycle of gaining levels simply to unlock the next zone.

Instead, your progression comes from your equipment, mastery, upgrades, skills, and long-term character development.

Gear can be refined, upgraded, socketed, and developed into increasingly powerful builds.

Equipment Fame allows you to develop mastery around specific weapon and armor types as you use them.

Active and passive skills allow you to customize your combat style.

Q, W, and E equipment skills connect your abilities directly to the equipment you choose to wear.

Combat Power provides a clear representation of your current equipped strength.

Rebirth, titles, and long-term progression provide additional goals for players looking to continue developing their characters.

You don't simply become stronger because a level number increased.

You become stronger because you earned it.

A WORLD THAT CONTINUES TO GROW

Tarnish Online is designed as an evolving online world.

The current Early Access experience focuses on exploration, combat, progression, gathering, crafting, dungeons, PvP, pets, mounts, trading, guilds, and social interaction.

The world will continue to expand throughout Early Access with new regions, monsters, bosses, equipment, activities, challenges, events, progression systems, and quality-of-life improvements.

Our goal is to create an MMORPG that becomes deeper and more engaging over time while preserving the core sandbox experience.

COMBAT, DUNGEONS AND CHALLENGES

The open world is only part of Tarnish Online.

Take on structured PvE content, push your limits, compete for rankings, and search for powerful rewards.

Wave-based dungeons test your ability to survive escalating encounters.

Sequential-kill challenges reward efficiency and combat mastery.

Star-rated dungeons provide additional challenges for experienced players.

Endless Rift offers repeatable challenges with weekly rankings.

Tower Defense scenarios challenge players to defend valuable objectives against waves of enemies.

Scheduled world bosses create opportunities for players to gather, cooperate, compete, and fight for valuable rewards.

The 1v1 Arena provides a dedicated competitive environment with spectator support.

Whether you're farming Fame, chasing rankings, testing your build, or hunting rare equipment, Tarnish gives you multiple ways to challenge yourself.

BOSS HUNTING AND RARE LOOT

Powerful enemies are more than obstacles.

They are opportunities.

Explore dangerous regions.

Search for elite encounters.

Track boss spawn schedules.

Prepare your equipment.

Gather allies.

Take the risk.

Rare enemies can reward rare equipment, valuable resources, and powerful upgrades.

Every boss encounter can create an opportunity.

And every valuable drop can make you a target.

GATHERING, HUNTING, FISHING AND CRAFTING

Not every adventure requires a sword.

Tarnish Online gives you multiple ways to progress outside direct combat.

Gather and harvest valuable resources.

Use the right tools to collect materials.

Hunt creatures across the world.

Fish through dedicated fishing activities.

Use gathered materials to craft and produce valuable goods.

Discover treasure maps and hidden opportunities.

Resources collected by one player can become equipment, crafting materials, trade goods, or profit for another.

Every profession is connected to the world economy.

PETS AND MOUNTS THAT MATTER

Pets and mounts are more than visual accessories.

They are part of your adventure and part of your progression.

Combat pets can support you in battle.

Gathering pets can help with resource-focused playstyles.

Wild mounts can be captured using lasso mechanics.

Pets can evolve, gain abilities, and become valuable companions.

Mounts allow you to travel and explore the world more efficiently.

Bringing valuable companions into dangerous areas can also increase the stakes.

The more valuable your companion becomes, the more carefully you must decide where to take it.

A PLAYER-DRIVEN ECONOMY

Tarnish Online's economy is shaped by players.

Supply and demand matter.

Resources have value because players need them.

Equipment has value because players want it.

Use the Auction House to buy and sell valuable items.

Trade directly with other players.

Send items through player mail.

Use NPC shops and city reputation systems.

Operate private shops and character markets.

Store valuable items securely in your bank.

As Tarnish grows, the economy will continue to evolve alongside the player community.

GUILDS, SOCIAL SYSTEMS AND TERRITORY

Tarnish Online can be played solo, but the world creates opportunities for cooperation and competition.

Join or create a guild.

Form parties.

Communicate with other adventurers.

Participate in guild activities and conflicts.

Challenge other players through duels.

Compete in structured PvP.

Build your reputation.

Take part in territory-focused gameplay.

Future updates may expand guild, territory, and social interaction systems throughout Early Access.

Build a character.

Build a guild.

Build a reputation.

Then defend everything you have created.

EXPLORE A VIBRANT FANTASY WORLD

Travel through a colorful fantasy world filled with distinct environments, creatures, resources, settlements, and challenges.

Explore peaceful meadows and forests.

Travel through villages and dangerous wilderness.

Discover deserts, frozen regions, volcanic territories, mysterious caves, and other unique environments.

Each region offers new enemies, new resources, new encounters, and new opportunities.

The world is designed to reward exploration.

Discover hidden locations.

Find valuable resources.

Encounter powerful enemies.

Track down bosses.

Search for rare loot.

Follow roads — or leave them behind.

There is always another place to discover.

AN ONLINE WORLD BUILT AROUND PLAYERS

Tarnish Online is designed from the ground up as an online multiplayer MMORPG.

Your character exists in a persistent shared world alongside other adventurers.

Players can cooperate, compete, trade, fight, form guilds, build wealth, and create their own stories.

The economy is shared.

The world is shared.

The risks are real.

The opportunities are yours.

Play together across supported platforms and experience the same world with other adventurers.

CROSS-PLATFORM MULTIPLAYER

Tarnish Online is designed to connect players across supported platforms.

Players can join the same online world, interact with one another, participate in combat, trade, form parties, and progress together regardless of their supported platform.

The Steam version is built specifically for PC with keyboard and mouse controls and a dedicated PC interface, while cross-platform multiplayer allows players to share the same online experience.

BUILT FOR PC AND CROSS-PLATFORM PLAY

Tarnish Online's PC version is designed around keyboard and mouse controls and a dedicated desktop interface.

The game uses server-authoritative systems for important online gameplay such as combat and loot.

The goal is to provide a stable and persistent multiplayer world where players across supported platforms can interact and play together.

EARLY ACCESS

Tarnish Online enters Steam Early Access on September 25, 2026.

The Early Access version provides a playable foundation built around exploration, combat, full-loot PvP, equipment progression, gathering, crafting, dungeons, world bosses, pets, mounts, trading, guilds, PvP, and social systems.

During Early Access, we plan to continue expanding the world with new content, enemies, equipment, activities, events, progression systems, balance changes, performance improvements, and quality-of-life updates.

Some systems may evolve significantly during development based on gameplay data, technical requirements, balancing, and community feedback.

Early Access players are joining Tarnish at the beginning of its journey and will help shape the future of the game.

WHAT TO EXPECT FROM EARLY ACCESS

Tarnish Online is being developed as a long-term online world.

Some features will arrive gradually rather than all at once.

Some systems may change based on gameplay data, community feedback, balancing requirements, and technical limitations.

Our goal is not simply to add more content.

Our goal is to build a world where exploration, risk, combat, trade, progression, and player interaction remain meaningful over time.

KEY FEATURES

• Full-loot sandbox MMORPG
• Cross-platform multiplayer
• Open-world PvP and player conflict
• No traditional character levels
• Gear-based progression
• Equipment Fame and weapon mastery
• Refining, sockets, tiers and set bonuses
• Active and passive skills
• Q / W / E equipment skills
• Combat Power and long-term progression
• Rebirth and titles
• Dynamic quests and world systems
• Dungeons and Endless Rift
• Tower Defense content
• 1v1 Arena and competitive play
• Scheduled world boss encounters
• Gathering, hunting, fishing and crafting
• Treasure maps and exploration
• Combat and gathering pets
• Wild mount capture
• Pet evolution and abilities
• Auction House and player-driven economy
• Player trading, mail and private shops
• Guilds and parties
• Territory-focused gameplay
• Leaderboards and competitive progression
• Persistent online world
• Windows PC + cross-platform multiplayer

THE WORLD IS YOURS. THE RISK IS YOURS.

Earn your equipment.

Build your wealth.

Master your abilities.

Choose your battles.

Explore dangerous territory.

Protect what you've earned.

Fight alongside other players.

Make your mark on the world.

And remember:

In Tarnish, nothing valuable is truly safe.

Explore. Fight. Trade. Survive — or become someone else's loot.

store_data.about_the_game:
In most tower defense games, you protect the fortress. Here, you are the horde at its gates.

Lairs & Lordships is a single-player reverse tower defense strategy game set in a dark fantasy world. Assemble an army of monsters, divide it into waves, deploy each formation, and send your creatures against human walls, towers, defenders, and commanders.

Every battle begins with a plan. Combine sturdy front lines, ranged support, magic, and siege specialists. There is no universal army: each fortress and region demands a different approach.

KEY FEATURES

Reverse the tower defense — Lead the attacking horde and break through walls, towers, defenders, and fortified strongholds.

Plan multiple waves — Choose your creatures, arrange their deployment, combine complementary classes, and refine formations between attempts.

Conquer and hold territory — Advance across a branching world map, collect income from captured regions, and defend your lands when enemy raids arrive.

Develop your faction — Recruit monsters and invest in branching upgrades for your units, commanders, and lair. Unlock new abilities and evolve creatures into specialized roles.

Adapt to every battlefield — Forest ambushes, sealed towers, wall limits, regional penalties, enemy commanders, and changing world events challenge familiar strategies.

Keep pushing — Revisit conquered regions at higher difficulties or enter escalating endless battles to test new army builds and push your strategies to the limit.

store_data.about_the_game:
Engagement is a tactical space-duel game built around the moment before the exchange. Time stops while both captains queue their next orders. Burn for speed, turn onto a bearing, bring a weapon online, brace an arc, or vent heat. Then commit. The clock runs until one plan ends first, and that captain gets the next decision.

Every command takes ticks. A long weapon spin-up buys time for an opponent to react. A short manoeuvre may win the next replan. The fight is decided by what each hull can do now, what it will do next, and what the other captain has already shown.

Start with a hull, then choose the argument it makes. A lance cutter bets on a clean firing line. A broadside ship asks for an angle. A seeker sloop creates pressure at range. An assault ram wants the distance gone.

Each hull carries its own three hardpoints and alternate equipment. Spinal lances, prow chasers, batteries, seeker racks, point defence, flares, and smoke change the range you want, the heat you can carry, and the openings you must deny.

Guns do different work. Batteries tear at shields. Lances walk through a shield arc. Seekers force a response. Point defence destroys incoming seekers, but it spends a firing window. Damage builds surge; surge can overdrive the next weapon. A heavy strike can stagger a hull and tear up its plan.

Every weapon gives the other captain a read. Use that information. Break the expected bearing, force a bad arc, or make the enemy choose between defence and their own shot.

Openings change the rules of the first exchange. Meet head-on across open void. Start inside knife range. Trade a crossing pass. Chase a retreating stern. Work around the rocks of The Reef, or bring a dead ship back under control in The Drift.

Asteroids block gunfire and turn space into cover. Momentum persists. A burn adds velocity, and a second burn is required to take it back. Position is a resource, and a line of sight is never free.

- One-on-one tactical space duels built around queued orders and alternating replans.

- Eight distinct hulls: Vesper, Ossuary, Reliquary, Anvil, Wick, Cathedral, Pyre, and Warden.

- Hull-specific weapon fits and alternate hardpoints.

- Opening scenarios including Long Approach, Knife Range, Crossing Pass, Stern Chase, The Reef, and The Drift.

- Shield arcs, heat, surge, burst movement, flares, smoke, and system damage.

- Machine opponents, local same-screen duels, best-of-three series, a gauntlet mode, and saved-duel viewing.

store_data.about_the_game:
LineManager is a public transport construction and operations simulation built on real-world maps.
You do not simply draw a line on a map and watch what happens. You build the infrastructure, place stops and stations, plan routes and timetables, and make sure your network actually works in day-to-day operation.
You can keep things relatively simple – or dive deep into track geometry, signalling, routes and operational details.

Build your network on real-world maps

The game uses maps based on OpenStreetMap. Dortmund is included as a large playable region, alongside Riga Central and a separate test area for experimenting with track construction.

Roads, buildings, parks, waterways and existing transport infrastructure form the foundation of the map. Existing tram and light-rail tracks can partly be incorporated into your own network, while new routes can be built freely or along existing streets.

Single and double track, street-running sections, reserved track, switches, crossovers, sidings, turning loops and tunnels are all part of the standard toolkit. Curves, track direction and physical connections actually matter.

Buses and trams work differently

Bus routes use the existing road network and have to follow traffic directions, junctions, traffic lights and surrounding traffic.

Trams, on the other hand, operate on their own track network. You decide which tracks are used in which direction, where vehicles can turn around and which platform belongs to which route.

Shuttle services, circular routes, short workings and more complex termini are possible. If a connection does not work, LineManager does not simply ignore the problem – it shows you where the route is broken.

Timetables are more than just a frequency

For each route, you can define operating hours, service frequency and vehicle requirements. Peak extras, short workings and temporary frequency increases can be added as well.

Vehicles follow actual duties, including leaving the depot, operating scheduled trips, taking breaks, switching routes and returning to the depot later in the day.

You can move or cancel individual departures, assign vehicles manually and watch how delays and conflicts affect the rest of the operating day.

Passengers have somewhere to go

Demand is generated by residents, workplaces, education and retail, and changes depending on the time of day and day of the week.

Passengers have their own origin and destination. They wait, board, travel, transfer and can miss connections. Vehicle capacity, service frequency and route design therefore have a direct effect on how well your network performs.

Alongside current passenger numbers, you can also monitor forecasts, waiting times, loads and the accessibility of different areas.

Go deeper if you want to

LineManager can automate many operational tasks, but players who want more control can take over the signalling and protection of the network themselves.

The game includes block sections, routes, switch locking, opposing-movement protection, overlaps, flank protection and protection systems for single-track sections. Routes can be set automatically or manually.

Balises and different signal types are also part of the system. In the signalling panel, you can monitor occupied sections and understand why a vehicle is currently being held.

This level of detail is optional. You decide how much of it you want to handle yourself.

Depots, vehicles and workshops

Trams need suitable storage and turning facilities. Depots can contain several tracks, and their usable length genuinely determines how many vehicles can be stored there.

Both single-ended and bidirectional trams are supported, as well as multiple-unit formations. Vehicle length, platform length, capacity, speed and driving behaviour are taken into account.

Workshop tracks and maintenance capacity form the basis for a vehicle-management system that will continue to expand during development.

Traffic does not only exist on your tracks

Cars and trucks move through the city as well. Buses and street-running trams can be delayed by road traffic, while segregated track remains unaffected by congestion.

Traffic lights have their own phases and can be grouped together. Tram and bus signals can also be integrated into the control system.

External rail services, walking and cycling connections, and larger events can influence demand and overall traffic patterns.

Run a transport company

In the end, the network also has to make financial sense.

Fare revenue, subsidies, vehicle costs and staff costs all contribute to the operating result. LineManager also includes a simplified tax and finance system, along with staff, recruitment, qualifications, sickness and other operational factors.

An optional AI operator can develop its own routes, vehicles and strategies, acting either as a competitor or as a cooperative partner.

A simulation to experiment with and grow into

LineManager is designed as a sandbox. You can build a small, manageable network or take on a complex city with tunnels, depots, timetables and your own signalling systems.

Many systems can be automated or opened only when needed. Players who simply want to build and observe should be able to enjoy the game just as much as those who want to know why that signal still refuses to clear.

LineManager is currently in active development. Some areas – including the vehicle market, staff and duty planning, maintenance, construction costs, audio and mod support – are still being expanded. The interface, visuals and individual game systems may also change significantly during development.

store_data.about_the_game:
Your calls. Your club. Your dynasty.

Not another arcade football game. You're the head coach. Call every offensive and defensive snap yourself, or set the plan and hand the headset to your coordinators. AI athletes execute 11-on-11 in readable Tactical 2D—you coach the club, you don't steer a player.

  • Call it or delegate it — Make sideline decisions play by play, or trust ranked coordinator recommendations with confidence and risk.
  • Watch every snap—or jump ahead — Live matchday, key-moment jumps, or sim ahead. Timeouts, pace (5 / 10 / 15-minute quarters), and staff advice when the drive matters.
  • Build the roster — Scout, draft, trade, and manage contracts under a $300M salary cap.
  • Run the club between Sundays — Depth chart, injuries, facilities, morale, chemistry, and coordinators who fit your scheme.
  • Chase a lasting dynasty — Sixteen fictional franchises in real American cities. Schedules, standings, playoffs, and franchise records across seasons.
  • Feel the broadcast — Gridiron Live openings, halftime, and postgame. Touchdown and first-down celebrations when you move the chains.
  • Play your way — Keyboard and mouse, plus Xbox and PlayStation-style controllers. Three local career slots with rolling save backups.

Coach every turning point

Read the defense. Weigh coordinator advice. Manage timeouts as 11-on-11 plays unfold in Tactical 2D. Watch live, jump to key moments, or simulate ahead—then adjust at the half.

Step into the broadcast booth

Gridiron Live brings your matchup into focus with an animated host, team comparisons, and players to watch. Opening, half, and postgame follow the story of the game.

Celebrate the big ones

Scoring plays get their own animated celebration—scorer spotlight, stadium confetti, first-down pops, and home sideline energy after the huge moments.



Build a club that lasts

Lead one of sixteen fictional franchises based in real American cities through multiple seasons. Shape your draft board, negotiate contracts and trades, keep payroll inside the cap, and hire the staff who fit how you want to play.




  • Roster management with contracts, injuries, and player development
  • Scouting, draft wishlists, free agency, and trade counteroffers
  • Coaching staff, facilities, morale, and chemistry
  • Schedules, standings, playoffs, and franchise records across seasons
  • Three local career slots with rolling save backups

Before you take the sideline

Do I directly control the athletes? No. You coach and manage the club; computer-controlled athletes execute your decisions on the field.

Can I choose the match pace? Choose 5, 10, or 15-minute quarters (game-clock settings, not a promise of real-world session length). Watch live, jump to key moments, or simulate ahead.

Is this multiplayer? Pocket Dynasty is a single-player coaching and franchise game.

What controls are supported? Keyboard and mouse, plus Xbox and PlayStation-style controller support across menus, play calling, matchday decisions, and franchise management.

A fictional football league

Pocket Dynasty uses fictional clubs, players, coaches, emblems, and competitions. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or licensed by any professional or collegiate league, club, athlete, or other football video game.

  • Scouting, draft wishlists, free agency, and trade counteroffers
  • Coaching staff, facilities, morale, and chemistry
  • Schedules, standings, playoffs, and franchise records across seasons
  • Three local career slots with rolling save backups

Do I directly control the athletes? No. You coach and manage the club; computer-controlled athletes execute your decisions on the field.

Can I choose the match pace? Choose 5, 10, or 15-minute quarters (game-clock settings, not a promise of real-world session length). Watch live, jump to key moments, or simulate ahead.

Is this multiplayer? Pocket Dynasty is a single-player coaching and franchise game.

What controls are supported? Keyboard and mouse, plus Xbox and PlayStation-style controller support across menus, play calling, matchday decisions, and franchise management.

A fictional football league

Pocket Dynasty uses fictional clubs, players, coaches, emblems, and competitions. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or licensed by any professional or collegiate league, club, athlete, or other football video game.

store_data.about_the_game:
Find the cursed objects hidden among your customers' belongings. The call is yours.

In a night district that still carries the atmosphere of old Japan, you inherit Hyakume Pawnshop from your missing uncle, Gensai Katori. You have three months to prepare 100,000 yen. The items brought through the door, however, include counterfeits, damaged antiques, and cursed objects that prey upon their owners.

Appraisal means measuring the object


Each of the five tools examines the item itself. What you find is the evidence.

  • Magnifying Glass — Magnify the surface and hunt for flaws. A miss still reports the distance to the nearest one. The number of flaws you find is the condition. But a cursed piece carries one mark that is not a flaw
  • Antique Ledger — Compare the item's stamp against the records, character by character. No matching record means a forgery
  • Spirit Mirror — Measure the residual reading and decide which band of the reference table it falls into. Only cursed things ring in the resonance band — though a quiet reading is no guarantee of safety
  • Incense Board — Draw the scent still clinging to the item and judge whether it comes from the material, from storage, or is something that belongs to neither
  • Seal Verifier — Compare the clay, the cord marks, and the wear against an intact reference. A single mismatch means the seal has been broken

Different objects reveal themselves to different tools. Some curses never show in the mirror.

Cursed, or ordinary — make the call


If you believe an item is cursed, you can say so and take it in.

  • Right — it stays with you as a vessel, usable once after closing. On the night of the full moon, only the objects you kept can break the barrier of the Hundred-Eyed Devourer
  • Wrong — you are holding an antique nobody wants, and it moves for 35% of what you paid

Reselling a curse turns a profit but erodes your sanity. Buy, refuse, or claim it as cursed — that judgment is the work of this shop.

The closing report reveals the truth of everything: what you bought and what you turned away. Whether you saw it, missed it, or wisely let it go.

The nights you choose add up


Four moments ask whether you press forward or hold the line. Your drift shows in the ledger each night and changes how the black market prices you, how well you are warded, and how far you can push a negotiation. And over twenty-one nights, your uncle's ledger reveals whose name is written in the column marked "next."

More than one run


  • Three difficulty tiers — Normal, Hard, and a Very Hard tier unlocked by the true ending
  • A hidden second-loop boss — Clear the game once and a second form waits on the final night
  • Endless Trade — Unlocked by the true ending. A tribute falls due every seventh night, and it never stops growing

Features


  • A 21-night loop divided into three seven-night months
  • 30 items, 12 customers, 17 black-market relics, and 4 permanent shop investments
  • Five hands-on appraisal minigames with 12 puzzle rule variants, generated from the item itself
  • One-time night events, three story routes, and four endings
  • Full controller support (D-pad/stick navigation throughout; L/R cycles appraisal tools)
  • Six original BGM tracks and 37 original sound effects
  • 23 achievements (13 hidden)
  • Full Japanese and English text support

But your car is always really there. It could be the next one you check… or almost the last.

movies.name: Night Shift Motel - Early Access Gameplay Trailer

store_data.about_the_game:
RUN THE MOTEL BY DAY. SURVIVE IT BY NIGHT.

Night Shift Motel is a first-person psychological horror and management game where you take over an isolated motel and learn that keeping the business running is only half the job.

During the day, welcome guests, listen to their stories, assign rooms, maintain the motel and decide who you can trust.

But when night falls, the motel changes.

Watch the security cameras. Investigate strange activity. Report anomalies. Repair broken equipment. Lock the doors when something feels wrong.

Some guests may be hiding more than they admit, and the details of their stories can matter. Pay attention to contradictions, unusual behavior and the things you discover around the motel before deciding who should stay.

MANAGE YOUR MOTEL

Accept guests, assign rooms and improve the motel as you build the business. Better rooms and equipment can increase the value of your property, but every new guest may also bring new problems.

WATCH THE CAMERAS

At night, CCTV becomes one of your most important tools. Monitor corridors and rooms for unusual activity, document anomalies before they disappear and respond when something damages the motel.

QUESTION WHO YOU TRUST

Guests have their own stories, requests and secrets. Listen carefully, investigate when something does not add up and decide whether allowing someone inside is worth the risk.

FACE THE SUPERNATURAL

Strange figures may appear where they should not be. Lights fail. Cameras break. Something may be watching from the edge of a doorway.

Sometimes seeing it is the easy part.

YOUR DECISIONS HAVE CONSEQUENCES

The people you admit, the dangers you ignore and the choices you make throughout your stay at the motel can change how your story unfolds.

store_data.about_the_game:
Two rivals. One revolver. No one knows what fires next.

Take a seat aboard the Last Round Express, racing through a stylized England in the early decades of the 20th century. Before every shot, gather information, disrupt your rival's plan, or build a combination of your own. Then choose: aim across the table, or risk a shot at yourself and keep the turn if the cartridge is blank.

You know the count. The order is hidden.

Whenever the revolver is loaded, both players see how many live rounds and blanks enter the cylinder. Their order stays hidden. Track what has already left the cylinder and reassess the risk after every shot. A blank fired at yourself keeps your turn; a live round costs one life. Aim at your rival—or take the risk for another move.

Turn chance into a plan with 15 abilities

Peek at the next or last cartridge, eject one, reshuffle the remaining cartridges without revealing their order, block the next live round your rival fires at you, or give the next live round a 50% chance to misfire regardless of who fires or whom they target. These are only some of the 15 abilities at your disposal. Play as many available cards as you like before the mandatory shot, and combine their effects to create an advantage your rival did not see coming.

Choose who sits across the table

Invite a friend to a private online duel, find a rival through public matchmaking, or play a complete solo match offline.

Win two rounds. Take the match.

Each player begins a round with 3 lives. Within that round, health and cards carry over from one load to the next. Later rounds bring larger loads and tougher decisions. The first player to win two rounds takes the match.
  • Private online duels with friends and public matchmaking
  • Full offline solo play
  • 15 distinct abilities whose effects can be combined
  • Short best-of-three matches
  • A stylized night train and original soundtrack
  • Game text available in 20 languages

store_data.about_the_game:
From one logic gate to a computer.


IT THINKS! is a hands-on hardware puzzle game about discovering how computers grow. Place parts, draw wires, watch signals move, and prove each design on a live test bench. Your first component is NAND: a tiny logic gate with two inputs and one decision. From there, your designs grow into arithmetic, memory, a programmable processor, parallel cores, matrix multiplication, and finally a chip that recognizes your handwritten digits.

Build it. Test it. Ship it.


  • Complete 36 handcrafted contracts across six eras, from a small workshop to an AI lab.
  • Turn working circuits into reusable chips and build a catalogue of components you designed yourself.
  • Program the hardware you built with a compact assembly language and run the same kernel across many cores.
  • Balance real architectural trade-offs such as area, ticks, memory bandwidth, power, and parallel efficiency.
  • Learn at your own pace with optional hints, the Master's Notebook, and skip tests for concepts you already know.
  • Make every solution yours with exportable die views and looping GIF captures.

No electrical-engineering background is required. Build by doing, inspect what happened, and improve the machine one clear step at a time.

Language support at launch: The interface, tutorials, and all in-game text will be available in all 15 languages listed on the store page.

We taught sand to think.

store_data.about_the_game:
Trucazo! is a fast-paced card game about bluffing, reading your opponent, and confidently making terrible decisions.

Inspired by the Argentine card game Truco, Trucazo! takes its core ideas and throws them into a strange elemental card game where Earth, Water, Fire, and Wind clash, interact, and occasionally ruin whatever plan you thought you had.

You get three cards. Your opponent gets three cards. That's probably enough.

PLAY YOUR HAND

Every card belongs to an element, and each element has its own advantages and disadvantages. Knowing what your cards can do is useful.

Convincing your opponent that you know what you're doing is even more useful.

CALL THEIR BLUFF

Winning isn't only about having the strongest cards.

Raise the stakes with Dares, fight for extra points with Synergy, bluff your way through a terrible hand, or confidently challenge someone who absolutely has better cards than you.

Sometimes it works.

SOMETHING IS A LITTLE OFF

You're playing cards against a strange robotic host in an abandoned office with no context in sight.

Why?

Good question.

Play some cards first.

CURRENTLY IN DEVELOPMENT

Trucazo is still being actively developed, so mechanics, visuals, content, and probably several questionable decisions are subject to change.

But the cards work.

Mostly.

store_data.about_the_game:
WALK YOUR OWN FACTORY FLOOR Phantom Tycoon is an idle tycoon you walk through. Stroll the line as machines drop, upgrade and ship your products, buy the next machine with a deliberate confirmed purchase - never by accident - and watch a dusty 1890s warehouse grow into a valley of ten factories that ends at a starforge in orbit.

A CENTURY OF INDUSTRY Every site is its own era: textile bales, blast-furnace ingots, coil works, motor lines, chip fabs, fusion cells, star alloy. Machines, products and music modernise with the century, and each era is drawn in hand-made pixel art.

SELL THE COMPANY. KEEP THE LEGACY. Restructure to sell everything for legacy shares: permanent revenue, perks, and a company ledger that remembers every firm you built and sold. Blueprints from finished sites let the next company open with machines already standing.

A CREW WITH FACES Hire Reyes, Hollis, Vance, Sokolov and Lin - the caretakers from the story - and post them to sites. Each one changes how their floor runs: cheaper machines, faster lines, richer contracts, more premium drops.

ALWAYS SOMETHING HAPPENING Golden rushes strike the machine next to you. Contracts arrive with deadlines and payouts. Boosts, daily returns, and 45 achievements. And when you put it down, the factory keeps earning - offline progress is counted and paid when you come back.

store_data.about_the_game:
Eldwyn's Dungeon Academy is a small action-adventure game. You are an adventurer in training. Having completed your first year at the Academy, it is time for your final exam. Enter the magical dungeon and use your skills to complete it.

You will collect your sword and dash ability at the start of the exam. As you explore the dungeons you will find additional tools. Some will be needed to complete the exam. Others will be optional, but can be very beneficial. The exam is broken up into different dungeons. You will start with access to 4 dungeons. You may go between them as you wish. You can choose to enter one and complete it in one go, or explore a bit and move on to others, returning later to finish it. There will be enemies to fight, traps to avoid, and puzzles to solve. Some dungeons may favor challenges of one type, or the other, and some will be a good mix of both. Explore the dungeons, solve puzzles, collect tools and other items, defeat the bosses of each, uncover secrets, and show your instructors what you have learned!

Note: This game is currently under development and this is an early version.

Controls can be seen by pausing while in game (Escape/P/Start). They can be remapped in the settings. Hold the "Use Tool" button when equipped with the Sword to charge up a Whirlwind attack. Can be played with keyboard, keyboard & mouse, or joypad.

store_data.about_the_game:
About the Game

Coffee Keeper is a cozy first-person organizing simulator set in a two-storey coffee house. The night's delivery has been scattered across the shop, and 4,179 bags, tins, bottles, cartons, brewing tools, pastries, chairs and more must be put back where they belong before morning.

Every item belongs to a marked family, and every fitting carries an engraved brass reference. Read the stock, find its bay and shelf, and turn complete chaos into perfect order.

Gameplay

Pick stock up by the armful, cycle through the stack in your hands, and carry each piece to its correct place. The coffee house itself is your guide: brass bay letters, engraved shelf plates, painted setting-out marks and a detailed plan help you navigate the building rather than follow a quest list.

Across 4,179 places, 267 rows and 76 fittings, you will restore everything from the wall displays and island gondolas to the working counter, glazed pastry case, green room and mezzanine. Even the chairs and window stools have a proper place.

Make the Coffee House Your Own

In Cozy mode, completed rows earn skill points. Unlock and improve seven helpful abilities across five levels to carry more, move faster, find missing pieces and make every route through the shop more efficient. There is no fail state: nothing breaks, nothing is lost and nothing chases you.

Prefer a challenge? Hardcore mode removes the help, starts the clock and records your finished nights on the leaderboard.

Features

  • Sort 4,179 pieces across one hand-built two-storey coffee house
  • Match every item to 267 marked rows using brass bay and shelf references
  • Carry up to ten pieces at once and cycle through the stack in your hands
  • Unlock and improve seven efficiency skills in relaxed Cozy mode
  • Race the clock in Hardcore mode and compete for a faster finishing time
  • Save your progress and return to the same night whenever you like
  • Steam Achievements, leaderboards and Cloud saves
  • Nine interface languages and full controller support

store_data.about_the_game:
Turn discoveries at the recipe table into a coordinated restaurant district. Cat's Fish Stall is a restaurant management game where every new dish opens a specialty shop and every operating choice leaves a visible result: shop order, facilities, and promotion hours reshape customer flow, sales momentum, and the performance of the whole district.

Visit the merchant, choose up to three ingredients, and pair them with grilling, boiling, frying, stir-frying, mixing, or chilling. Find 100 valid recipes, add each discovery to your collection, and unlock a matching specialty shop to build on the street.

Every new restaurant extends the street by one more lot. Decide what opens next and whether neighboring businesses support—or compete with—one another. Shop order matters: a decision made near the entrance can change what happens farther down the line.

For each shop, choose from facilities such as the Catwalk Takeout Counter, Cat-Tower Lounge, Heated Cushion Waiting Area, Catnip Garden, Pawprint Wayfinding Sign, and Canned Treat Display. Special events include New Menu Tasting, Timed Discount, Combo Menu Promotion, Alley Joint Promotion, Stamp Reward Campaign, and Pre-Order Sales.

Event time slots are Morning 05–09, Day 09–13, Afternoon 13–17, Evening 17–21, Night 21–01, and Late Night 01–05.

Choose freely between Campaign and Sandbox Mode from the start. Campaign offers eight stages with distinct market conditions and clear goals, while Sandbox lets you test your own shop order and operating plan without stage objectives. Whichever mode you choose, the route is yours: expand quickly, keep a focused lineup, specialize by time slot, or steer customers toward quieter shops.

Key features:

- 100 discoverable dishes built from varied ingredients and cooking methods

- A growing food district filled with visiting cats

- Shop-order strategy and facilities that affect neighboring customer flow

- Facilities, special events, and daily time slots, including neutral options

- Campaign and Sandbox Mode, both freely selectable from the start

- Operating choices that shape individual shops and the district as a whole

store_data.about_the_game:
The Super Seven is a mixed-media visual novel inspired by the colourful, energetic style of 1980s and 1990s sitcom television. The game blends a variety of visual styles, from traditional 2D animation to live-action sequences, creating an unpredictable experience where you never quite know what will come next.

At its heart, The Super Seven is a celebration of sitcoms, friendship, and the challenge of finding your place in the world. It explores a question that many of us face at some point: what does it really mean to be cool just after school? Sometimes, the lengths we go to in order to fit in, make friends, or prove ourselves can have explosive—and often unexpected—consequences.

The Super Seven follows Cheng, a new student who has recently moved to Sydney to begin university. As he tries to navigate an unfamiliar city and settle into university life, Cheng is quickly swept up by an eccentric group of seven students. Determined to make an unforgettable first impression, the group decides that the best way to make new friends is to throw a huge open-house party.

What begins as a simple plan to bring everyone together quickly spirals out of control. As the party gets underway, one disaster leads to another, and soon everything that could possibly go wrong does. With friendships tested, secrets revealed, and the night descending into complete chaos, Cheng finds himself caught in the middle of a group that is far more complicated—and far more entertaining—than he could have imagined.

Blending comedy, coming-of-age storytelling, live action, animation, and the exaggerated energy of classic sitcoms, The Super Seven introduces a group of characters learning that fitting in isn't always as easy as it looks.

This episode serves as the pilot for a longer-form series, establishing the characters, world, and comedic tone while setting the stage for the adventures—and disasters—that await the Super Seven.

store_data.about_the_game:
A high-speed auto-battle 3D crowd RTS.

There are two ways to play: **Auto War Mode**, where the battle unfolds in real time, and **Magic War Action Mode**, where you control the Orc Elder and cast spells.

In Magic War Action Mode, character combat proceeds automatically, while spells can be activated manually. The faster the girls move, the more difficult the battle becomes. Set the Movement speed to x3 and then increase it to x5, the setting immediately to its right, to reach the highest difficulty.

Real-Time Controls

ATK (Attack), DEF (Defense), and ATK Speed can be changed in real time, allowing you to influence the course of the battle as it unfolds.

If you prefer to watch the Auto War at a slower pace, set ATK Speed to around 0.333–1.

3D Crowd Animation

* Auto War: 500–1,200 characters

* Manual War (Magic War): 251–601 characters

* Legions: 176–250 units

Characters

* Girls: 8 types

* Orcs: 5 types

Maps

* 9 maps

Characters and Movement Speed

Map 1: Rin — Movement Speed 3

Map 2: Koharu — Movement Speed 8

Map 3: Saki — Movement Speed 6

Map 4: Shiori — Movement Speed 5

Map 5: All Stars!

Map 6: Aoi — Movement Speed 10

Map 7: Mika — Movement Speed 7

Map 8: Kaede — Movement Speed 9

Map 9: Chihiro — Movement Speed 4

*Map 5 features all girl characters.*

*Orc movement speed varies depending on the map.*

Configurable Options

1. Manual / Auto Mode

2. Skirmish / Battle / Mass Battle

* Character count, character size, and number of legions change.

3. Movement Speed

* Adjustable from x1 to x15

4. Damage ON / OFF

5. Smoke ON / OFF

6. Markers ON / OFF

7. Sound Effects ON / OFF

Language Selection

Switch between English and Japanese using the **“English / 日本語”** button in the bottom-left corner of the screen.

PC Requirements

A gaming PC or equivalent is recommended.

The 1 million grass and flowers used to create the atmosphere, along with the beautiful Weather System, are the main sources of performance load.

For the Weather System, changing **“Beautiful”** to **“Lite”** in the settings menu in the top-right corner of the screen may improve FPS.

Content Creation Guidelines

Gameplay videos and livestreams featuring this game are welcome. Both commercial and non-commercial use are permitted without prior approval.

**Note:** You are free to feature this game on blogs, social media, and other platforms, including the use of screenshots and videos, without any restrictions.

store_data.about_the_game:
A cyberpunk bullet heaven with loot worth discovering. Build something outrageous. Tear through the horde. Bring the good stuff home. Optimized for Steam Deck.

OUTBUILD THE HORDE




Start with one weapon. Stack upgrades, combine weapons with boosts, and unleash devastating evolutions. Turn a desperate fight for space into a crowd-clearing power trip.

Your weapons fire automatically. You steer the destruction. Pick an operator with a distinct starting weapon and signature ability, dodge through the swarm, and find the build that makes it all click.

EXPLORE THE SPRAWL




See a reward worth fighting for? Go get it. Trigger dynamic events, wipe out defenders, and crack open equipment chests. Hold a contested zone, chase a moving objective, or survive a fresh wave of enemies.

Push farther for tougher fights and a chance at stronger gear. Choose your detours, take on dangerous encounters, and put your build to the test.

FIND YOUR NEXT BUILD




Hunt for weapons, armor, and accessories with different combinations of bonuses. Discover unique items with special effects, compare your finds, and equip the gear that gives your build something new.

A great drop is more than a reward for this run. Get it home and make it part of the next one. Try another operator, combine different equipment, and see what you can build around your latest find.

BRING THE LOOT. COME BACK STRONGER.




Found something you want to keep? Extract early to secure your haul, or push on and fight for the final lift. Die before you get out and that run's carried gear is lost. Equipment already secured stays yours.

Equip your finds, buy permanent upgrades, and jump back into the horde. Normal missions reach final extraction at ten minutes. How much you risk before then is up to you.

store_data.about_the_game:
GRIMLIFE

An open-world survival RPG set in a post-apocalyptic zombie-infested world. Meet fellow survivors, develop your character, and learn how to survive as you explore the world after a viral outbreak leads to the end of civilization.

Single-Player

The game is a single-player experience, set in a large open-world area. For the sake of the simplicity and embracing limited, achievable scope there are no plans to make this into a multi-player experience. There are many games that occupy this territory and the intention of this project is to deliver a great single-player experience.

CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION

Character customization is a key feature in roleplaying games. Choose a variety of character models and an assortment of colors to customize your character. Further customize your character by spending attribute points and increasing skill values to help you survive.

DYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT

Featuring a dynamic weather system, players will encounter a variety of weather conditions to navigate through. The world operates under a 24 hour day and night cycle. 

LIVELY CHARACTERS

Characters will do more than bark the same voice lines on repeat. The game will have a wide cast of interesting and unique characters to meet and interact with. Each character has their own interests, hobbies, and routine. Spending time with the world's characters is a core part of GRIMLIFE. 

SURVIVAL MECHANICS

Combat in the game will be a variety of melee, guns, and crafted items, along with using medical supplies such as bandages, medical kits, and other items to help the player survive. There will be three main types of enemies, humans, animals, and zombies. Within each main type, there will be subtypes of enemies that have their own unique identity.

store_data.about_the_game:
TamerTamer is a 2D roguelite action game where you collect, fuse, and raise monsters,

then form a party with your raised monsters to battle.

Aim to become the ultimate Tamer alongside over 100 unique monsters!

Simple-to-control 2D roguelite action

Combat controls consist mainly of the following four actions:

・Movement via WASD keys

・Emergency dodge via the Space key

・Skill activation via Left-Click

・Switching to a reserve monster via Right-Click

(There are also basic attacks that trigger automatically when you get close to enemies.)

No complex inputs are required, yet you can enjoy flashy and deep combat.

Collect monsters!

Win battles to recruit the monsters you fought as allies.

Collect a wide variety of monsters!

There are over 100 types of monsters, each with unique skills and traits.

Make full use of these skills and traits in battle to mow down approaching enemies.

Fuse monsters to create new ones!

"Monster Fusion" is one of the game's core features.

By fusing two different monsters, you can create a completely new and unique monster.

Additionally, when fusing, you can inherit one basic attack, one skill, and one trait from the material monsters.

Inherited basic attacks and skills trigger in a chain alongside the monster's innate attacks and skills.

Furthermore, fusing monsters increases their "+ value."

This "+ value" can be allocated as bonus points to the monster's stats.

Raise your own unique monsters through inheritance and stat bonuses from "+ values"!

Form a party with your monsters!

You can organize a party of up to four monsters you've raised.

Switch between your party members during battle.

Even in situations a single monster can't handle alone, you can overcome them with the help of your allies!

Strengthen your monsters further with weapons and badges!

As you adventure, you may obtain weapons and badges.

Weapons come with enchantments that, when equipped by a monster, can boost its stats

or grant it access to unique abilities.

Enchantments are assigned randomly, but you can also add new ones at your base.

Acquire or forge the ultimate weapons to make your monsters even stronger!

Badges, on the other hand, are equipped by the party as a whole;

equipping one strengthens every monster in your party.

Empower your monsters further with weapons and badges!
