store_data.about_the_game:
[h2]A garden, and whoever calls at it[/h2]

Sweet Street is a quiet game about an Edwardian front garden and the animals that wander into it. You put things out — a saucer, a wicker basket, a boot scraper, a bee skep — and then you wait. Cats come over the fence. Which ones come, and how long they stay, depends on what is out and on what you have worked out about them.

Nothing here is timed against you. The garden carries on while you are away, and coming back is how you find out what happened.

[h2]What you do[/h2]

[list]

[*][b]Set the garden out.[/b] Eighty objects, each one a different invitation. Some are beds, some are food, some are simply odd enough to be worth investigating.

[*][b]Notice things.[/b] Thirty cats, each with her own likings, and nobody tells you what they are. The catalogue writes pencil notes only from visits you actually saw, and the shopkeeper's gossip about each object is the other half of the puzzle.

[*][b]Feed them.[/b] Kitchen scraps bring the ordinary cats of the street, reliably. A tin of sardines brings the ones from further off. A saucer of cream brings the fussy and the well-kept.

[*][b]Collect.[/b] An animal that visits often enough leaves you a keepsake. The catalogue fills. So does the shelf.

[/list]

[h2]Nine places[/h2]

The garden is where it starts. There is a parlour with a fire in it, a bedroom where the cats that know the house settle on the quilt, a park with a bandstand, a wood where the dog is properly walked, a farm with ponies in knitted jumpers, and a glass lean-to you build yourself — where the rain runs down the panes and none of it gets in.

[h2]The year turns[/h2]

Seasons pass in fortnights. Snow settles for the whole of winter. Cold weather makes visitors stay longer. A wet week used to be a dead week — until the glasshouse is built, and then it is the reason the garden is full.

[h2]Every voice is made from scratch[/h2]

There are no sample libraries in Sweet Street. Every meow, bark, whinny and piece of birdsong is synthesised from published measurements of how those animals make sound: vocal fold length, the resonances of the throat, and the way roughness arrives in short bursts at the peak of effort rather than running all the way through a call. It is why a big dog and a small dog sound like different animals rather than the same animal pitched down.

The music is the real thing — public-domain Edwardian compositions and recordings, heard through a wall, under rain, from the next room.

[h2]What this game will not do to you[/h2]

[list]

[*]Nothing dies, nothing is punished, and being away never costs you anything.

[*]No energy bar, no lives, no timer running down while you are not looking.

[*]No advertising.

[*]Money buys pennies and commissions, and nothing else. Every catalogue entry, every keepsake and every rare animal's conditions are unreachable with money — not as a promise in a document, but as a property of the code, with a test suite that fails if it ever stops being true.

[/list]

While fending off attacks from hostile forces, use boost mode to reach the next space station within the time limit.

The last lights still burn. The dead do not rest.

Hold the Dawn is a 3D tower defense game set in a post-apocalyptic wasteland. By day, you rebuild and expand your stronghold. By night, the horde comes. Choose a hero with a distinct fighting style—they battle on their own while you command the defense: place towers, shape the battlefield, and keep the base standing until sunrise.

A Day to Build. A Night to Survive.

Daylight is scarce. Use it to raise defenses, deploy towers, and upgrade your base before the next assault. Every placement is a bet on how the night will unfold—choke points, overlapping fire, fallback lines.

When darkness falls, zombies surge across the wastes. Your towers open fire. Your hero auto-fights in the thick of the swarm. Cut them down, hold the line, and make it to dawn.

Heroes Who Fight. You Who Decide.

Each survivor brings a different edge to the field. Unlock new heroes and grow their abilities as you progress, so the next night starts stronger than the last. You set the plan. They hold it.

Towers With Tactical Weight

A varied arsenal of defensive structures—damage, control, and support—meant to be combined, not stacked blindly. The right layout breaks a wave. The wrong one collapses.

Hold the Line Together

Play solo, or defend the base with friends. Local, LAN, or Steam online.

  • Distinct auto-fighting heroes

  • Tactical defensive towers

  • Satisfying horde-clearing combat

store_data.about_the_game:
Survive. Explore. Arm yourself. Build. Don’t let this world take you.

VELKOR is a harsh survival game set in a dangerous world where every expedition could be your last. Abandoned territories hide resources, weapons, hostile camps, infected creatures, and threats that cannot always be overcome by brute force.

Monitor your character’s condition, gather supplies, craft equipment, reinforce your shelter, complete missions, and gradually grow stronger. You can explore the world on foot, by land vehicle, or from the air—but the farther you go, the more dangerous the journey home becomes.

Survive the world

Hunger, thirst, temperature, toxicity, oxygen levels, and stamina directly affect your survival. Weather and environmental conditions can inflict negative effects, forcing you to change your route, equipment, and tactics.

Run, crouch, go prone, peek around cover, slide, swim, climb, and use vehicles to explore the world.

Weapons

At your disposal are more than 25 types of weapons: assault rifles, rifles, pistols, melee weapons, bows, explosives, RPGs, and much more.

Customize your weapons with modifications, monitor their condition, and manage your ammunition. Realistic recoil, weapon movement, aiming, and fully functional optics make every firefight feel more physical and intense.

The damage system accounts for hits to different body parts, critical strikes, and headshots.

ENEMIES

You are not the only one trying to survive.

Infected creatures, armed bandits, and other enemies use a perception system, react to noise and movement, become suspicious, and can search for you after detecting your presence.

Use stealth, tall grass, and the environment to avoid unnecessary confrontations.

But some enemies require an entirely different approach.

You will face powerful bosses, including a devastating mechanical spider with destructible body components.

BUILD & CRAFT


Gather resources throughout the world and turn them into weapons, tools, equipment, and essential survival items.

Use:

• an advanced inventory and equipment system
• quick slots and storage containers
• workbenches and production stations
• crafting queues
• equipment repair and dismantling
• fuel-powered processing stations

Build your own base using a construction system with object previews and snap-based placement.

Install doors and locks, upgrade structures, repair damage, and protect your territory from unwanted visitors.

EXPLORE

The world of VELKOR is filled with resources, points of interest, enemy camps, and interactive objects.

Gather resources, farm, fish, pick locks, search for valuable loot, and hunt for cargo dropped from the air.

For long expeditions, use vehicles with fuel systems, damage mechanics, and passenger seats.

And when the roads are no longer enough, take to the skies in a helicopter equipped with a searchlight and an emergency evacuation system.

Quest

Complete missions, earn experience, and unlock new abilities through the skill tree.

Meet characters, talk to them, trade, and make decisions through a branching dialogue system. Some encounters may lead to new missions, rewards, or alter the path ahead.

Customization

Customize your character’s appearance and observe them from more than just a first-person perspective.

VELKOR supports a fully modeled character body, first and third-person views, male and female characters, Groom hairstyles, facial expressions, and extensive customization.

The world of VELKOR is not waiting for a hero.

It is waiting for someone who can survive one more day.

Run, crouch, go prone, peek around cover, slide, swim, climb, and use vehicles to explore the world.

Weapons

At your disposal are more than 25 types of weapons: assault rifles, rifles, pistols, melee weapons, bows, explosives, RPGs, and much more.

Customize your weapons with modifications, monitor their condition, and manage your ammunition. Realistic recoil, weapon movement, aiming, and fully functional optics make every firefight feel more physical and intense.

The damage system accounts for hits to different body parts, critical strikes, and headshots.

ENEMIES

You are not the only one trying to survive.

Infected creatures, armed bandits, and other enemies use a perception system, react to noise and movement, become suspicious, and can search for you after detecting your presence.

Use stealth, tall grass, and the environment to avoid unnecessary confrontations.

But some enemies require an entirely different approach.

You will face powerful bosses, including a devastating mechanical spider with destructible body components.

BUILD & CRAFT


Gather resources throughout the world and turn them into weapons, tools, equipment, and essential survival items.

Use:

• an advanced inventory and equipment system
• quick slots and storage containers
• workbenches and production stations
• crafting queues
• equipment repair and dismantling
• fuel-powered processing stations

Build your own base using a construction system with object previews and snap-based placement.

Install doors and locks, upgrade structures, repair damage, and protect your territory from unwanted visitors.

EXPLORE

The world of VELKOR is filled with resources, points of interest, enemy camps, and interactive objects.

Gather resources, farm, fish, pick locks, search for valuable loot, and hunt for cargo dropped from the air.

For long expeditions, use vehicles with fuel systems, damage mechanics, and passenger seats.

And when the roads are no longer enough, take to the skies in a helicopter equipped with a searchlight and an emergency evacuation system.

Quest

Complete missions, earn experience, and unlock new abilities through the skill tree.

Meet characters, talk to them, trade, and make decisions through a branching dialogue system. Some encounters may lead to new missions, rewards, or alter the path ahead.

Customization

Customize your character’s appearance and observe them from more than just a first-person perspective.

VELKOR supports a fully modeled character body, first and third-person views, male and female characters, Groom hairstyles, facial expressions, and extensive customization.

The world of VELKOR is not waiting for a hero.

It is waiting for someone who can survive one more day.
store_data.short_description: VELKOR is a large-scale open-world survival experience where every decision can mean the difference between life and death. Build your base, craft your gear, master brutal combat, explore a ruined world, and uncover the truth buried beneath the remains of VELKOR.

“There is a sinner among the girls.”

A young man awakens in a special facility known as “Paradise,” but he has lost all of his memories.
He doesn’t know who he is—or why he was brought here.

Paradise is home to patients suffering from “Fairy Tale Syndrome.” Each girl believes she is a character from a fairy tale, living according to her own “Bible.”

Then, one day, the boy discovers a mysterious sketchbook in his room.

There is only one sentence written inside:

“There is a sinner among the girls.”

Who wrote these words?
And who is the “sinner”?

Meanwhile, a young doctor named Ikeno meets Dorothy, a girl whose “Bible” is The Wizard of Oz.

To cheer her up, Ikeno begins playing the role of one of her “Three Companions.”

But this seemingly kind gesture causes Dorothy’s fantasies to spiral out of control.

And the once-peaceful “Paradise” begins to show strange and inexplicable abnormalities.

Game Features

  • 🕯️ Dark Fairy Tale × Psychological Mystery

  • 📖 A world where reality and fantasy intertwine

  • 🧩 Hidden clues and carefully placed foreshadowing

  • 👧 Every girl has a secret of her own

  • ⚙️ A slowly collapsing “Paradise” and a mystery waiting to be uncovered

The ending of the fairy tale has already been written. So… are you brave enough to rewrite it?

Add to your wishlist and uncover the truth.

store_data.about_the_game:
King Ewich of Eswahr has grown weak, but still he endures. The Land yearns for renewal, its calls unanswered. Until one day, out of the swirling mists of possibiity that surround the Kingdom's borders, steps a Hero named "Wille", destined to change everything.

Eswahr Eternal is a Fantasy role-playing-game with turn-based combat and random encounters. Alone, you will wander the undying lands of Eswahr, in search for the power to become King.

Features:

  • A space to make mistakes

    Things will go wrong and you will end up in uncomfortable situations. Embrace it.

  • A completely open world

    You can go anywhere you want. Whether or not this is a good idea is a different question.

  • Open ended battle-system

    You want to put an awful status effect on a Boss? The game will likely let you do that. With luck, you might even get access to every attack the game has to offer.

  • Fast, but difficult combat

    Random Encounters are designed to be over quickly, regardless of outcome.

  • (Almost) no failure state

    Losing a battle will not always sent you back to your last point of rest. As long as you have the Potential, you will be able to move forward.

  • A chance to create your own Kingdom

    Choose which of your five principles to sacrifice for power, and which one to hold on to. At the end, your last principle might shape the nature of your Kingdom.

  • Potential instead of Money

    Potential keeps you going when you fail, but it can also be used to prepare powerful Words

  • Words instead of items

    Words are powerful abilities that you can prepare ahead of time, or 'purchase' directly in battle.

  • Only one town in the entire world

    Kings don't need Inns

Some Numbers:

  • Lots of very cute rodents to hunt for their Potential.

  • Around 8 hours of playtime, depending on how lost you'll get

  • 4 main Dungeons

  • 60+ enemies to fight

  • 20+ different abilities

  • 6 different weapons to find

  • 12 Different accessories to find

  • 13 kinds of Misfortune to suffer from

  • 4 directional movement

  • 2 frames of animation

  • 1 King

  • 0 Tutorial

5198450.name: Ramen Shop in the Floating Slums

store_data.about_the_game:
Start Another Life, One Bowl at a Time

After losing your job and nearly every penny to your name, you find yourself in a floating slum. Scrounging together makeshift equipment and a handful of ingredients, you open a tiny ramen shop in a back alley.

Ramen Shop in a Floating Slum is a first-person ramen shop management and life sim where you develop your own ramen, grow your business, and experience another life in a city on the water.

Create Your Own Ramen

Combine pork bones, chicken bones, seafood, aromatic vegetables, and other ingredients, then take the time to simmer them into a flavorful broth.

Choose your noodles and their firmness, tare seasoning, flavored oil, and toppings to develop ramen that is truly your own.

Give each finished bowl a name and set its price. Learn your customers’ preferences, keep up with changing trends, and serve even better ramen.

Earn Money and Grow Your Shop

You begin with a tiny street stall tucked away in an alley. Save the money you earn from selling ramen, then buy ingredients, equipment, and decorations to build a shop that feels like your own.

As you progress, you will be able to move into new locations around the city. Expand into a larger shop or stay somewhere you have grown attached to—the choice is yours.

Explore the Floating Slum

Step away from the counter and freely explore a maze-like city of waterways and densely packed buildings.

Visit food suppliers, equipment stores, fishing shops, fishing spots, and waste disposal sites. Buy supplies, go fishing, scavenge discarded items, and search the city for your next shop location.

You may also discover unexpected items and scenic spots that become your favorite places in the city.

Ramshackle, yet inviting enough to explore on a day off—enjoy the lived-in atmosphere of a Japanese-inspired neighborhood combined with the unfamiliar beauty of a city built on water.

Connect with the City Through Ramen

As you run your ramen shop, you will meet people who call the city home, including an inspector from the Entertainment Audit Bureau and a fishing engineer.

Serve them ramen and deepen your relationships to uncover their individual stories. As you grow closer, they may give you useful items—and eventually even lend a hand at your shop.

Build a Shop and a Life of Your Own

Pursue the perfect bowl. Create the ramen you love. Build an efficient kitchen. Open your shop in your favorite location and wander the city between shifts.

Step away from reality for a little while and begin another life running a ramen shop in this floating city.

Stinky Tofu: Kitchen Survivor is a kitchen horde survivor 1.0. You’re a block of tofu that wants to live—survive waves of ingredient foes in a kitchen that cheats. Master the signature loop: hit the same foe with fire + ice to shatter. Learn that first, then push deeper.

Each run is one stage. Clear it to unlock the next. Finish all ten floors, then dive into Endless. Stages rewrite your movement logic in one line—run sideways like you’re chopping; walk straight and you’re on the cutting board.

Included

  • Signature core: fire + ice shatter, ten stages + Endless

  • Cursed food-cart contracts: risk for reward mid-run

  • Rush hour: prep / late-night peaks when the kitchen suddenly gets busy

  • Streamer chaos (optional / toggleable): Twitch or offline simulation

  • 16 unlockable tofu heroes with unique passives (feel polish ongoing)

content_descriptors.notes:
This is a cartoon-style kitchen horde-survival game with fantasy combat. Players fight mutant food enemies using kitchen utensils and cooking-themed weapons. Defeat effects may include stylized food juices and splatters (sometimes red), which can resemble non-realistic blood.

The tone includes dark kitchen comedy: enemies are “cooked” into dishes, critic characters use sharp roasting humor, and themes such as fermentation, rotting food, and kitchen chaos appear throughout.

Mild alcohol references appear in flavor text and setting (e.g. an izakaya-style restaurant and cooking-wine themed enemies). There is no realistic depiction of drinking, drug use, sexual content, sexual violence, self-harm, or graphic realistic gore.

Venture beyond Base Camp into a vibrant but dangerous fantasy wilderness. Fight hostile creatures, gather loot, and bring your earnings back before the day runs out. Sell what you find, stock up at the shop, strengthen your weapons at the blacksmith, and unlock new routes through ancient portals.

Every day comes with a payment that must be made to the Mage. Submit enough gold during the day to raise the Due. Submit it at night and the Due falls instead. Miss the deadline, and the penalty is twice as severe. Plan your route, decide when to return, and do not let one bad night undo the work of the whole party.

store_data.about_the_game:
Three players. Sixteen cards. Who goes out first?

Every card you play brings you closer to victory—but the order matters. PaoDeKuai is a three-player shedding card game where each player starts with 16 cards. The player holding the 3 of Hearts leads, and the first to empty their hand wins.

Take control of the table now, or hold a combination for later? Plan your plays, respond to your opponents, and find a way to get those last cards out.

Practice solo. Challenge your friends.

Play against computer opponents whenever you want a solo game. Choose normal bots for a relaxed match, or challenge a harder opponent powered by a local decision-making model.

For a game with friends, create or join a three-player Steam friend room using a four-digit room number. Add an optional password to keep your table private.

Keep your focus on the cards

Use hints to find a playable move and arrange your hand by rank or card combination. Keyboard shortcuts help you act quickly, while optional auto-play can take over when you need it. If you have no legal response, the game passes automatically.

Find the right combination

Play singles, pairs, triples with attachments, straights, consecutive pairs, airplanes, four-of-a-kind with attachments, and bombs. Decide how to use each combination—and what to leave in your hand for the next turn.

Make the table your own

Choose from the available avatars, table backgrounds, card styles, and music to personalize your games. Play with a Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, or English interface.

Features

• Three-player games with 16 cards per player.
• Single-player matches against normal or hard computer opponents.
• Steam friend rooms with four-digit room numbers and optional passwords.
• Hints, keyboard shortcuts, optional auto-play, and automatic passing when no legal move is available.
• Hand sorting by rank or card combination.
• Selectable avatars, table backgrounds, card styles, and music.
• Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, and English language support.

store_data.about_the_game:
9 Box — a chaotic party game where even death isn't the end.

Ten players enter the arena. Only nine boxes appear. Grab one, pick your ability, aim fast — because in five seconds, everyone acts at once, and the arena will never be the same.

9 Box is a fast, chaotic party battler for up to 10 players. Every round is a mad scramble: move, grab a box, choose one of two abilities inside it, and lock in your target — all in seconds. Then everything resolves simultaneously. Rockets get blown off course by wind. Fire gets doused by water. Walls turn a shove into a knockout. No two rounds play out the same way twice.

Survival isn't the goal — score is. Land smart hits, heal an ally at the right moment, dodge a killing blow, or turn a Neutral ability into a game-changing combo. The last player standing gets a bonus, but they won't automatically win the match.

And dying doesn't take you out of the fight. Fall in battle and you become a Grave — still mobile, still able to mess with the living using a hidden effect only you can see. Even from the grave, you're still playing for score.

Key Features:

  • 10-player free-for-all — fast matches, roughly 5-8 minutes each

  • Grab, Choose, Aim, Resolve — a tight round structure where every ability fires at the exact same moment

  • Deep ability interactions — Wind bends Rockets off course, Water extinguishes Fire, Push sends enemies crashing into Walls, and Tornadoes redirect projectiles mid-flight

  • Score over survival — win by playing smart, not just by staying alive

  • The Grave System — death isn't the end; dead players keep moving, keep scoring, and keep influencing the match through a hidden effect

  • No dominant strategy — abilities rotate so you're never stuck spamming the same move, and power always depends on positioning, timing, and context

  • Stylized 3D toy-world art style — battle it out across a kid's bedroom rug, scaled up like a living toy diorama, with cinematic lighting and vivid VFX

store_data.about_the_game:
PASS THE EMBER OR BLOW UP

A statue spits out a burning Ember. Grab it and RUN.

You can only hold the Ember for 10 seconds before it blows up in your hands and stuns you. Pass it, throw it across the room, or make it somebody else's problem.

Keep the Ember alive for 5 minutes and the Tricksters win. Let the Wardens destroy it, and you're done.

TRICKSTER OR WARDEN?

As a tiny Trickster, keep the Ember moving, dodge the Warden, and work with or completely screw over your friends to survive the round.

As an armed Warden, enter the hunt 10 seconds later. Track the Tricksters with your scanner and land 7 shots on the Ember before the timer runs out.

FIGHT DIRTY

Choose your abilities before the round and ruin somebody's day.

Grapple away from danger. Throw mud in the Warden's face. Leave banana peels and tripwires behind you.

Or, as the Warden, teleport through portals, drop rat traps, throw electric grenades, and trick players with squeaky-hammer illusions.

Launch yourself across rooms with bounce pads, cool the Ember using vents, or freeze it on a heatsink to buy your team precious time.

TINY PLAYERS, GIANT WORLD

Run across oversized furniture, squeeze through hidden passages, launch yourself across rooms, and use multiple traversal routes to lose whoever's chasing you.

Bright, hand-painted environments are packed with shortcuts, hiding spots, and ways to cause trouble.

SCREAM AT YOUR FRIENDS

Bring up to 10 players into customizable online lobbies, decide how many Wardens you want, and then immediately regret inviting everyone.

Proximity voice chat means the screaming gets louder as somebody gets closer, and quieter as your friends abandon you with a burning Ember in your hands.

LOOK RIDICULOUS

Every round and every win gives you experience. Keep playing to unlock unique head, back, body, and leg cosmetics, plus titles, and build the most unhinged Trickster or Warden you can.

No microtransactions. Everything is unlocked through gameplay.

FEATURES:

  • Online multiplayer for up to 10 players

  • Asymmetric PvP: Tricksters vs. armed Wardens

  • 3 Game Modes: Hot Potato, Infection, and Mole (Impostor)

  • Proximity voice chat

  • Giant hand-painted environments with multiple traversal routes

  • Wild abilities, traps, gadgets, and movement tools

  • Interactive bounce pads, cooling vents, and heatsinks

  • Gain experience to unlock cosmetics and titles

store_data.about_the_game:
Cute toys. Heavy machinery. No survivors.


PLOW is a fast side-scrolling action roguelite about driving an armed snowplow through a possessed toy apocalypse. Hold the road against waves of corrupted Christmas toys, intercept their arcing attacks, and turn every opening into a crushing counterattack.

Weaponize the Winter


Unload a high-rate candy-cane minigun, arc globs from the Frosting Sprayer, or chain a Tinsel Tesla beam through dangerous targets. Every weapon builds heat, so reckless fire turns the mount red and forces a smoky cooldown at the worst possible moment.

Charge the PLOW


Shoot hostile candy, fruit, ornaments, and other festive ammunition out of the air to charge the PLOW meter. When it is ready, become briefly unstoppable and drive across most of the battlefield, smashing everything in your path before reversing back into position.

Build a Better Snowplow

Peephole Talk is a first-person psychological horror thriller that puts you in the middle of an ordinary night that quickly becomes anything but ordinary.

  • Immersive horror : No need for constant action. Sometimes, anticipation is the scariest part.

store_data.about_the_game:
[h2]THE CITY IS THEIRS. TAKE IT BACK.[/h2]

A swarm of unmanned drones has occupied the airspace above the city. They fly in formation, they break when you close in, and the ones you leave alive land on rooftops and start shooting back.

You have one drone. Go and get them.

[h2]HUNT, DON'T RACE[/h2]

No checkpoints, no lap times. Every mission is a pursuit: close the distance, hold the lock, and put them down before they put you down. Machine gun for the ones in front of you, missiles for the ones weaving through the skyline.

[list]

[*][b]Lock-on missiles[/b] — hold the reticle long enough to acquire, then let the missile do the chasing

[*][b]Sustained machine gun[/b] — for when the target is close and you want it personal

[*][b]Radar and threat indicators[/b] — because a drone that breaks hard is a drone you will lose

[/list]

[h2]60 MISSIONS. SIX SKIES.[/h2]

Three cities, an open sea, a desert and a mountain range. The environment changes what a chase means — canyons to lose them in, open water with nowhere to hide.

[list]

[*][b]60 hand-tuned missions[/b] with a campaign map and star ratings

[*][b]Four boss craft[/b] — a carrier, a gunship, a stealth interceptor and a bomber, each laying mines you have to fly through

[*][b]Rooftop turrets[/b] from the mid-campaign on: leave a drone alive and it becomes a gun emplacement you have to route around

[*][b]Eight flyable drones[/b], unlocked as you play

[/list]

[h2]SCORED ON MARKSMANSHIP[/h2]

Stars are earned on accuracy, not speed. Finishing a mission is one star. Hitting what you aim at is three.

[h2]BUILT FOR PC[/h2]

[list]

[*]Full gamepad and keyboard support

[*]Resolution and fullscreen options, borderless or windowed

[*]No online requirement — the whole campaign plays offline

[*]No microtransactions, no ads

[/list]

store_data.about_the_game:
Gods of Earth is a dynamic action game, a gripping adventure into the secrets of the world, guarded by a force invisible to humanity. You play as an ancient God who finds himself on a planet ruled by the gods of a dark world. You must understand the methods of human control in order to help the inhabitants of Earth. The main problem is that the local inhabitants will defend the established order with their lives. You will have to fight the rulers of the dark world, embarking on a thrilling journey to discover the truth and tell it to the people. Download the game and begin to uncover the truth for yourself and those around you!

What to Expect From the Game

• Dynamic Third-Person Action

• Enemies – ordinary people connected to energy-draining parasites

• Sword fights and magical techniques

• Obtaining ancient knowledge through TV and radio sources implemented in the game

• Any similarities to real life are considered fictional by the author

store_data.about_the_game:
MAKE IT MOVE


Every machine begins with a simple question: what should happen next?

In IT MOVES!, you build the answer. Connect sensors, filters, controllers, and motors in a visual signal graph. Run the machine, read its telemetry, find what went wrong, and tune the design until it survives the test bench.

FROM ONE PISTON TO A HUMANOID


Start in a small repair shop with a single conveyor piston. Across 25 handcrafted contracts and six eras of robotics, your work grows into wheeled couriers, autonomous navigation systems, articulated arms, balancing machines, and finally a two-legged humanoid that can walk onto a stage.

Each new idea grows from something you already understand. Proportional control becomes PID. Wheel motion becomes odometry. Two joints become inverse kinematics. Balance becomes gait. You do not memorize a textbook—you make a machine move, watch it fail, and understand why.

BUILD, RUN, READ, TUNE


  • Wire readable, reusable control systems with a visual node editor.
  • Watch deterministic simulations and inspect live telemetry.
  • Test one design against several scenarios before delivery.
  • Turn successful solutions into modules you can reuse later.
  • Meet noise, drift, saturation, unstable control, and reward hacking in practical form.
  • Learn at your own pace in a warm workshop story—no engineering degree required.

There is no single magic solution. A machine that works once may fail under a heavier load, a noisier sensor, or a different floor. The satisfying part is not merely passing—it is knowing why your robot moved.

store_data.about_the_game:
100 Years atop Mount Ellumbee is a turn-based strategy game where up to six factions fight over one mountain for a century. It is a board game at heart. I designed it as one, with a real board and real cards, and then used my good bud Claude to build this version so that people could play it without me having to print everything.

You pick a faction, claim Provinces on the mountain, build up your economy, research, and fight your neighbors in a series of Battle Card exchanges. These activities earn Legacy Points. The player with the most Legacy Points at the end of the century wins. Legacy Points are never lost, so every one you earn is yours for good.

The Mountain: The game board consists of three rings of Provinces around the most valuable Province, the Summit. The game board grows and shrinks depending on the number of players, with the maximum game board involving Seventy-two uniquely-named Provinces.

A turn. Everyone takes their turn at the same time, so nobody waits around. In one turn you can:

  • Claim a new Province.

  • Take a market action (buy a new Battle Card, pick up a Liberty for certain advantages, or use the Forge to make a card you already own stronger).

  • Build and research. Extraction Sites pay you every round, Barracks unlock market actions, a Monument scores Legacy Points at the end of the game. Complete research tasks to unlock additional advantages: a second Commander, cheaper cards, free marching, and many more.

  • March your Commanders as far as you can afford.

  • Declare War, or don't. Declaring is secret, and the order people declare in is the order they fight in. Declare first and gain the Momentum of battle.

The game uses two resources, gold and materials. Players need both throughout the game. Materials are capped and can be wasted. Gold accumulates and adds to a player's end-game score.

The fight. Every War is settled the same way, in a Battle Card duel I call an Engagement.

Players each hold a hand of Battle Cards, select one to play during each Battle Card Exchange, and reveal them at the same moment. The Battle Card with the higher Force wins the Exchange, and Battle Card text applies to sway the battle. A battle tracker called the "Standard" moves along the battle board (the "Tide of Battle") so players can visualize the battle's progression.

Card effects control the battle. Some hold the line even when they lose. Some pay their holder. Some reach across the field and weaken what your opponent plays next. Commanders have a reaction that can be used to affect the battle; Liberties are one-shot cards that can be played to do the same.

Players' Battle Card hands start small, at 5 cards, and grow as the game progresses through the Eras of the Century.

Six factions, and none of them play alike

Everybody's board is identical. Nobody's deck is. There are 168 Battle Cards in the game, 28 to a faction, and each faction is built around one idea:

  • The Metal Munchkins hold ground and get paid for it.

  • The Haymakers hit the hardest.

  • The Crones lose ground slowly and take it back forever.

  • The Featherweights have low Force and high evasion. They reverse the Tide instead of winning it.

  • The Diehards replenish their hand. Their best cards keep coming back.

  • The Weasels win with small cuts.

Battle Cards also read the field, and have secondary effects that trigger depending on what has been played earlier during the Engagement. So no two fights are alike.

Ways to play

  • Against the computer at four difficulty levels, with three to six factions at the table.

  • Online with friends through Steam. Create a table, invite people from your friends list, and everyone picks their own chair and faction. The game starts when everybody says they are ready.

  • The Ladder, a two-player match that is all duel and no map: best of seven Engagements, with new Battle Cards and Liberties to buy between fights. Around twenty minutes.

  • Three game lengths . The full 27 round Century, two-thirds of the century (18 rounds), or a nine-round evening.

  • Turning Peak, a variant where the inner ring of the mountain rotates every round once anyone takes a Province on it.

  • A guided tutorial for each game, with a coach who talks you through your first fight in his own voice (and what a wonderful voice it is!).

  • Achievements. 23 achievements to earn.

How long it takes: A nine-round game against the computer is about twenty minutes. The full century is an hour or two, and longer with friends who like to think.

Where it came from: This started on a table, with a board in six printed sheets and cards I cut out myself. The look is still that: ink on paper. Nothing on the screen is doing anything you could not do by hand (ish). The computer just does the counting, and finds you someone to play.

store_data.about_the_game:
UNGLAMOROUS

Narrow and technical time trial motorsport disciplines. Buy cheap cars and drive them to their absolute limit.

NO RESTARTS

Each event gives you a handful of timed runs on a course you're still learning. No reverts, each crash or off-track effectively ruins the run. Only your fastest run counts.

DYNAMIC

As more cars drive along the track, it heats up and grip levels can improve. Of course, this is dependant on the weather; cloud cools the track surface, and rain washes away grip. 

COMPETITION

Play against real opponents with asynchronous multiplayer, or play against AI opponents. Every entry is automatically classed based on vehicle modifications and you compete in your bracket.

DRIVETRAINS

Each drivetrain - FWD, RWD, and AWD - all handle differently with their standout effects exaggerated. Tuned for precision and competitiveness between keyboard and controller inputs.

CUSTOMISATION

Vehicle customisation changes how the vehicle actually drives. Bolt on huge aerofoils to cars that have no business wearing them. Source vehicles and parts through a marketplace full of dodgy listings and dodgier sellers, and try to haggle them down.

store_data.about_the_game:
Freaky Wheels is a physics-driven vehicular combat roguelite where driving, shooting and chaos all collide.

It’s the early ’90s. Morgan has spent his whole life inside an isolated cult hidden between the desert mountains.

Then one routine delivery exposes a secret he was never meant to see. Something the cult has kept buried for years. Now the gates are closed, his own people are hunting him, and the only way out is behind the wheel.

  • Physics-Driven Combat: Drift, boost, jump and blast your way through enemy vehicles using an arsenal of weapons, gadgets and abilities.

store_data.about_the_game:
FIGHT is a tactical fighting game about hidden plans. Queue movement, guards, strikes, and special attacks on a shared timeline. Commit before you know the opposing plan. Then watch the two sequences meet in real time. FIGHT rewards choices made before impact. Close the distance with aggressive strikes, hold ground with guards and parries, create space for a projectile, or use movement to bait an answer.

Choose from over twenty weapon-led fighters. Each move set changes the questions you ask: who controls distance, who threatens a guard, and which attack creates space for the next plan. Learn what every fighter can represent before both players lock in. 

Choose the arena before the round begins. Every stage frames the same focused duel on a 2.5D combat plane, where spacing, timing, and your opponent’s next decision stay visible.

Every action has a place on the timeline. Build a chain of movement, defense, strikes, and specials, then commit blind. You do not see the opposing sequence until both plans resolve. Damage matters, but posture creates the opening: pressure a guarded opponent, force a response, and turn a broken defense into a punish.

Once both players commit, the fight runs in real time. Watch the collision, pause on the decision that changed the exchange, and replay the sequence to see how a guard, parry, strike, projectile, or repositioning determined the result.

store_data.about_the_game:
Just Another Shift

You were an ordinary pool cleaner, doing another quiet round of daily maintenance. But routine soon slips away as familiar tiled walls and echoes begin to feel deeply, dangerously wrong.

No-Clipped Into the Poolrooms

One wrong step, and reality tears open. You wake up submerged in an endless, tranquil labyrinth of warm water and ceramic tiles. No exits. No sky. Just infinite, quiet halls stretching into the unknown.

Uninvited Company

The silence doesn't last. Distant splashes and shifting shadows signal that something is tracking your every move. You have no weapons—when you hear them coming, your only choices are to run or hide.

Unravel the Labyrinth

Survival takes more than speed. Decipher environmental puzzles, operate cryptic machinery, and navigate shifting geometry to unlock pathways leading deeper into the levels.

Anomalies Beyond Reason

Physics and logic hold no ground here. From sudden water surges and reality-bending loops to hallucinations that prey on your senses, expect the unexpected at every turn.

store_data.about_the_game:
A first-person survival horror game inspired by horror films from the 1960s. You are one of the victims of Jack Hatter, a former detective who began kidnapping women. Now, your only chance of survival is to find a way to escape his house.

 

Armed with an axe, Jack Hatter will hunt you down and pursue you through every corner of the house, so whatever you do, don't make a sound. If he sees you, run immediately and find somewhere to hide, even if it won't be long before he finds you.

Explore the house in search of a way to escape. Any item could prove useful, so search every corner and manage your resources wisely. Jack Hatter has made any attempt to escape nearly impossible, but your life depends on it.

   

Jack Hatter is a former detective who began kidnapping women in the dead of night, but why? Now, as one of his victims, you may find the answer in the worst way possible.

  • Exploration : Search every corner of the house for items that may be useful for survival and escape.

  • Stealth : Move carefully through the house, hide behind objects, and listen closely for Jack Hatter's sounds to determine his location.

  • AI : His movements are unpredictable. He can be anywhere, opening doors, climbing stairs, lurking nearby, searching hiding spots, listening for you, and of course... chasing you.

  • Investigation : As you search for a way to escape, you'll uncover answers about Jack Hatter hidden throughout the house.

  • Puzzles : Escaping won't be easy. Jack Hatter has already anticipated attempts to flee. Locked doors, chests, safes, and various challenges stand in your way.

  • Replayability : A new experience every time. Items won't always be in the same locations, and neither will Jack Hatter.

store_data.about_the_game:
A passionate, one-night affair with your son's friend's quiet, unassuming mom—

■ Story

You glance at your phone and see an unfamiliar name on the screen.

It's your wife's friend—a mom whose child is friends with your son.

You had exchanged contact information because your children often spent time together.

But the message contains just one sentence:

"Would you have sex with me?"

And nothing more—

■ Concept

The Affair Ryokan is a 3D sex simulator centered around the raw desire between two mature adults.

An affair allows you to indulge in reckless, passionate acts that you could never show your wife or husband.

Give in to the desire you've both been suppressing, and lose yourselves in a night of uninhibited passion.

The game was created to capture the slightly vulgar, raw, and intimate atmosphere of a secret affair between two married adults at a traditional Japanese ryokan.

■ Content

Enjoy an intimate night with the mom at your own pace.

  • Freely choose between voices recorded by four different voice actresses

  • Costume customization and free camera control

store_data.about_the_game:
Descend. Battle. Fall. Return stronger.

Dungeonbound is an incremental first-person dungeon crawler where the fighting runs itself. Pick a hero, lock in a loadout, and start the descent. Attacks, dodges, crits, counters and status ticks all resolve on their own in speed-driven turns, watched through a PS1-era CRT.

Death costs you the floor and nothing else. Every trip home is a chance to spend your gold, buy upgrades, merge your gear and walk back in meaner than you left.

Two ways to descend

The Long Haul (incremental, 3 heroes). Warrior, Mage and Rogue, each with their own gold, their own levels and their own permanent upgrades. Progress on one is never lost while you play another. Dying is a setback measured in floors, not hours. You keep the loot, the levels and the upgrades, and go again.

The Climb (roguelite ladder, 10 characters to unlock). A self-contained run with a roster of specialists, each built around a tag affinity and a passive that fires between floors. Five hearts, shop-first rounds, and a rank that carries between climbs. Lose your last heart and the build is destroyed. The rank is the only thing that comes home with you.

Somebody else's build is waiting

Every floor of the climb ends with a challenger standing between you and the ladder down, and that challenger is a real build somebody actually played. Clear a floor and your own loadout is snapshotted into the pool, stat for stat and item for item, to block somebody else's descent later.

No turns to wait on and nobody to matchmake with: you fight the ghosts of other people's runs, and yours goes back in to haunt theirs. Ranked climbs promote you at floor 8 and demote you when a run dies out.

The same dungeon for everyone, once a day

One seed, one endless descent, everyone in the same corridors. The Endless Delve doesn't have a bottom. It scales past the point of survival and asks how far you got. Same enemies, same drops, same rooms for every player that day. Bragging rights are the only prize.

Combat with real teeth

Turn order runs on speed: act first, act more often, and outpace slow enemies for extra swings. Fights layer dodge, crit, multistrike, overkill damage that spills into the next enemy in the rank, and a full status game of poison, burn, bleed, freeze and stun, each stacking and ticking on its own clock.

Over 200 hand-painted enemies wait across the descent, and they don't all fight fair: thorns that punish every hit you land, berserkers that grow stronger the longer you take, bloodthirsty things that heal off your wounds, thieves that flee with your gold. Nine elites guard the deeper floors and five bosses hold the bottom of each dungeon.

Loot worth dying for

Everything down there pays out. Over 200 items across five rarities drop from regular enemies, elites and bosses: weapons that scale off your missing health or your gold, gear that triggers the moment your armour breaks, cursed pieces that hand you a fortune and a real drawback.

Duplicates aren't dead weight: merge two identical items into a stronger one, all the way to level 10. And at the forge, any two pieces fuse into a hybrid that inherits abilities from both parents. Over 21,000 different first pairings, before you count that hybrids fuse again, and again, and level up afterwards. Nobody else is running your weapon.

Build the hero you want to send below

Gold and skill points buy from a list of over 160 permanent upgrades, sorted into Damage, Defense, Sustain, Economy and Unlocks: more weapon slots, more gear slots, better luck, cheaper shops, statuses that chain, immunities that shut a whole enemy archetype down.

The Mage picks a subclass of Lightning, Frost or Fire, and each keeps its own purchases, so you respec by switching, never by starting over.

Five descents and one that doesn't end

  • The Mudking Warrens: kobolds, orcs and brutefolk in the mud

  • The Bonevault Crypts: the restless dead, curses and cold

  • The Chittering Deep: beasts with deep health pools

  • The Infernal Court: demons that hit hard, crit often and burn everything

  • The Wyrmroost: the dragons at the bottom

  • The Endless Delve: the daily run, and it never ends

Chart your route on the floor map, pick your fights, and choose when to spend at the shop and when to push your luck one room deeper.

A dungeon from another era

Dungeonbound wears its retro heart on its sleeve: a first-person corridor view, chunky pixel-filtered art, and a full PS1-style CRT presentation with scanlines, dither and chromatic flicker. Adjustable battle speed and a readable turn timeline keep it legible while it cooks.

Features

  • Auto-resolving, speed-driven turn-based combat. Set up the build, watch it cook

  • 3 heroes in the incremental campaign, each with separate gold, levels and upgrades

  • 3 Mage subclasses (Lightning / Frost / Fire), each keeping its own progression

  • A 10-character roguelite ladder with hearts, ranks and asynchronous PvP challengers

  • A daily delve on a shared seed, endless and unwinnable by design

  • Over 200 hand-painted enemies, 9 elites and 5 bosses across 5 escalating dungeons

  • Over 200 items in 5 rarities. Merge duplicates to level 10, fuse any two into a hybrid

  • Over 160 permanent upgrades across Damage, Defense, Sustain, Economy and Unlocks

  • Deep status system: poison, burn, bleed, freeze, stun, thorns and more

  • Death-friendly loop. Every defeat banks progress for the next run

  • Authentic PS1/CRT visual style

  • Day/Night Survival - Gather, build, and prepare before the timer hits zero. Then defend your base core against escalating zombie waves.

  • Modular Weapons - Pistol, rifle, shotgun, and melee. Customize with scopes, muzzles, grips, magazines, and stocks across five rarity tiers.
  • AI Cat Companions - Rescue infected cats, recruit healers and assault cats, and command them with a radial wheel.
  • Islands & Dungeons - Resource islands, shop islands, a storm island, a boss island, and themed dungeons: Trap Trial, Rune Sequence, Escape Rush.
  • Co-op for up to 4 - Online multiplayer. Every cat counts.

store_data.about_the_game:
Loomchild is an action-adventure dungeon crawler that combines physics-based brawling with roguelite upgrades. Enter a charming and interactive fantasy world where you can knock, grab, throw or smash enemies into countless breakable objects or into each other. Choose between a colorful cast of characters with unique kits to play! Like Velvet, a half-vampire, half-elf gunslinger with her trusty shadow hand that has a mind of its own. Or Lacetta, a silent maid with a shapeshifting black cat familiar that has an endless appetite and can transform into a vacuum cleaner. Discover items and power-ups that drastically evolve their abilities and the way you play them.

Features

• Kinetic Combat: Physics-based combat allows you to push and pull both enemies and objects. Use these mechanics at your disposal to perform combos, explore and solve puzzles.     

• The Children of the Loom: Choose from a variety of characters to play, each blessed with a fragment of a divine garment and a unique kit with many ways to build them. Meet a colorful cast of NPCs and befriend them for favors, some can be recruited!

• Procedural and Interactive: Maps are a mix of carefully handcrafted and procedurally generated rooms to make each encounter feel fresh. Environments can be damaged, and there will be no shortage of hazards or objects to throw. Beyond clearing the map, monsters can also have randomized drops that add variety to each playthrough.

• Items and Fusions: You can discover and unlock items that evolve your abilities in interesting ways. There are also certain conditions you can meet to unlock secret and powerful transformations for your character.

• An original soundtrack by James Landino, blending genres like breakcore with fantasy elements.

store_data.about_the_game:
Your day, with a little company.

Working... is a relaxing desktop companion and outfit-collecting game. Give your favorite girl a corner of your screen while you work, study, browse or play. Glance over, pick a look that suits your mood, and make an ordinary desktop feel a little warmer.

Five heroines. Find your favorite.

Meet gentle, laid-back Shuning; bright, lively Qingling; calm, mature Zhiyao; refined, thoughtful Ziyuan; and fresh, easygoing Chengxia. Five distinct personalities to brighten different kinds of days. Five starting looks are unlocked from the beginning, so you can choose your companion right away.

One favorite, so many looks

Discover delicate anime art, adorable chibi designs and nostalgic pixel art. Explore outfits and poses inspired by reading at home, handheld gaming, cat cafés, snowy postal routes, arcane scholars and throne queens. Each skin is a complete look, ready to equip. Enable automatic outfit changes to let your owned collection take turns on your desktop.

A collection to make your own

Browse by character, series, art style or rarity. See what you own and what is still waiting to be discovered. Collect across five rarities, from Common to Legendary. Every skin is cosmetic, with no power or productivity bonuses.

  • Eligible online Steam playtime offers a reward opportunity every 30 minutes; actual grants depend on Steam.
  • Keep reward items until you feel like opening them and discovering a new look.
  • Combine 3 eligible duplicate skins of the same rarity for 1 random skin of the next rarity. At least 1 copy of every owned skin is kept. Legendary skins cannot be upgraded further.

Company at your pace

Drag and resize your companion, and choose whether she stays on top of other windows. A transparent background and click-through behavior leave room for the task at hand. No repetitive clicking to grind numbers, no tasks pushing you to hurry. Quiet company while you are busy; a collection to enjoy on your break.

store_data.about_the_game:
NÓN – The Forgotten Hand fuses tactical card strategy with split-second reflexes. Build your formation like you would in any tactics game — then defend it in real time, parrying every incoming strike with a single, perfectly-timed key press. Forget turn-based card battles where you wait your turn and watch numbers tick down: here, a botched parry can kill a card for good, and if your Leader ever falls, the run ends with it.



1. White-knuckle, cinematic showdowns Block one strike, and the enemy fires back immediately with the next in the chain — real-time parries chained beat after beat, tension climbing with every clash. One clean chain of perfect parries is pure spectacle; one wrong beat can unravel it all.

2. Attacks that keep you guessing Every foe pulls from its own set of attack sequences — slow telegraphed strikes, lightning-fast ones, decoys that punish careless button-mashing, and feints that skip your front line to strike the cards behind. Reading the cue in time is the whole game.


3. Failure has real weight Miss your timing and your card eats full damage and burns stamina. Push a card too far and it dies — permanently — leaving a gap in your formation the enemy will exploit for the rest of the fight.

4. Everything rides on your Leader Lose every card in a lane, and the enemy's next strike goes straight for your Leader. They can parry and counter just like any card — but with no stamina to fall back on, every hit taken is a hit that matters. Lose the Leader, lose the run.

1. Build Your Roster Before You Fight Assemble your lineup before the battle even begins — choose which cards hold your three lanes and which wait in reserve on the bench. Your Leader stays fixed for the whole run, but every other card is yours to place. Once the fight starts, there's no hand, no draws, no do-overs — only the formation you built.

2. Adapt Your Lines Mid-Fight At the top of every round, freely rework your formation — pull a battered card to safety, rotate in someone from the bench, or reinforce a lane about to buckle. The instant the round begins, though, your lines lock in — so every swap is a real decision, made with the clock already ticking.

A Roster of Foes, Each With Its Own Rhythm No two enemies fight the same. Each one draws from its own set of attack chains — different colors, different speeds, different tricks — so mastering one foe's timing won't save you against the next. Chip away at their posture with clean parries, and a fully broken guard leaves them staggered wide open for a devastating strike. Boss encounters are on the way in a future update.

Discover a fresh visual experience deeply rooted in indigenous culture.
Mosaic stained glass: 100% hand-drawn graphics with flat color blocks, thick black outlines, and a refined color palette.
“Frameless” cards: The traditional card background is completely removed. Combat cards are objects/symbols floating directly on pedestals, divided into 4 core concepts: Heroes, Mystics, Warriors, and Myths.
Vietnamese inspiration: Throughout the deck, you’ll easily spot familiar images like Nón lá (conical hat), bamboo… stylized impressively and carrying their own distinct powers.

store_data.about_the_game:
🎓 Graduation's Over. Time to Hit the Road!

After graduating from college, you take your old car and set off on your very first solo road trip.

You thought it would just be a simple journey to enjoy the scenery and clear your head…

Until you meet her by the roadside.

“Can I get a ride?”

And just like that, your road trip suddenly gets a lot more interesting. 💕

💕 On the Road, There’s Always Someone to Meet

Along the way, you’ll meet all kinds of girls.

They might be waiting by the roadside, crossing paths with you in a small town, or joining your journey because of an unexpected accident.

Give her a ride? Have a chat? Grab a meal together?

Or sit together in the car at night and talk about things only the two of you know?

Some relationships begin with nothing more than a short ride together.

Your choices will shape the distance between you.

🗺️ Keep Traveling, Keep Meeting Them

Plan your route, stock up on gas and food, and keep your old car in one piece.

Then, hit the road again.

Flat tire? Lost? Giant brown bear? 🐻 Meteor strike? ☄️

Doesn’t matter.

Because you never know who you’ll meet around the next corner.

Unlock new locations, vehicles, items, and stories. Meet more girls and slowly collect memories from your journey.

🌤️ What Is the Meaning of a Journey?

Maybe it’s seeing unfamiliar scenery. Maybe it’s meeting interesting people.

Or perhaps… one evening, you realize that the girl sitting beside you is no longer just “a stranger who happened to need a ride.”

🚗💨 So, Where to Next?

Maybe you should ask her where she wants to go.

store_data.about_the_game:
One Furnace, Ten Thousand Paths.


Alchemy Master is a single-room incremental game rooted in Chinese xianxia cultivation, alchemy, realm breakthroughs, and reincarnation. Begin at the first layer of Qi Refining and manage a continuously operating alchemy chamber. Watch pills leap from each furnace and roll across the floor as you gather resources, deepen your Cultivation, and ascend through thirteen major realms to become a Dao Ancestor.

Pills are both the foundation of cultivation and the heart of every strategic choice. Consume them to gain Cultivation and break through realms. Sell them for Spirit Stones to obtain better alchemy rooms and furnaces. Invest Cultivation in five talent paths, or preserve pills to exchange for artifacts. What you consume, sell, or save determines how each cycle unfolds.

All progression takes place inside one evolving alchemy chamber. Expand from one furnace to six, then hand repetitive collection duties over to the Pill-Gathering Array. New furnace slots and facility upgrades visibly transform the production floor in front of you.

Consume Pills and Break Through the Realms


Consume regular pills to turn their medicinal power into Cultivation. When you have enough, choose when to advance each layer, stage, and major realm. Begin at Qi Refining I, pass through all twelve Qi Refining layers, then ascend through Foundation Establishment, Core Formation, Nascent Soul, Spirit Transformation, and beyond until you reach Dao Ancestor. After that, infinite Dao Ancestor levels remain to be climbed.

Every breakthrough succeeds. The real decision is when to save and when to advance. Higher realms unlock access to stronger pill recipes, facility promotions, and higher artifact-auction tiers. Cultivation can also be invested in talents, creating a constant choice between immediate realm progress and long-term alchemy power.

Upgrade Your Alchemy Operation with Spirit Stones


Sell pills to earn Spirit Stones. Spend them on stronger recipes, expanding and upgrading the alchemy room, promoting each furnace independently, improving the Pill-Gathering Array, or preparing a Reincarnation Pill for the next cycle. The room has twenty levels, furnaces span eight ranks, and your operation can grow from one furnace to six working at once.

Furnaces continuously attempt the recipes you have mastered. A successful pill is not merely a number added to a resource bar: it launches from the furnace, lands on the floor, and rolls into view. Sweep over pills with the mouse or a virtual controller pointer to collect them, or hold the stoking control to accelerate every active furnace.

Each furnace advances independently. Furnace and Pill-Gathering Array upgrades gain distinct ranks and appearances, while room upgrades improve production and random rewards. Every investment prepares you for stronger pills and more distant realms.

Every Pill Is a Choice


Each regular pill has one destination:

  • Sell: Gain Spirit Stones for recipes, room and furnace upgrades, the Pill-Gathering Array, and a future Reincarnation Pill.
  • Consume: Gain Cultivation for realm breakthroughs and talent activation.
  • Save: Store pills and exchange them for artifacts at the realm auction.

No single choice can fund every form of growth. Your next furnace, breakthrough, and artifact often compete for the same batch of pills, so priorities must change with your current goal. Failed refinement may also produce Waste Pills. Sell them for a small return, or risk consuming them for a chance to gain or lose Cultivation.

Master Talents and Trade Pills for Artifacts


Five talent paths, Fire Control, Alchemy, Spirit Sense, Formations, and Artifact Arts, contain 118 nodes. Spend Cultivation to activate and improve talents that shape refining speed, success, multi-pill criticals, stability, random opportunities, automatic collection, and facility synergies.

Artifacts can appear as rare room drops or in the realm auction. The auction displays an artifact's value in Spirit Stones, but completing the trade consumes an equivalent value of pills from your highest currently mastered tier. Saving pills for an artifact delays immediate Spirit Stone and Cultivation gains, but its equipment effects and affixes can transform many future batches.

From Manual Gathering to Automation


At the beginning, move the pointer through pills scattered around the furnaces to collect them. Once purchased and upgraded, the Pill-Gathering Array periodically gathers all furnace-side products and eligible random pills.

Choose one automatic policy for all regular pills: store everything, sell everything, consume everything, or split them between selling and consuming. Automation removes repetitive movement, but it never chooses your next construction project, cultivation route, artifact build, or moment of reincarnation.

Reincarnation Is Not Starting Over


After gathering enough Spirit Stones, purchase and consume a Reincarnation Pill. Reincarnation resets most construction and cultivation progress from the current cycle, then converts your real accomplishments into permanent Fortune. Fortune strengthens production and random gains in every later cycle, steadily shortening roads that once felt distant.

You may also postpone reincarnation and continue climbing infinite Dao Ancestor levels. You decide when a cycle ends and how much present progress to exchange for future speed.

Key Features


  • Pill recipes from Tier 0 through Tier 12, eight furnace ranks, and up to six independently upgraded furnaces.
  • Twenty alchemy-room levels, ten Pill-Gathering Array levels, and configurable automatic pill handling.
  • Thirteen major realms, infinite Dao Ancestor progression, and 118 nodes across five talent paths.
  • Random pills and artifacts, realm auctions, equipment affixes, a codex, statistics, and cycle archives.
  • Keyboard and mouse, native controller navigation, and touch assistance, with UI scaling, reduced-flash, and trail options.
  • Autosaves, ten manual save slots, and Steam Cloud support.

About Offline Progress


The alchemy chamber produces while the game process is running. Time spent minimized is batch-resolved when you return. Closing the game produces no offline gains.

  • Sell: Gain Spirit Stones for recipes, room and furnace upgrades, the Pill-Gathering Array, and a future Reincarnation Pill.
  • Consume: Gain Cultivation for realm breakthroughs and talent activation.
  • Save: Store pills and exchange them for artifacts at the realm auction.

No single choice can fund every form of growth. Your next furnace, breakthrough, and artifact often compete for the same batch of pills, so priorities must change with your current goal. Failed refinement may also produce Waste Pills. Sell them for a small return, or risk consuming them for a chance to gain or lose Cultivation.

Master Talents and Trade Pills for Artifacts


Five talent paths, Fire Control, Alchemy, Spirit Sense, Formations, and Artifact Arts, contain 118 nodes. Spend Cultivation to activate and improve talents that shape refining speed, success, multi-pill criticals, stability, random opportunities, automatic collection, and facility synergies.

Artifacts can appear as rare room drops or in the realm auction. The auction displays an artifact's value in Spirit Stones, but completing the trade consumes an equivalent value of pills from your highest currently mastered tier. Saving pills for an artifact delays immediate Spirit Stone and Cultivation gains, but its equipment effects and affixes can transform many future batches.

From Manual Gathering to Automation


At the beginning, move the pointer through pills scattered around the furnaces to collect them. Once purchased and upgraded, the Pill-Gathering Array periodically gathers all furnace-side products and eligible random pills.

Choose one automatic policy for all regular pills: store everything, sell everything, consume everything, or split them between selling and consuming. Automation removes repetitive movement, but it never chooses your next construction project, cultivation route, artifact build, or moment of reincarnation.

Reincarnation Is Not Starting Over


After gathering enough Spirit Stones, purchase and consume a Reincarnation Pill. Reincarnation resets most construction and cultivation progress from the current cycle, then converts your real accomplishments into permanent Fortune. Fortune strengthens production and random gains in every later cycle, steadily shortening roads that once felt distant.

You may also postpone reincarnation and continue climbing infinite Dao Ancestor levels. You decide when a cycle ends and how much present progress to exchange for future speed.

Key Features


  • Pill recipes from Tier 0 through Tier 12, eight furnace ranks, and up to six independently upgraded furnaces.
  • Twenty alchemy-room levels, ten Pill-Gathering Array levels, and configurable automatic pill handling.
  • Thirteen major realms, infinite Dao Ancestor progression, and 118 nodes across five talent paths.
  • Random pills and artifacts, realm auctions, equipment affixes, a codex, statistics, and cycle archives.
  • Keyboard and mouse, native controller navigation, and touch assistance, with UI scaling, reduced-flash, and trail options.
  • Autosaves, ten manual save slots, and Steam Cloud support.

About Offline Progress


The alchemy chamber produces while the game process is running. Time spent minimized is batch-resolved when you return. Closing the game produces no offline gains.

Spend Spirit Stones on better alchemy rooms and furnaces, Cultivation on five talent paths, and saved pills on artifacts; reincarnate for permanent Fortune.

store_data.about_the_game:
*Desktop - Habitable Planet*

A healing little planet forever floating on your desktop, a [healing, companionable desktop idle game] just for you. While you're busy working, rushing to finish projects, or attending online classes, it quietly spins in the corner of your screen. No need to rush, no need to complete tasks, no need to remember to log in to collect rewards. When you're tired, just glance at it and watch the little animals wandering, dozing, and chasing butterflies in the grass. In the time it takes to relax, the days slowly pass by.

On this planet, you can!

Cultivate a small plot of land, plant flowers and fruit trees, leisurely fish by the lake, collect all sorts of cute little decorations, and decorate your little world according to your own preferences.

You'll meet a group of animal neighbors with distinct personalities: a kind and reliable orange cat, a lively and energetic pink curly-haired cat, and many more friends with their own unique habits. They don't need your constant attention; they'll wander on the grass, nap under the trees, chase butterflies, find food when they're hungry, and simply daydream when they're bored, living their lives to the fullest on their own.

On this planet, you can still do it!

When you have some free time, there are many leisurely little pleasures: assemble soft pixelated beads, collect small stamps and stickers scattered throughout the planet, and gather adorable hanging cards into a collection album; occasionally spin the lucky wheel for a little surprise. There's no need to deliberately collect them all, no need to rush; these little trinkets, collected slowly, are unique souvenirs of this planet.

The Unique Features of This Little Planet

A Slowly Growing Little World

This is a small game independently developed by an individual; the initial release is just the beginning. More new neighbors, decorations, and gameplay elements will be added gradually, allowing you to nurture this planet into a more vibrant and complete world.

Truly Zero Pressure, Play as You Like

No daily check-ins, no red dot reminders, no time-limited rewards, and no so-called optimal solution. Play when you want—plant flowers, fish, and discover a vast array of fish species! Don't want to play? Just leave it running. Even if you don't open it for days, the planet will remain intact, without any loss or progress lag. 🪐

A Desktop Companion You Can Place Anywhere

Supports arbitrary window size scaling and transparency adjustment, and can be docked to any corner of the screen. It won't obstruct your work interface or disturb your tasks, quietly serving as your desktop background.

Little Surprises Hidden in the Details

Each little animal has its own unique actions and temperaments; day and night and weather subtly change; and inconspicuous little Easter eggs are hidden in the grass. A casual glance can always reveal a little bit of sweet happiness.

store_data.about_the_game:
What if you could live a thousand lives?

From your very first breath to your final moments, you will experience every year of an ordinary life. You’ll learn to walk, go to school, make friends, fall in love for the first time, choose a career, meet strangers, perhaps start a family… You’ll laugh, you’ll fail, you’ll lose people you love. Sometimes, almost nothing will happen.

And yet, every decision matters.

At every stage of your life, situations will arise and you’ll have to make choices. Some may seem insignificant. Others will completely change the course of your life. A forgotten encounter from years ago may resurface. A decision you made at 15 could follow you all the way to 70. And some of the most important moments may only reveal their meaning much later.

You might have a brilliant career or spend your entire life in the same small village. Fall in love, stay alone, have children… Or just a dog. Take risks or choose a quiet life. Make the right choices… or the wrong ones.

There is no victory. Only a life to live.

And when that life comes to an end, another one will begin.

With millions of possible combinations of choices, encounters, relationships, and events shaping your existence, no two playthroughs will ever tell the same story.

You won’t simply play Oda’s life.

You’ll discover who Oda could have become.

• 1 year = 1 event: each year of your life, a new event is presented to you.

• 2 choices per event: decide how Oda reacts and shape the course of his life.

• Long-term consequences: your decisions can influence the events, relationships, and opportunities that appear years later.

• Millions of possibilities: choices, encounters, relationships, and events can combine in countless ways to create a different life every time you play.

• Reincarnation: when Oda dies, choose to begin an entirely new life or relive the exact same life to try to change certain events and alter his fate.

• Every life is unique: no two playthroughs will unfold exactly the same way.

Enter a strange world filled with colorful sweets, dangerous obstacles, mysterious environments, and a witch standing in your way.

FACE THE WITCH

Overcome the obstacles ahead, survive dangerous encounters, and work together as you make your way toward the witch waiting at the end of your journey.

Hansel & Cookie is designed for two players and focuses on cooperation, communication, and overcoming challenges together.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Swarm has taken the world. Everything worth having is still out there, and somebody has to go and get it.

LOOT, EXTRACT, UPGRADE, REPEAT

Drop in with your squad, fight through infested ground, and grab whatever you can carry - weapon parts, samples, research containers. Then call the extraction drone and get out. What you carry home rebuilds your HQ. What you were carrying when you died stays on the ground.

Runs are short. What you are building with them is not.

AN EXTRACTION SHOOTER THAT LETS YOU LOSE

No PvP. No wipe that puts you back to nothing. Standard-issue gear is always free and always waiting for you, so a bad run costs you the loot you got greedy with and nothing else. Bring nothing and risk nothing, or bring your best and set your own stakes. You decide how hardcore this gets.

SHARED-SCREEN CO-OP

You move as one unit down one road. Fall behind and the screen stops until the squad regroups, so nobody sprints ahead and nobody gets left behind. Friendly fire is on, ammo runs out, and a downed teammate needs somebody to come back for them.

THREE ROLES, ONE UNIT

Assault brings a shotgun and a War Cry that turns you berserk when the crowd closes in. Support carries the heavy machine gun, moves slowly, and drops ammo for everyone. Medic has an SMG and speed, scouts ahead and drops medkits.

EXTRACTION IS A DECISION

You can call the drone at any moment. Calling it is loud: the whole map hears it, and the seconds before it lands are the most dangerous of the run. Leave early with a little, or push deeper and gamble everything you are carrying.

EVERY SUPPLY DROP IS A CHOICE

Three drops per mission, three options each - a weapon attachment, armor plating, or a utility upgrade. Grenade rifle, extended dash, ammo belt, shield. No dead picks, and no two runs armed the same way.

THE BOARD ALWAYS HAS WORK

Scavenge runs, extermination contracts, boss hunts for Monster Hosts, and events that appear without warning when an enemy base turns up on the map. The further your HQ gets rebuilt, the harder the work and the better the pay.

REBUILD THE HQ

You start with a dark base and one free rifle. Research containers turn the lights back on, one facility at a time. The Armory crafts and upgrades weapons from blueprints and scavenged parts. The Lab converts samples and intel into raw stats and mutations. The Workshop tunes your active skills. The Gym turns Steroids into muscle, health and stamina. The Bar sells a round that buffs the whole squad on the next drop, and the Cloakroom sells the outfit you do it in.

KNOW WHAT IS OUT THERE

Swarmers come in numbers and die in numbers. Acid spitters and flyers pick apart your positioning. Mini-bosses are smart enough to plan. Monster Hosts reshape the level while you are fighting in it. And the people who caused all this are still around - unlike the bugs, they shoot back.

PC AND MOBILE, SAME SQUAD

One build, full cross-play. Your friend on a phone drops into the same run as you at a desk.

PC AND MOBILE, SAME SQUAD

store_data.detailed_description:
The Swarm has taken the world. Everything worth having is still out there, and somebody has to go and get it.

LOOT, EXTRACT, UPGRADE, REPEAT

Drop in with your squad, fight through infested ground, and grab whatever you can carry - weapon parts, samples, research containers. Then call the extraction drone and get out. What you carry home rebuilds your HQ. What you were carrying when you died stays on the ground.

Runs are short. What you are building with them is not.

AN EXTRACTION SHOOTER THAT LETS YOU LOSE

No PvP. No wipe that puts you back to nothing. Standard-issue gear is always free and always waiting for you, so a bad run costs you the loot you got greedy with and nothing else. Bring nothing and risk nothing, or bring your best and set your own stakes. You decide how hardcore this gets.

SHARED-SCREEN CO-OP

You move as one unit down one road. Fall behind and the screen stops until the squad regroups, so nobody sprints ahead and nobody gets left behind. Friendly fire is on, ammo runs out, and a downed teammate needs somebody to come back for them.

THREE ROLES, ONE UNIT

Assault brings a shotgun and a War Cry that turns you berserk when the crowd closes in. Support carries the heavy machine gun, moves slowly, and drops ammo for everyone. Medic has an SMG and speed, scouts ahead and drops medkits.

EXTRACTION IS A DECISION

You can call the drone at any moment. Calling it is loud: the whole map hears it, and the seconds before it lands are the most dangerous of the run. Leave early with a little, or push deeper and gamble everything you are carrying.

EVERY SUPPLY DROP IS A CHOICE

Three drops per mission, three options each - a weapon attachment, armor plating, or a utility upgrade. Grenade rifle, extended dash, ammo belt, shield. No dead picks, and no two runs armed the same way.

THE BOARD ALWAYS HAS WORK

Scavenge runs, extermination contracts, boss hunts for Monster Hosts, and events that appear without warning when an enemy base turns up on the map. The further your HQ gets rebuilt, the harder the work and the better the pay.

REBUILD THE HQ

You start with a dark base and one free rifle. Research containers turn the lights back on, one facility at a time. The Armory crafts and upgrades weapons from blueprints and scavenged parts. The Lab converts samples and intel into raw stats and mutations. The Workshop tunes your active skills. The Gym turns Steroids into muscle, health and stamina. The Bar sells a round that buffs the whole squad on the next drop, and the Cloakroom sells the outfit you do it in.

KNOW WHAT IS OUT THERE

Swarmers come in numbers and die in numbers. Acid spitters and flyers pick apart your positioning. Mini-bosses are smart enough to plan. Monster Hosts reshape the level while you are fighting in it. And the people who caused all this are still around - unlike the bugs, they shoot back.

PC AND MOBILE, SAME SQUAD
