store_data.about_the_game:
Guard the world's last campfire and form a three-hero expedition from a roster of six. Combine skills, gear, pets, and tactical synergies across a five-chapter campaign, readable multi-enemy auto battles, route expeditions, fixed challenges, and an endless mode.

The campfire marks the beginning of every expedition—and the one light still waiting after defeat.

In Campfire Expedition, you do not swing the heroes' weapons yourself. You recruit and train heroes at a night-time camp, choose three from a roster of six for the front, middle, and back positions, configure their automatic skills and equipment, and bring a pet that can attack, protect, heal, or alter the pace of battle.

The expedition begins in the Whispering Forest and continues through the Abandoned Mine, Ashen Ruins, Storm Cliffs, and Eternal Night Coast. Victories bring back gold, upgrade dust, and fixed equipment, while bosses, quests, and camp facilities advance the five-chapter journey. Inventory filters, the forge, set tracking, and source information make every equipment decision understandable. When the game is closed, the party continues gathering limited resources for up to eight hours.

After Chapter One, Route Expedition offers branching choices between battles, elites, events, rests, and merchants, with run blessings supporting distinct build directions. Beyond the five-chapter campaign, six fixed challenges, the thirty-wave Ember Trial, and Endless Expedition continue to test the party. Battle reports explain damage, protection, healing, pet contributions, and the causes of defeat.

Features:

- Six recruitable heroes, with three chosen for front, middle, and back positions.

- 24 configurable skills, 84 fixed gear items, and 9 themed equipment sets.

- Six trainable pets plus hero, skill, and pet synergies.

- Five chapters, 31 main-story nodes, 30 enemy types, and multi-enemy auto battles.

- Route events and run blessings, six fixed challenges, the Ember Trial, and Endless Expedition.

- Detailed results, battle reports, failure guidance, and manual build presets.

- Three local save slots and up to 8 hours of offline resources; the game itself is playable offline.

- Simplified Chinese and English interfaces with keyboard/mouse, window/fullscreen, and separate volume settings.

- One purchase, with no ads or in-app purchases.

store_data.about_the_game:
Build your club. Develop your players. Chase championships.

Renz Soccer Sim is a 2D soccer management simulation where you take control of your own club and guide it through season after season of competition.

Build your squad, develop players, make transfers, manage your finances, customize your club, and prepare your team for each match. Once the whistle blows, watch your players take the field and see if the club you’ve built has what it takes to win.

Every match matters. Victories push you toward the top of the table, while poor performances may force you to rethink your squad, tactics, and long-term plans.

BUILD YOUR SQUAD

Scout and sign players to improve your roster. Develop your existing squad over time and make decisions about where your club needs to improve.

Build a balanced team capable of competing now—or invest in the future and create a squad that can dominate for seasons to come.

WATCH THE ACTION

Your job doesn’t end when the match begins.

Watch your team compete in simulated 2D soccer matches where the players you’ve assembled take to the pitch. Follow the score, statistics, and action as your management decisions are put to the test.

MANAGE YOUR CLUB

Success isn’t only about what happens on the field.

Manage your club’s finances, make roster decisions, customize your team, track player and club statistics, and navigate the challenges of building a successful soccer organization.

BUILD A LEGACY

One good season is only the beginning.

Compete across multiple seasons, chase league championships, break club records, earn achievements, and see how far you can take your team.

Can you turn your club into a soccer dynasty?

FEATURES

• 2D simulated soccer matches you can watch unfold
• Multi-season career mode
• Squad and roster management
• Player development and progression
• Scouting and player transfers
• Club finances and economy management
• League standings and season statistics
• Club and jersey customization
• Career records and awards
• Multiple save slots
• Steam achievements
• 8 supported languages
• Single-player management gameplay
• Long-term progression and replayability

store_data.about_the_game:
Pawnimals brings classic chess to life with a royal cast of animated animal armies. Choose your champions, step onto a 3D board, and play at your pace—whether you are learning your first moves, sharpening tactics, or challenging a friend on the same PC.

Choose Your Army

Lead pigs, rhinos, bears, cats, dogs, elephants, frogs, penguins, dinosaurs, or unicorns. Each army brings its own character designs, animations, sounds, and reactions to the board.

Play Your Way

  • Five computer difficulties — From Beginner to Expert.
  • Danger Sense — Preview the first three different risky moves in Beginner and Easy computer matches. A ghost capture shows how your moved piece could be taken, then you can choose another move or move anyway. Repeating the same preview in the same position uses no extra warning.
  • Local two-player matches — Share the board with a friend on the same PC.
  • 100 mate-in-two puzzles — Find the forcing finish in themed tactical challenges.
  • 100 guided lessons — Explore board basics, tactics, strategy, and endgames with Professor Hootington in the Royal Chess Academy.
  • Gauntlet mode — Choose your champion and climb a nine-battle tower, with Easy, Medium, and Hard challenges.
  • Flexible time controls — Play untimed or choose Classical, Rapid, Blitz, or custom clocks.
  • Replay support — Review saved games and import PGN files.
  • Make it yours — Adjust text size, animation speed, music and effects volume, reduced animation, and color-assist markers.

Chess With Character

Animal pieces hop across the board, react to captures, and celebrate or despair when the match is decided. Switch between perspective and top-down views, rotate the board, and adjust sound and camera settings to suit your game.

The Academy's short lessons and practice moves let you learn without a timer and try again as often as you like.

Pick your champions. Claim the crown.

store_data.about_the_game:
Strawberry Season is a slice-of-life visual novel game where you play as Selene, a third-year high school student dating her childhood friend, Juno. As Juno prepares for her entrance exams, she's also planned six fun dates for the two of you to spend together before she leaves for university.

You'll get to decorate ita bags, take and decorate cute purikura photos, a gentle relief from the pressures of school and the hustle of your part-time cafe job. As the semester comes to a close, however, you start to wonder about Juno's true feelings about what future the two of you may have. What will be of your relationship once the physical proximity is no longer a factor? 

Features:

Slice-of-life Visual Novel

Enjoy the sweet and casual moments spent with Juno, your girlfriend and longtime childhood friend. A top student, she uses fashion as an escape from the dull routine of studying.

Cute Cooking Minigame

While not on dates or at school, you often pick up shifts at Cafe Etoile, a Cafe run by a family friend who allows you to make anything you like. Choose your shifts, as well as their difficulty level, to pick up some pocket change that can be spent on gifts for Juno or anything else you like.

Cozy Date Activities

Play cozy, stress free minigames on your dates with Juno, whether it be phototaking, ita bag decorating, or even doing your nails together! You'll have no timer, just a sweet activity planned that you can enjoy together.

Choices Matter

As university looms closer, both you and Juno start to become more unsure about the arrangement of your relationship, but neither of you is brave enough to bring it up. Dialogue choices and the gifts you select for Juno will affect the ending of the game. Will your relationship be one of high school sweethearts, or end with a bittersweet graduation?

store_data.about_the_game:
Feeling overworked, you’ve decided to take vacation and spend 3 nights at “The 4th Ryokan,” a remote ryokan in the mountains.

You’ll be staying in a luxurious Japanese style room that overlooks a beautiful courtyard.

If there are no anomalies, you should go to bed; whereas if there is an anomaly, you should call the reception in order to progress to the next day.

“The 4th Ryokan”is a short, first-person game with a bit of horror that should take around 60 to 90 minutes to complete.

The game controls are simple. To play, navigate the room by walking (mouse movement with WASD keys,) selecting options (left click,) and zooming in (right click.)

It’s a walking simulator game inspired by The Exit 8 where players navigate a closed room, searching for anomalies to continue to the end of the ryokan stay.

There is no restriction on streaming the gameplay and/or uploading play-through videos; however, the creators assume all risks.

store_data.about_the_game:
HIDE. PAINT. SNITCH.

A ten-minute round in a Soviet apartment block. Up to seven of you are the tenants. One of you is the NKVD. The NKVD has a dog. The dog has a hat.

PAINT YOURSELF INTO THE FLAT

Take a color from the wallpaper with the eyedropper, paint your body by hand, back into the wall — and freeze. The pattern runs straight from the carpet onto you. Take one step and it doesn't. A perfect paintjob is invisible. A sloppy one is unforgettable.

THE DOG HEARS YOUR HEART

The closer she gets, the louder it beats — for both of you. She can't open doors. Paws.

THE FUSES WILL BLOW

Twice a round the block's fuses go. An address is called out. Someone has to leave a perfectly good hiding spot, cross the building and reset the meter in a stranger's flat. Nobody goes? Blackout: fifteen seconds of darkness and spinning red emergency lights — and the NKVD confiscates the furniture you were painted as.

YOUR FRIENDS ARE THE PROBLEM

Call the landline in a friend's flat and let it ring. Invite them for a smoke break they physically have to walk to. Or open the menu and become the snitch: walk in the open, take compromising photos, point the NKVD at everyone. The tenants get one tip about where the snitch went. What they do to him ends up on the Wall of Shame.

THE ANTHEM

When the NKVD plays the anthem, everyone stands at attention. Everyone. For twenty seconds. Right where you are.

FROM THE LIFE OF THE COLLECTIVE

Every photo taken during the session goes up on the courtyard newspaper board. Every mugshot too. The grannies on the bench have opinions about your camouflage.

• 2–8 players online, ten-minute rounds, no classes, no unlocks — just paint and bad decisions

• One block: three floors, a basement, a courtyard. Home if you grew up there. A museum of weird if you didn't.

• Dry, bureaucratic, absurd. Not a history lesson.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Story:

Maria Vasilievna sat alone in the drawing room, like a solitary flower put on public display. Nikolai Andreyevich, her husband—a man of honor and high standing—preferred the world of his business dealings. Maria Vasilievna felt the drawing room—that den of "vipers"—closing in on her, suffocating her. Her attempts to maintain her dignity within this cage of flattery and gossip were crumbling to dust. She left; the click of her heels on the parquet floor seemed to count down the final moments before her escape. Outside, she encountered a junk dealer trying to hawk his wares. Her gaze was drawn to a mirror that had once belonged to a noblewoman who had lost everything. Purchasing the mirror triggered an unexpected change in her husband, sparking an inexplicable fear and driving Maria Vasilievna to fight for her happiness.

Games with the Entity:

The Game of the "Black Queen." The goal is to discard all the cards. One must remember: each card is not merely paper; it represents memories—fragments of family life and the souls of the spouses. Yet, bear in mind: the more precious the memory, the more intensely it will torment you. Winning the game yields the first clue needed to unravel the mystery.

The Game of the "Two Chalices." The entity holds two chalices. One is elegant, crafted from pure silver and filled with a pale-gold, sparkling liquid that radiates a gentle warmth. The other is crude and black—carved from dark, petrified-looking wood—and filled with a thick, swirling, dark-purple substance that emanates a palpable chill. One holds the "Essence of Truth"; the other, the "Mist of Oblivion." Only by choosing the right chalice can you obtain the second clue.

The "Cards" game: the Entity holds three cards in its clawed hands. Each depicts a flower. The first card shows a lupine; the second, withered marigolds; and the third, a hawthorn branch. Only by passing the Entity's trial can you discover the way to save Nikolai Andreyevich.

Secrets history has kept hidden:

The mirror triggered the Entity's appearance, setting a countdown in motion. Nikolai Andreyevich—a prisoner of obligation and the world beyond the looking-glass—awaits Maria Vasilyevna’s decision. Three paths, three destinies. Only one path leads to salvation; two lead to the abyss. You must choose—wisely or in desperation. As Maria Vasilyevna uncovers more of the story, more questions arise. Who is the Progenitor, and how is he connected to the otherworld? Why does Nikolai Andreyevich remain silent about his family's past?

The final game decides everything. Make the right choice to discover the key to Nikolai Andreyevich’s salvation.

Game features:

A narrative visual novel featuring fully fleshed-out dialogue and atmospheric storytelling.

Play games against the Entity while unraveling the secrets of an aristocratic family.

Choice and branching system: your decisions shape the plot and determine the heroine's fate.

Multiple endings—ranging from house arrest to fleeing abroad. One wrong choice could be your last.

Vivid characters: the acerbic Maria Vasilyevna, the mysterious Entity, Nikolai Andreyevich—who is becoming increasingly obsessed with the mirror—and other enigmatic figures in the story.

movies.name: A Needle In A Haystack: Sorting Game

store_data.about_the_game:
Find the needle in a haystack!

Welcome to A Needle In A Haystack: Sorting Game, a satisfying sorting simulation game where you take one of the world's most impossible sayings and turn it into your job!

Your mission is simple: there's a needle somewhere in that enormous pile of hay. Find it.

Start small by picking up hay piece by piece, sorting through the pile and selling what you collect for money. The more you earn, the more you can invest back into your barn and turn a painfully slow search into a hay-sorting operation!

SORT. SELL. UPGRADE.

Every piece of hay gets you closer to finding the needle — and closer to your next upgrade.

Use the money you earn to upgrade your barn, improve your equipment and unlock new ways to tackle increasingly massive haystacks.

UNLOCK NEW TOOLS

Picking up hay one piece at a time might work at first... but you're going to need something better.

Buy shovels to scoop up more hay at once, unlock ladders to reach the top of towering haystacks, and discover even more useful equipment as you progress.

The bigger your operation becomes, the faster you can sort!

THERE'S A NEEDLE IN THERE... SOMEWHERE.

Dig deeper. Clear the pile. Upgrade your barn. Buy better tools.

And most importantly...

Find the needle in a haystack!

store_data.about_the_game:
Move left and right. Command the whole formation.


Ember Crown is a vertical 2D arcade action game built around left-right movement and automatic volleys. Your archers attack on their own, while you guide the princess, shield wall, and bow line across two lanes. Intercept enemies, preserve the formation, and help incoming reinforcements reach your ranks.

The rules are simple, but positioning, timing, and the size of your army shape every battle.

Endless Escape


Protect the princess and shield wall, gather reinforcements under ever-growing pressure, and push your distance record as far as you can.

Siege


Command a growing army and advance on the gate. Defeat defenders and bosses, strengthen each volley, breach the gate, and improve your clear time.

Features


  • Vertical 2D arcade action built around left-right movement and automatic volleys
  • Two main modes focused on distance and clear time
  • A formation that grows from a small royal guard into a massed army
  • Short, easy-to-learn runs designed for repeated attempts
  • Many Easter eggs
  • In-game achievements
  • Full text support in Simplified Chinese, English, and Japanese

A Note from the Developer


I've always loved the excitement and joy of discovering something unexpected in a game through my own observations and trial and error.

Ember Crown is a small game. Endless Escape is deliberately challenging, and its difficulty is the result of repeated testing and adjustments. I've also tucked quite a few Easter eggs into the game. While making it, what I looked forward to most was the moment a player would discover one for themselves.

If you'd prefer something more relaxed, Siege offers a more laid-back, satisfying path to victory.

I hope this game can bring you some of that joy of discovering a surprise for yourself.

— PrismDiscus Studio

store_data.about_the_game:
Terrarium is a deck-builder about a medieval village growing inside a sealed glass case. You never order a villager around. You play cards, and villagers are what the cards cost. Each one you spend walks out across the board, does the work, and comes home a turn later. Villagers you do not spend widen your hand next turn, so a card held back is worth part of a card later.

BUILDINGS ARE CARDS, AND CARDS COME OFF THE BOARD

Every building in your deck is a one-shot card. Place it and it leaves the deck for good, so raising your village is also how you thin it.

What goes back into the deck comes off the board. A Farm hands you Harvest. A Lumber Camp sends Fell, a Tower sends Muster, a Smithy sends Forge Arms. If a raid burns that building down, the card it gave you leaves the deck from wherever it is sitting, whether that is your hand, the draw pile or the discard.

The market is a rack of shelves at the side of the case, and it sells things rather than cards. A building bought there goes straight onto a tile and is paid for when it lands. What the shelves stock depends on what already stands in your village. No Smithy, no Hired Swords.

THE BOARD IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE PUZZLE

Each tile is a 3x3 grid of smaller cells, so footprints straddle tile borders and neighbours matter. Mills boost the farms beside them. Palisades stiffen each other. A Gate is worth more with wall on both sides. Trees block the cells they stand on and leave the gaps buildable. Docks want water, quarries want stone.

Ground outside your start square is locked and fogged until you buy it. Every tile you clear is also a tile the raiders have counted, so growth and threat are the same number. The lantern on the corner post of the case runs from green through ember to red as exposed threat climbs. Tap it and the tally swings out so you can do the arithmetic yourself.

RAIDERS LOOT BEFORE THEY BURN

A raid measures its threat against your defence, and anything left over is damage. Damage first steals from your largest stockpile, so hoarding carries its own risk. Buildings only start coming down once there is nothing left to take.

Muster puts your idle villagers on the wall, where they die before your buildings do. Play another card after mustering and you have thinned your own line.

AGES

Every village starts with a Town Centre. Pay for the next age and the Builders leave for two turns. When they come home your hand grows, the stalls open a new shelf, and the deck owes a burn: any card, from any pile, out of the run permanently. Cards of a later age carry that age's dye in their wood.

Raiders who get past everything else do not burn the Town Centre. They pull it down an age, and the shelves close behind them.

THE ROAD

A case is one run. Win it and you go out onto a road across an island you drive yourself. You are the ox cart, and the country around each stop is that stop's own biome, so the desert you can see from the track is the desert you will land in.

Each place is a run with its own bed, outline and rule. Raiders wading in off the coast. A quarry already standing. Walls already up. Every edge at once, at the last case.

Between places, notes offer a choice of two: cards into the deck, a purse, a card burned out, an upgrade. Jars hold relics that rewrite the rules of the next run, such as cheaper tiles, wider markets, boosts that linger, or a warning turn before every raid.

Lose a place and the road ends there. Start again and the island is laid out fresh.

FEATURES

Villagers as energy. Cards cost people, not mana. Spent villagers walk out, work, and return a turn later. Unspent ones widen your next hand.

Buildings are one-shot cards. Placing a building removes it from the deck, so construction is deck thinning.

A deck that answers to the board. Buildings put their own boost cards on top of your draw pile. Burn the building and the card goes with it.

A market of things, not cards. Six stalls, one reroll a turn, stock gated by what stands in your village.

Sub-cell placement. Tiles split 3x3, footprints straddle borders, and terrain decides where a building is worth building.

Growth is threat. Every tile you clear counts toward the next raid, and the lantern on the case shows how exposed you are.

Raids that take before they break. Damage loots your biggest stockpile first, then your walls, then your buildings, then your people.

Ages. Pay the Town Centre, lose your Builders for two turns, gain a card in hand and a new shelf of goods, and owe the deck a permanent burn. Raiders can knock an age back off you.

A drivable road. An island laid out fresh each campaign, with places, notes and jars in tiers. Steer the ox cart between them and choose which stop to take next.

Places with rules. Six board outlines and four biomes, each place scaled to how far along the road it sits.

Relics in jars. Most rewrite the rules of every run that follows. A few are read by the road itself.

Rarity that means supply. Rare cards have a fixed number of copies for the whole run, and the shelf ink tells you how many are left.

Built to be looked at. Flat-shaded low poly under glass, selectable art looks, and a camera you can orbit and push in on.

CONTROLS

Drag the glass to turn the case, scroll to zoom, tap a card to lift it and tap again to play it. The hand rests low against the glass and rises to meet the pointer. Everything is one pointer, so nothing is buried in a modifier key.

store_data.about_the_game:
Ever wanted to run your own pet shop? My Fantasy Pet Shop lets you do just that - in a fantasy world filled with strange and adorable creatures.

Take care of your animals, keep your shop stocked, serve your customers, and slowly turn a small shop into something you're proud of.

Run Your Shop

Buy and sell creatures, keep them happy, and help adventurers find their perfect companion.

Make It Yours

Place furniture, decorations, shelves, animal enclosures, and whatever else your shop needs. Arrange everything the way you want and create a shop that feels like your own.

Take Care of Your Pets

Your animals aren't just things to sell. Feed them, look after them, and make sure they're happy and healthy.

Grow Your Business

Start with a small shop and use your earnings to improve it. Buy new equipment, stock up on supplies, and make your shop bigger and better over time.

A Cozy Fantasy Setting

Your shop is your home base, with a small area outside to explore and enjoy between customers. Take your time, look after your animals, and build the pet shop you've always wanted.

Welcome to My Fantasy Pet Shop.

store_data.about_the_game:
🤾 The Arcade Handball Experience

Handball, but not quite the way you know it.

Take full control of your team in a fast-paced arcade-style experience designed around the full width of the arena. Simple controls let anyone jump in and start playing within seconds, while the action stays focused on quick decisions, movement, passing, and scoring.

This isn't a hardcore simulation — it's handball made to be easy to pick up, fun to play, and exciting from the very first match. Play completely offline, customize your team, master your skills, and lead your squad to victory.

🏆 LIVE THROUGH HANDBALL HISTORY — PAST AND FUTURE!

Relive real tournaments starting with the 2007 World Cup, or jump ahead and play events that haven't happened yet, like the 2027 Handball World Cup — real teams, real groups, before the world sees them!

🔥 Game Modes

• Quick Match – Jump straight into action by selecting home and visiting teams

• League – Compete across a season and win prestigious trophies

• Tournament – Face selected teams and fight for championship glory

• Real-World Tournaments – Play through actual tournaments like World Cups and other major competitions, starting in 2007 — and get ahead of the game with future events like the 2027 World Cup before they're even played!

🏆 Progress & Achievements

• Unlock 40+ achievements with stylish collectible badges

🌍 Locations

• Arena – Classic indoor stadium atmosphere for major matches

• City Court – Outdoor games with optional rain effects

Note: Due to licensing restrictions, player names used in the game are fictitious and do not represent real athletes.

store_data.about_the_game:
The tower has never been beaten. You have one life to be the first.
Every adventurer who walked through the gate came for the same reason you did. To climb it. To reach the top. To be the one who finally conquers it. That is what adventurers do. So you take up your blade and you begin.

One life permadeath with a twist!
Losing all your health doesn't mean you're finished. Go down in battle and you can drag yourself back to your feet, up to three times, weaker each time, but still alive. This isn't permadeath that ends you on a single mistake. It's permadeath that makes you earn every recovery. And even after that third fall, you are not as finished as you think. There is one more chance, in a form you won't see coming.

Every floor is a different environment!
Each one has its own characters to uncover. New enemies, new dangers, new things to piece together the higher you climb. Examine the battlefield before you commit. Study your opponents, learn how they move and strike, and prepare. The insight you gather is the difference between surviving the room and falling in it.

But not every choice is made with your blade.
The tower is full of choices, and what you decide has a real impact around you. Fight, flee. Trust or turn away. Your choices genuinely change what happens next, opening some paths and closing others. No two climbs are the same.

Features

  • One life, but a fair one: go down in a fight and rise up to three times, weaker each time.

  • Even the final fall isn't the end you'd expect. The tower has one more chance waiting…

  • Every floor is its own environment: examine each area and study your enemies before you strike, then turn what you learn into your strategy to stay alive.

  • Choices that matter: who you help, who you fight, and what you decide genuinely change how your climb unfolds.

store_data.about_the_game:
Blightwinter is a dark medieval town-building deck-builder.  Assign townsfolk to regional structures, build your fall deck, and balance survival against an encroaching plague. Will your settlement endure, or crumble to disease and shadow?

Seasonal Cycle

  • Recruit arriving townsfolk in Spring

  • Construct buildings and assign workers in Summer

  • Draw from your assembled deck in Fall to face events, collect resources, and endure Winter

Push-Your-Luck Mechanics

How far will you push your draw each year?

Risk pulling plague cards, vermin, and dark events to gain the extra resources needed to keep your populace alive.

Building-Driven Deck Construction

Completed buildings paired with assigned townsfolk contribute cards to your annual deck.

From crops and coins to dark rituals and plagues.

Distinct Medieval Regions: Each with unique gameplay pools

  • The Lowlands: Pastoral farmlands focused on kinship and abundant harvests.

  • Holyreach: Sacred grounds of faith, tithes, and sanctuary.

  • The Old Burgh: A bustling center of commerce, coins, and crowd management.

  • The Black March: A dangerous, bog-choked borderland where necromancy and dark extraction reign.

  • Wayward Lands: Randomized building pools for endlessly dynamic survival runs.

Villagers with unique Traits & Afflictions

Every citizen features procedurally generated suits (Food, Gold, Faith) and game-altering traits. Harness hardworking townsfolk, or manage infected, superstitious, and undead villagers.

store_data.about_the_game:
EVERY STEP LEAVES EVIDENCE

SET THEM UP is a 4–12 player social deduction game built around one simple rule: your footprints never lie — unless someone makes them.

Complete your task, manipulate the evidence, frame another player, and clean up the trail before the detectives figure out what really happened.

COMPLETE YOUR TASK

At the start of the round, players spread across the map to complete their assigned tasks.

But wherever you go, you leave a trail of footprints behind.

Everyone can see the evidence forming around them, turning every movement into a decision. The route you take could eventually be used against you.

FRAME YOUR TARGET

Finishing your task is only the beginning.

Once you're done, you can start leaving another player's footprints behind instead of your own.

Lead the trail somewhere suspicious. Connect someone else to the wrong place. Create evidence that tells a completely different story.

But you only have a limited amount of fake trail to work with, so choose your route carefully.

ERASE THE EVIDENCE

When the task phase ends, the investigation begins.

No new footprints are created. What happened has already happened.

Now players can remove selected footprints from the map, destroying evidence that could expose them — or evidence that could prove someone else's innocence.

Every footprint you erase changes the story the detectives are trying to reconstruct.

PLAY AS A DETECTIVE

Some players take the role of detectives.

During the task phase, detectives enter the map later and see delayed footprint information rather than simply watching everything happen in real time.

Follow the trails. Catch players during the task phase. Then use the evidence left behind to work out who was really responsible.

TRUST THE TRAIL. OR DON'T.

A trail leading directly to a player might be genuine.

It might have been planted.

Part of it might already be missing.

And the person who looks completely innocent might simply have cleaned up better than everyone else.

In SET THEM UP, you're not just trying to avoid suspicion.

You're deciding where the suspicion goes.

FEATURES

  • 4–12 player online multiplayer

  • Footprint-based social deduction

  • Complete tasks while leaving physical evidence behind

  • Copy other players' footprints to frame them

  • Limited fake-trail distance forces strategic choices

  • Erase individual footprints during the investigation

  • Play as a detective and follow delayed trails

  • Catch players during the task phase

  • Multiple playable characters

  • Public and private multiplayer lobbies

  • Short rounds built around deception, evidence and misdirection

store_data.about_the_game:
The Kingdom of Brightmere has never known night.

Its people, the Wicklings, have candles for heads and a Sun that never sets. Today the Procession barge came for Pip's little sister. It is a great honour to be chosen. Everyone said so.

Pip is going to catch that barge.

It plays exactly like the platformers you grew up with. Eight worlds of tight, hand-built levels. A world map with chapels, memory panels and wandering lamplighters. Seven suits: Moth Wings that let you fly when your P-meter fills, a Wax Mask that turns you into a statue, a Newt Suit for the lakes, a Bell Suit that rings enemies off the screen. Fortresses with crushers and ghosts. Barges full of cannons. End-of-level cards that pay out in spares.

And every one of those systems has been turned a few degrees toward dread.

  • Your head is the timer. The level clock is the wax of your own candle. When it gutters, the music thins out, the dark closes in, and you hear your heartbeat.

  • The Hush. A tall, pale thing that lives in the background of certain levels. It only moves while you face away from it. Look at it and it stops. You still have to reach the exit.

  • Graves. Every death leaves a candle stub on the world map, forever. World 8's map is nothing but them.

  • The Lamplighter walks the map. If he reaches your square, you run.

  • Gifts, not power-ups. The kingdom is generous. It is a little too generous.

  • Letters from home after every world. Her handwriting changes.

  • 8 worlds, ~70 levels, 8 bosses, 7 suits, 15 map items

  • Authentic 256×240 pixel art in the NES palette; optional CRT filter

  • A live 2A03-style chiptune soundtrack that the horror systems bend in real time

  • Full keyboard and gamepad support with rebinding; Steam Input ready

  • Twelve save files, synced through Steam Cloud so a save follows your account to any machine

  • A "Horror intensity" setting (Full / Reduced) that removes the flashing and the static for photosensitive players

  • Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel)

It plays exactly like the platformers you grew up with. Eight worlds of tight, hand-built levels. A world map with chapels, memory panels and wandering lamplighters. Seven suits: Moth Wings that let you fly when your P-meter fills, a Wax Mask that turns you into a statue, a Newt Suit for the lakes, a Bell Suit that rings enemies off the screen. Fortresses with crushers and ghosts. Barges full of cannons. End-of-level cards that pay out in spares.

And every one of those systems has been turned a few degrees toward dread.

  • Your head is the timer. The level clock is the wax of your own candle. When it gutters, the music thins out, the dark closes in, and you hear your heartbeat.

  • The Hush. A tall, pale thing that lives in the background of certain levels. It only moves while you face away from it. Look at it and it stops. You still have to reach the exit.

  • Graves. Every death leaves a candle stub on the world map, forever. World 8's map is nothing but them.

  • The Lamplighter walks the map. If he reaches your square, you run.

  • Gifts, not power-ups. The kingdom is generous. It is a little too generous.

  • Letters from home after every world. Her handwriting changes.

  • 8 worlds, ~70 levels, 8 bosses, 7 suits, 15 map items

  • Authentic 256×240 pixel art in the NES palette; optional CRT filter

  • A live 2A03-style chiptune soundtrack that the horror systems bend in real time

  • Full keyboard and gamepad support with rebinding; Steam Input ready

  • Twelve save files, synced through Steam Cloud so a save follows your account to any machine

  • A "Horror intensity" setting (Full / Reduced) that removes the flashing and the static for photosensitive players

  • Windows and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel)
store_data.short_description: A cheerful 8-bit kingdom platformer with a candle for a head and something wrong underneath. World maps, power-up suits, fortresses and airships in the spirit of the NES classics. And a stalker that only moves when you look away. Don't let your flame go out.

store_data.about_the_game:
It is 11:48 PM on November 6, 1989.

Seventeen years after a fire sealed the telephone exchange beneath the Municipal Archive, its dead lines begin ringing again.

You are the night archivist assigned to an unfinished intake. Below you: twelve impossible calls, one working service elevator, and an operator-shaped thing that turns every footstep and tuning pulse into a trail.

MORROWTAPE is a no-combat first-person psychological horror game built around a compact, high-tension extraction loop.

Take the field receiver. Follow the carrier. Decide what comes back to the surface.

Tune the line. Take the tape. Reach the lift.

Each of four escalating dives sends you deeper into a fixed, learnable complex whose objective placement, lighting, and dressing shift between runs. Match exact carrier frequencies to reveal sealed routes and recover three red-spooled call records. Find the lift fuse, choose when to sprint, and extract before your noise catches up with you.

Every sound leaves an address

Footsteps, tuning pulses, and dead circuits coming online all give The Listener somewhere to search. You have no weapon. Break its search through route knowledge, timing, and deciding when noise is worth the risk.

Twelve calls. One buried line.

Every recovered reel unlocks a complete on-screen dramatic transcript. Across twelve calls, a child counts telephone poles that appear after dark, a dead subscriber disputes his bill, a patrol officer hears her own voice issue impossible orders, and a vanished operator traces a line the city meant to bury.

Choose the official record

After every extraction, Preserve the Originals or Erase the Carrier. The record you build across four dives leads to one of three endings.

Features

• Four escalating extraction dives, each built around three reels, one lift fuse, and a route back out

• Hands-on exact-frequency tuning that reveals sealed routes and recoverable evidence

• The Listener: a sound-reactive threat that turns movement and activated circuits into risk

• No combat — survive through route knowledge, timing, and nerve

• Twelve complete on-screen call transcripts forming one buried municipal mystery

• Preserve-or-Erase decisions leading to three endings

• Three operator modes — Story, Standard, and Overtime — adjust pursuit pressure

• Keyboard and mouse controls with gamepad support

• Subtitles and descriptive sound captions

• High-contrast presentation, flicker reduction, camera-effects control, and independent volume settings

• Offline single-player play with local saves

Put on headphones if you can. You will not need them to survive.

content_descriptors.notes: MORROWTAPE contains sustained psychological horror, dark and claustrophobic environments, stalking and pursuit by a supernatural entity, threatening dialogue, and intense sound and visual effects. Its story includes grief, missing people, a child in danger, implied off-screen deaths, trapped voices, a fatal historical fire, a municipal cover-up, and the destruction or preservation of evidence. Being caught is implied, but no attack, bodily injury, blood, corpse, dismemberment, or gore is shown. The game contains no sexual content or sexual violence, nudity, self-harm or suicide, drug or alcohol abuse, profanity, or player-performed violence.

store_data.about_the_game:
Emberholme is a singleplayer fantasy RPG with the feel of an old-school MMO. Train 13 skills to level 100, hunt for that elusive equipment upgrade and make a name for yourself in Emberholme. There’s always another goal to work towards, and you decide which one matters next.

You share the realm with 100 living adventurers finding their own way through it. They’re earning better gear, discovering unfamiliar places and chasing drops of their own. You’ll meet them on the roads, trade with them in town and hear about their adventures while making a few stories yourself. Set out for a quiet evening’s fishing and see how far you get before something catches your attention.

Find a weapon you want to wield and work towards it. Train melee, ranged and magic on the same character, with no fixed class locking you into one style. A rare staff might give you a reason to learn magic; a difficult boss might send you looking for a different approach.

There’s always something else to get sidetracked by. Follow a clue trail, take a Huntcraft assignment or help someone whose troubles turn out to be bigger than they first let on. Quests take you from village life into buried halls and across the sea, with decisions that shape how their stories end.

Choose a goal and chase it, or see where the day takes you. When you need a little direction, your journal can point you towards something you’re ready to begin.

The adventurer you pass on the road has somewhere to be. They gather, train, bank their supplies, trade at the Exchange and prepare for fights. Come back later and you might find them in better gear, working towards a different goal.

They learn the realm as they explore it. A place they haven’t discovered or heard about is still unknown to them. Conversations can give them a new lead, and experience teaches them what equipment works against the bosses they encounter. Each adventurer builds their own knowledge of the world, with discoveries still to make and lessons still to learn.

Their money and equipment belong to them. They earn what they use and can lose possessions when a plan goes wrong. Stop for a conversation to ask what they’re doing or hear about an earlier trip. Rare finds appear in the World Drop Journal, including the ones you wish you’d found first.

Start with a fishing spot, a vein of ore or a tree worth cutting. Turn your haul into meals, bars, equipment and runes, or sell it to fund something else. Higher levels open up new resources and recipes, giving you a reason to return to familiar places and push further afield.

Out east, excavate lost artefacts, restore your finds, work glass and escort supply caravans. Install workshops at home when you want your tools close by.

Every item and every coin traded on the Exchange has been earned in the world, by you or one of its 100 living adventurers. Nothing is generated just to stock the market. Those fish were caught, that sword was forged or looted, and someone worked for the gold they’re spending on your supplies. Early on, rare gear is scarce because adventurers are still earning their way towards it. As they train, explore and tackle harder fights, new finds reach the Exchange. The world grows with you, and so does its economy.

Pick your weapon and pack for the fight. Fast attacks suit some encounters; others reward a heavier hit or a spell cast from a safe distance. Watch for an enemy's warning, move out of danger and use the arena's cover when you can.

Hunt rare weapons and armour, learn special attacks from scrolls and choose Mastery perks with benefits and trade-offs. Imbue prized equipment, forge boss materials into stronger gear and fill out a collection log with over 300 items to discover.

There are companions to find and train, bosses to learn, and longer challenges in the Rookery, Skybreak Hunt and Rekindling Trials. Sometimes the next goal is a clear. Sometimes it's one more kill for the drop.

Follow mountain roads across the Crownspine, walk beneath Heartwood's giant redwoods, or pick your way through the western marshes. Travel east to Namar's workshops and desert ruins, then take a ship to Sunwrack's prehistoric coast.

Day turns to night, weather rolls in, and each region has its own creatures, resources and places to investigate. Discover waystones on foot to make the return journey shorter.

Blightmoor is more dangerous. Hostile adventurers can hunt you there, and defeat at their hands costs your tradeable carried gear and coins. Decide what you're willing to risk before crossing the boundary.

Search the live Adventurer's Codex for items, creatures, bosses, quests, places, shops, spells, Vows, Mastery perks and minigames. Spoiler controls keep boss strategies and full quest solutions hidden until you choose to reveal them. You can also discover the Gilded Knuckle, an illegal fight club where adventurers stake their own money foor a chance to make it big..

Earn the right to buy a holding on the Westfen road, choose a Timber Cottage or Country Farmhouse, then make the rooms and garden your own. Decoration Mode lets you arrange furnishings, useful fixtures, displays, garden features and animals, with staged changes that can be applied or cancelled safely.

Plant onions, carrots, pumpkins and corn, then cook them into compact two-portion meals. Chickens, cows, pigs, sheep and llamas produce useful supplies while you are away, storing up to 72 hours of provisions in the household chest. The fireplace works as a cooking surface and a place to reflect on recent quests, levels, bosses and discoveries before choosing a temporary skill or boss-drop focus.

Your Hearthstead, layout and ownership survive death and Rekindling. Friends can visit in co-op, rest by the fire and use ordinary facilities, while building, decorating, crops and provisions remain under the homeowner's control.

When you're ready for a fresh start, Rekindle into the next Ember Cycle. Training becomes slower, enemies get tougher and rare drops become more attainable. Choose the heirlooms you'll carry forward and work towards harder Trials.

Your quests, collections, companions, capes, home and purchased Mastery progress survive the reset. Later Cycles let you bind mastered skills so they return at level 100. Across ten Cycles, each new beginning gives you something different to aim for.

store_data.about_the_game:
Build a garden. Find a balance.

Zenden is a zen garden puzzle and decoration game about the relationships between the things you place. Arrange plants, rocks, water features, and traditional structures across isometric landscapes. Bring neighboring items into harmony, work within each garden’s constraints, and transform an empty patch of ground into somewhere worth meditating.

Every placement contributes to the garden around it. Similar items can create Unity, while contrasting types bring Variety. Spirit and Energy add further considerations, making each zen garden arrangement a balance of practical choices and personal expression.

Each garden presents its own terrain layout, palette, and goals. A limited space might ask you to bring related items together, introduce more variety, or find room for a particular combination of features. Paths, rivers, bridges, and carefully positioned structures offer new ways to think about how the landscape fits together.

Bonus goals invite you to look closer and find more in a garden you’ve already completed.

Shape the landscape

Paint terrain, build shrines, plant trees, and rotate your view to consider an arrangement from another angle. Combine greenery with stone, connect spaces with paths, and build around the features already present in the landscape.

Experiment freely with undo and redo. Move between ideas, revise a corner, or start again when a different arrangement catches your imagination. The garden takes shape one decision at a time.

Make room for the little things

Look beyond the puzzle and watch the garden’s quieter activity. Birds perch among its features, butterflies visit suitable habitats, and fish leap from the water. Plants sway, water ripples, and small animated details give you reasons to pause between placements to find your own moment of zen.

Features

  • Garden-building puzzles with distinct layouts, items, and goals.

  • A relationship-based scoring system built around aesthetic design concepts.

  • Terrain painting and layered placement for arranging plants, rocks, water features, and structures.

  • Paths, rivers, bridges, and spatial challenges that reward thoughtful use of the landscape.

  • Bonus goals that offer further challenges within completed gardens.

  • Animated wildlife and environmental details that bring activity to the spaces you create.

store_data.about_the_game:
Study the room


Something in the room has changed. Maybe a clock shifted, a chair moved, or a familiar object simply vanished. You only get a short look before the room blinks. Then it is up to you.

SightSplice is a focused observation game built around short, replayable runs. Each run visits 10 rooms and asks you to find 30 changes.

Find your pace


- Choose Easy, Medium, Hard, or Hardcore.
- Learn 30 distinct rooms and track them in the room archive.
- Build Memory, Focus, Precision, and Insight with points earned through play.
- Use limited hints when you are stuck, or finish a run without help for an extra challenge.
- Improve room mastery, chase faster times, and complete 24 in-game challenges.

Easy gives you more time and two safety chances. Medium keeps one safety chance. Hard removes the safety net and tightens the clock. Hardcore is the fastest, highest-scoring test, with hints available only to a fully trained Insight skill.

Built for another look


The same room can hide a different change on the next visit. Learn its natural layout, notice the small details, and trust your memory when the screen comes back.

store_data.about_the_game:
PC moments become little creatures

Tab-lings is a desktop companion game where optional, selected parts of your PC activity can create named creatures that live just above the Windows taskbar. Choose sources such as foreground window and browser titles or filenames from folders you select. You can also create every creature manually and play offline.

Care for a growing collection

Feed your Tab-lings, customize them, learn their traits, and help their relationships grow. Complete daily, weekly, monthly, and lifetime goals to earn rewards at your own pace. Draw a custom 16 x 16 creature and give it a full set of animated poses.

Make the habitat yours

Choose how many Tab-lings live above the taskbar, decide how the roster rotates, and arrange habitats across your displays. Empty habitat space stays out of the way while each visible creature remains ready for a visit.

Private and local by default

Every automatic discovery source starts off and has its own visible control. Candidate text passes through a local privacy gate before it can affect gameplay or be saved. Rejected text is not stored. Pause discovery immediately, inspect or clear local history, and remove saved game data whenever you want.

The game does not capture screenshots, pixels, keystrokes, password contents, or accessibility-tree text. Notification-sender discovery is unavailable in the Steam edition. The rest of the local game works offline without an account.

store_data.about_the_game:
Something stripped you down to your frame and left you in a junkyard. Now everything else on the planet hunts you. There's no default body to fall back on — only what you scavenge, what you build, and how far you're willing to go to keep moving.

Rebuild yourself from salvage

  • Assemble your body from dozens of salvaged parts — arms, legs, sensors, and stranger things — pulled from the wreckage of whatever came before you.

  • Every part changes how you move. Trades speed for flight, or height for power.

  • Upgrade at the workshop as you find better parts. There's no "best" build, only the one that gets you where you're going.

A world drawn, not rendered

  • Explore a hand-drawn, charcoal-textured world: a junkyard planet, a buried town, an old-growth forest, and the dark underneath all of it.

  • Reach orbit and beyond, into a canyon world ruled by something enormous, and a drowned, hostile swamp with its own machines and its own reasons to hunt you.

Everything out here hunts

  • The planet's machines don't wait for you to be ready — rooftop stalkers, ambush predators, and things that answer to sound before they ever answer to sight.

  • Something old lives in the dark below the surface. You'll hear it before you understand what it is.

Stakes that mean it

  • Permadeath is real — die, and the save is gone. If that's not the run you want tonight, Mercy mode keeps your last save waiting instead. Your call, every time you start.

You're not doing this alone

A scavenged companion rides with you from the start, and it gets better as you do. What you find out here adds up to something — this is a survival game with a story underneath it, told in fragments, in the dark, one salvage run at a time.

store_data.about_the_game:
A black hole swallowed your ship and spat it into a starless graveyard of the lost. Mine, build, and fight your way through the wreckage in order to follow the needles toward the only rumored way out.

You were an ordinary hauler on a routine run when your engines cut out. Now you're stranded in a pocket of dead space that appears on no chart, sharing the dark with generations of other castaways who fell through the same hole. Salvage what you can. Build something that lasts. Follow the rumors about the Iron Reach, or try to find your own way home.

Carve out a foothold

Mine asteroids, refine raw ore, and vacuum up resources on the fly. Lay down power networks, assemblers, and defenses to turn a patch of empty space into a working base.

Outfit your ship

Swap hulls, engines, and weapons. Craft consumables and modules at your assembler. Learn recipes scavenged from the dark, and tune your loadout for exploration, hauling, or a stand-up fight.

Survive the Wardens

The deeper you push toward the Iron Reach, the more the builders' ancient machines wake to turn you back. Progressive raids escalate as your base grows. Hold the line, or lose what you built.

Follow the needles

Ancient alien Solvanes stand scattered through the graveyard, their needles all fixed on one distant point. Chase them across a procedurally generated expanse, dock at scavenger outposts, take on the survivors' quests, and piece together what the Iron Reach really is.

A world built on rumor

Every scavenger has a theory and none of them match. The story is told through wrecks, contradictory tales, and a universe that never quite explains itself. What you believe is up to you.

store_data.about_the_game:
Take a quiet break with Cozy Jigsaw, a single-player puzzle game inspired by an art gallery. Drag, rotate, and connect pieces to bring each painting back together at your own pace.

A gallery to explore

Choose a painting and one of four difficulty levels. Zoom in to study the details and move around the puzzle table as you work.

Your pictures, your puzzles

Import a PNG or JPG, give it a title, and choose the rows and columns to create a personal puzzle in your collection.

Make yourself comfortable

Save an unfinished puzzle and return to it later. Hide the timer, adjust music and sound effects, and reduce background motion for a calmer session. There is no time limit.

Discover the art behind the pieces

Complete paintings to unlock their notebook pages, with information about the artist, date, style, and background of each work.

Collect achievements and personalize your profile

Complete difficulty challenges for the built-in artworks to unlock Steam achievements and collect letter, number, and other themed icons. Once Steam enables profile features for this game and your account has an Achievement Showcase, choose your unlocked icons to arrange a name, initials, or favorite numbers and give your profile a personal touch.

Prefer to collect at your own pace? After 121 minutes of total playtime, you can also unlock all achievements from the in-game achievement settings. Puzzle completion records are kept separately. Showcase availability depends on Steam enabling the relevant features and your account meeting its requirements.

store_data.about_the_game:
The Assistant is a choice-based adult visual novel that combines adventure, suspense, action, and sex. You play as a young man who gets a new job as the personal assistant to a wealthy family. You will get to know the members of the family and see how this new job changes your entire life.

IMPORTANT: For a better and more complete experience, we recommend playing The Assistant Season 1 and Season 2 first.

However, you can play The Assistant Season 3 without having played the previous seasons.

The Assistant Season 3 is the final season of the story, bringing the adventure to its conclusion.

About Season 3:

The story of The Assistant reaches its conclusion. Face the final twists and turns of the plot as you try to save Sister Clarice's school once and for all and put an end to the threat posed by Igor Spaski. At the same time, your relationships with the girls will reach a decisive point, and the choices you've made will determine how your story ends.

Main Features of Season 3:

  • 24 girls to meet and interact with.

  • 2,937 images.

  • 304 animations.

  • Music and ambient sound effects.

  • A scene gallery where you can replay the adult scenes you've unlocked.

  • An optional interactive guide to help you with important decisions throughout the game.

  • The definitive conclusion to the story of The Assistant, with different endings depending on the choices you make throughout the game.

During the game, you'll find yourself caught up in a web of corruption, drugs, and crime that reaches its climax. New twists, unexpected revelations, and final surprises will challenge everything you thought you knew, as your choices lead you toward the ultimate conclusion of the story.

YOU CONTROL THE STORY

The choices you make will shape the outcome of the game. You decide how to interact with each girl, choosing whether to be a good guy or a bad guy. Each main character has different paths and endings, depending on the choices you've made throughout the story.

store_data.about_the_game:
Stand up gladiator. The crowd wants more!

Rise from the sands, gladiator, and fight for glory, coin, and survival. Face ruthless archers and iron-wielding rivals in the arena. With every victory, claim your coin, sharpen your arms, and prepare for the next bloody contest.

Spend your hard-earned coin wisely. Upgrade your arms and armor, and fight your way through ever more brutal duels. The crowd watches. The Emperor awaits.

KEY FEATURES

  • Real archery. A charge-based bow with arrow physics.

  • Body-part damage. Head, torso, arms, and legs each track their own health.

  • Knockback. Low-HP hits send fighters flying with a finishing blow.

  • Gear up. Four equipment slots with lots of items and upgrades. Helmet, Shield, Chest, and Legs. Each with its own weight, protection, and trade-offs.

  • A permanent upgrade shop. Spend cash earned in the arena on stat upgrades for your bow draw, your stamina, your melee swing, and your body itself.

  • Choose your background. Farmer, Bread Taster, Chicken Wrangler, Grave Robber, and dozens more, each with its own perk.

  • Melee and active blocking. A charge-swing sword system and a stamina-gated block.

  • Two arenas to conquer. Beat both the Colosseum's archery gauntlet and the Duel Arena's melee gauntlet to be set free.

    What Gladiator will you become?

store_data.about_the_game:
Blue has been dog-napped, and summer school is on the line!

Elroy and his friend Syd have just assembled a machine called the Canine Revitalizer for their big school science project. But disaster strikes when they discover both Elroy's dog, Blue, and their precious machine go completely missing! If they don't recover it in time to hand it in, they are getting sent straight to summer school.

Join Elroy and Syd on a relentlessly inventive, fully animated urban rescue mission. This classic Headbone Interactive point-and-click adventure is making its triumphant return, rebuilt for modern desktop platforms.

You have to use your head as you play! To break into the gang's hideout, you'll have to learn about lasers, batteries, secret codes and special fuels. Navigate booby-trapped hideouts, bypass security cameras, and crack complex logic gates. Best of all, you decide where the story goes—you can play again and again to uncover different path choices and unlock multiple endings!

Key Features

  • An Urban Rescue Adventure: Follow Elroy and Syd through a high-stakes, comedic city story to save Blue from a sneaky criminal gang.

  • Real Science Mechanics: Solve interactive puzzles based on real-world concepts, including lasers, battery circuitry, secret codes, and chemical fuel mixtures.

  • Choose Your Own Path: Shape the story with your choices! Replay the game to discover alternate routes, avoid game-over screens, and unlock the best possible ending.

  • Sneak and Brain-Tease: Navigate tricky mazes, outsmart security cameras, and crack locked doors with the help of in-game maps.

  • Fully Restored 90s Animation: Re-experience Headbone Interactive's signature cartoon art style and voice acting.
